use std::fs;
use std::io::{Read, Write};
use std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};
use std::thread;

use vackrooms::adapters::web_renderer::WebRendererAdapter;
use vackrooms::domain::entities::position::Position;
use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::std_telemetry::StdTelemetry;
use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase;

/// Presentation Layer & Driver:
/// A minimalist, zero-dependency HTTP server that connects our
/// Clean Architecture engine to the Browser Voxel Renderer.
fn main() {
    let port = 3000;
    let listener = TcpListener::bind(format!("0.0.0.0:{}", port)).unwrap();
    println!("--- Backrooms Engine Running ---");
    println!("Server listening on http://localhost:{}", port);
    println!("Open the above URL in your browser to view the Voxel Rendering.");

    for stream in listener.incoming() {
        match stream {
            Ok(stream) => {
                thread::spawn(move || {
                    handle_client(stream);
                });
            }
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("Failed to accept connection: {}", e);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn handle_client(mut stream: TcpStream) {
    let mut buffer = [0; 1024];
    if let Ok(bytes_read) = stream.read(&mut buffer) {
        if bytes_read == 0 {
            return;
        }

        let request = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buffer[..bytes_read]);
        let request_line = request.lines().next().unwrap_or("");

        if request_line.starts_with("GET /maze") {
            // Serve the Procedural Voxel Data with support for coordinate query parameters
            let parts: Vec<&str> = request_line.split_whitespace().collect();
            let url = parts.get(1).unwrap_or(&"/maze");

            let mut chunk_x = 0.0;
            let mut chunk_z = 0.0;
            let mut spec = "high";

            if let Some(query_idx) = url.find('?') {
                let query = &url[query_idx + 1..];
                for param in query.split('&') {
                    let key_val: Vec<&str> = param.split('=').collect();
                    if key_val.len() == 2 {
                        match key_val[0] {
                            "x" => chunk_x = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
                            "z" => chunk_z = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
                            "spec" => spec = key_val[1],
                            _ => {}
                        }
                    }
                }
            }

            let config = if spec == "low" {
                vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
            } else {
                vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::high_spec()
            };

            let noise_provider = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
            let telemetry = StdTelemetry;
            let generator =
                GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::with_telemetry(&noise_provider, &telemetry);

            let chunk = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);

            // Adapt to Web Format (greedy meshed faces)
            let json = WebRendererAdapter::to_json(&chunk, config.voxel_scale);

            let response = format!(
                "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n{}",
                json.len(),
                json
            );
            let _ = stream.write_all(response.as_bytes());
        } else if request_line.starts_with("GET /octree") {
            // Serve the SVO Packed Data
            let parts: Vec<&str> = request_line.split_whitespace().collect();
            let url = parts.get(1).unwrap_or(&"/octree");

            let mut chunk_x = 0.0;
            let mut chunk_z = 0.0;
            let mut spec = "high";

            if let Some(query_idx) = url.find('?') {
                let query = &url[query_idx + 1..];
                for param in query.split('&') {
                    let key_val: Vec<&str> = param.split('=').collect();
                    if key_val.len() == 2 {
                        match key_val[0] {
                            "x" => chunk_x = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
                            "z" => chunk_z = key_val[1].parse().unwrap_or(0.0),
                            "spec" => spec = key_val[1],
                            _ => {}
                        }
                    }
                }
            }

            let config = if spec == "low" {
                vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec()
            } else {
                vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::high_spec()
            };

            let noise_provider = SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
            let telemetry = StdTelemetry;
            let generator =
                GenerateChunkArchitectureUseCase::with_telemetry(&noise_provider, &telemetry);

            // Generate chunk at position with GeneratorConfig
            let chunk = generator.execute(Position::new(chunk_x, chunk_z), 42, config);

            // Adapt to Web Format using SVO representation
            let depth = config.svo_depth();
            let world_size = config.svo_world_size();
            let binary = WebRendererAdapter::to_octree_binary(
                &chunk,
                depth,
                world_size,
                config.voxel_scale,
                config.chunk_size,
            );

            let header = format!(
                "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n",
                binary.len()
            );
            let mut response = Vec::with_capacity(header.len() + binary.len());
            response.extend_from_slice(header.as_bytes());
            response.extend_from_slice(&binary);
            let _ = stream.write_all(&response);
        } else if request_line.starts_with("GET ") {
            // Static file service for the WebGPU front end.
            let parts: Vec<&str> = request_line.split_whitespace().collect();
            let url = parts.get(1).unwrap_or(&"/");
            let path = url.split('?').next().unwrap_or("/");
            serve_static(&mut stream, path);
        } else {
            let error = "HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\n\r\n";
            let _ = stream.write_all(error.as_bytes());
        }
    }
}

/// Maps a URL path to a file under `static/` and serves it with the correct
/// MIME type. `application/wasm` matters: browsers refuse to instantiate
/// wasm streams served under the wrong content type.
fn serve_static(stream: &mut TcpStream, url_path: &str) {
    let relative = match url_path {
        "/" | "/index.html" => "index.html",
        other => other.trim_start_matches('/'),
    };

    // Path traversal guard: reject anything trying to escape `static/`.
    if relative.split('/').any(|seg| seg == "..") || relative.contains('\\') {
        let _ = stream.write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\r\n\r\n");
        return;
    }

    let file_path = format!("static/{}", relative);
    match fs::read(&file_path) {
        Ok(body) => {
            let mime = match file_path.rsplit('.').next() {
                Some("html") => "text/html; charset=utf-8",
                Some("js") | Some("mjs") => "text/javascript",
                Some("wasm") => "application/wasm",
                Some("css") => "text/css",
                Some("json") => "application/json",
                Some("png") => "image/png",
                _ => "application/octet-stream",
            };
            let header = format!(
                "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: {}\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\n\r\n",
                mime,
                body.len()
            );
            let mut response = Vec::with_capacity(header.len() + body.len());
            response.extend_from_slice(header.as_bytes());
            response.extend_from_slice(&body);
            let _ = stream.write_all(&response);
        }
        Err(_) => {
            let _ = stream.write_all(b"HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found\r\n\r\nFile not found.");
        }
    }
}

77:             && let Some(payload) = decode_chunk_payload(&bytes)
78:         {
79:             return payload;
80:         }
81:         // Absent, corrupt, or archived for a different renderer — the
82:         // artifact bits are part of the key, so a record built for the splat
83:         // renderer is simply not found by a mesh renderer rather than being
84:         // handed over with the wrong products.

90:         let encoded = encode_chunk_payload(&payload);
91:         let mut storage = self.storage.borrow_mut();
92:         let mut archive = self.archive.borrow_mut();
93:         // Bound the log before growing it. An append-only file cannot free
94:         // one record, so staying inside a budget means emptying it — see
95:         // `ChunkArchive::clear` for why that trade is the right one here.
96:         if archive.bytes() + encoded.len() as u64 > self.max_bytes {
97:             archive.clear(storage.as_mut());

101:         drop(archive);
102:         payload
103:     }

11901 Now worker_source.rs — the JS bridge.
11902 //! Web Worker chunk source — the multithreaded [`ChunkSourcePort`].
11903 //!
11904 //! Each worker (`static/worker.js`) is a second instance of this same wasm
11905 //! module running on its own OS thread. The main thread posts small
11906 //! `{gen, requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality}` messages
11907 //! round-robin. Workers always generate, bake, build the collision SVO, and
11908 //! extract collision; the artifact bitfield requests only the active
11909 //! renderer's mesh, face, or serialized-node products. One encoded byte
11910 //! buffer returns through `adapters::chunk_codec`; GPU resources remain owned
11911 //! by the main-thread render driver. Healthy pools keep generation off the
11912 //! frame loop. If every worker fatally fails, the driver uses its same-thread
11913 //! source as a correctness fallback instead of leaving the world pending.
11914 //!
11915 //! Stale-result rejection lives in the engine (`install_completed`), keyed
11916 //! by the echoed request. This driver owns transport failure detection and
11917 //! reports exact failed requests through the same application port.
11918

12248 
12249 1. **The worker ledger (`GenerationWorkerRequests`) is shared between the message handler closures (JS event callbacks) and `request()` (called from the engine tick).** On the wasm main thread, this is all single-threaded (JS event loop), so `RefCell` borrows are safe. But there IS a re-entrancy haz

12251 2. **`finish_exact` on `Completed`** — a stale `done` reply (not matching any in-flight) is dropped, BUT the payload is dropped too. Good.

12253 3. **Backpressure**: `request()` is called only when `pending.len() < max_pending` (engine-side cap = max_concurrent_requests = pool_size). So at most pool_size in-flight globally. Per worker, in-flight is a VecDeque — bounded by pool size. Fine — no unbounded queue.
12254 
12255 4. **Race between async worker replies and synchronous frame updates**: `poll_completed` drains `completed` (RefCell on main thread). Worker replies arrive as JS events between ticks — since engine tick and message handlers both run on the main JS thread, there's no race; ordering is deterministic b
12256

12285 // Generation worker: a second instance of the same wasm module, producing
12286 // renderer-selected chunk artifacts off the main thread. The handler is
12287 // registered synchronously at module scope so no message can be lost while
12288 // the wasm module is still instantiating; work is serialized through a
12289 // promise chain.
12290 //
12291 // Protocol (main -> worker):
12292 //   { type: "init", query, seed }        one-time generator setup
12293 //   { type: "gen", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality }
12294 //                   one chunk order; artifacts is a u8 bitfield and reality
12295 //                   is Uint32Array
12296 // (worker -> main):
12297 //   { type: "done", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality, ms, buf }
12298 //                                   buf transferred, encoded by chunk_codec
12299 //   { type: "failed", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality, message }
12300 //                                   one request failed and may be retried
12301 //   { type: "fatal", message }      worker initialization failed
12302 import init, { worker_init, worker_generate } from "./pkg/wasm_frontend.js";

12307   return wasmReady;
12308 }

12317 function reportFailure(message, error) {
12318   const description = errorMessage(error);
12319   console.error("[WORKER] generation failure:", description);
12320   try {
12321     if (message?.type === "gen") {
12322       postMessage({
12323         type: "failed",
12324         requestId: message.requestId,
12325         ox: message.ox,
12326         oz: message.oz,
12327         level: message.level,
12328         lod: message.lod,
12329         artifacts: message.artifacts,
12330         reality: new Uint32Array(message.reality),
12331         message: description,
12332       });
12333     } else {
12334       postMessage({ type: "fatal", message: description });
12335     }
12336   } catch (reportError) {
12337     // The browser's Worker error event is the final recovery path when even
12338     // the structured failure message cannot be cloned or delivered.
12339     console.error("[WORKER] could not report generation failure:", reportError);
12340   }
12341 }

12343 async function processMessage(message) {
12344   await ensureWasm();
12345   if (message.type === "init") {
12346     worker_init(message.query, message.seed >>> 0);
12347     return;
12348   }
12349   if (message.type !== "gen") return;
12350 
12351   const t0 = performance.now();
12352   const reality = new Uint32Array(message.reality);
12353   const bytes = worker_generate(
12354     message.requestId >>> 0,
12355     message.ox,
12356     message.oz,
12357     message.level,
12358     message.lod,
12359     message.artifacts >>> 0,
12360     reality
12361   );
12362   const ms = performance.now() - t0;
12363   console.debug(
12364     `[WORKER] chunk (${message.ox}, ${message.oz}) lod ${message.lod} generated in ${ms.toFixed(1)} ms`
12365   );
12366   postMessage(
12367     {
12368       type: "done",
12369       requestId: message.requestId,
12370       ox: message.ox,
12371       oz: message.oz,
12372       level: message.level,
12373       lod: message.lod,
12374       artifacts: message.artifacts,
12375       reality,
12376       ms,
12377       buf: bytes.buffer,
12378     },
12379     [bytes.buffer]
12380   );
12381 }

  49 /// Detail as a function of distance, so the resident world can reach past
  50 /// the fog without paying full resolution for all of it.
  51 ///
  52 /// The engine used to have exactly two detail levels: full, within
  53 /// `fine_distance`, and one coarse level everywhere else. That put a hard
  54 /// ceiling on how far the world could reach, because the outer ring — which
  55 /// is almost all of it, growing as the square of the radius — cost a
  56 /// quarter of full resolution no matter how far away it was.
  57 ///
  58 /// Measured cost of one 10 u chunk's surface mesh, which is what the ladder
  59 /// is trading against:
  60 ///
  61 /// ```text
  62 /// lod 0   252 KB   33.3 ms
  63 /// lod 1    94 KB    8.4 ms
  64 /// lod 2    21 KB    4.7 ms
  65 /// lod 3     2 KB    4.8 ms
  66 /// ```
  67 ///
  68 /// A chunk twelve times cheaper is a ring that can be twelve times larger,
  69 /// and the far ring is exactly where detail is least visible — Level 0's fog
  70 /// (`exp(-0.018 * (d - 12))`) has already removed 92% of a surface by 155 u.
  71 ///
  72 /// Distances are world units, not chunks, so one ladder describes both the
  73 /// 10 u and 20 u chunk profiles.
  74 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
  75 pub struct LodLadder {
  76     /// Full resolution within this distance.
  77     pub fine_distance: f32,
  78     /// Half resolution within this distance.
  79     pub mid_distance: f32,
  80     /// Quarter resolution within this distance; eighth beyond it.
  81     pub far_distance: f32,
  82 }
  83 
  84 impl LodLadder {
  85     /// The detail a chunk at this distance should be held at.
  86     pub fn lod_at(&self, distance: f32) -> u8 {
  87         // A NaN distance must not silently become the most expensive level:
  88         // every comparison below is false for NaN, so it falls through to
  89         // the cheapest, which is the safe direction to fail.
  90         if distance <= self.fine_distance {
  91             0
  92         } else if distance <= self.mid_distance {
  93             1
  94         } else if distance <= self.far_distance {
  95             2
  96         } else {
  97             3
  98         }
  99     }
 100 
 101     /// Chunks of `chunk_size` needed to reach the end of the ladder.
 102     ///
 103     /// This is what the visual streaming radius should be: holding chunks
 104     /// beyond it would spend memory on geometry the ladder has already
 105     /// decided is barely worth resolving.
 106     pub fn radius_in_chunks(&self, chunk_size: f32) -> i32 {
 107         if !(chunk_size > 0.0) || !self.far_distance.is_finite() {
 108             return 1;
 109         }
 110         (self.far_distance / chunk_size).ceil().max(1.0) as i32
 111     }
 112 }
 113 
 114 impl Default for LodLadder {
 115     /// Sized against Level 0's fog rather than against a memory budget.
 116     ///
 117     /// At 155 u a surface is down to 7.6% transmittance, so a chunk arriving
 118     /// at the far edge is a change to something already almost invisible —
 119     /// which is the whole point: the player must never watch geometry appear.
 120     /// For 10 u chunks this is a 31x31 footprint costing roughly 43 MB of
 121     /// mesh, against the 9x9 (~8 MB) it replaces.
 122     fn default() -> Self {
 123         Self {
 124             fine_distance: 30.0,
 125             mid_distance: 75.0,
 126             far_distance: 155.0,
 127         }
 128     }
 129 }
 130 
 131 /// Decides which chunks should be resident for a given player position.
 132 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
 133 pub struct StreamingPolicy {
 134     /// World-space side length of a chunk.
 135     pub chunk_size: f32,
 136     /// Chebyshev radius in chunks: 1 -> 3x3 resident set, 2 -> 5x5.
 137     pub radius: i32,
 138     /// Chunks within this Chebyshev radius stay resident no matter where
 139     /// the player looks, so turning can never expose an unloaded chunk.
 140     /// Only chunks *beyond* it are subject to view culling.
 141     pub core_radius: i32,
 142 }
 143 
 144 impl StreamingPolicy {
 145     /// Omnidirectional policy: every chunk in the square is desired.
 146     ///
 147     /// This is what collision and simulation must use. Physics residency
 148     /// may never depend on view direction, or walking backwards into an
 149     /// unloaded chunk would drop the player through the floor.
 150     pub fn omnidirectional(chunk_size: f32, radius: i32) -> Self {
 151         Self {
 152             chunk_size,
 153             radius,
 154             core_radius: radius,
 155         }
 156     }
 157 
 158     /// Returns the desired chunk origins, sorted nearest-first so the load
 159     /// budget is always spent on the most urgent chunk.
 160     pub fn desired_origins(&self, player_x: f32, player_z: f32) -> Vec<(f32, f32)> {
 161         self.desired_origins_in_view(player_x, player_z, None)
 162     }
 163 
 164     /// Returns the desired chunk origins, optionally culled to a view cone
 165     /// beyond `core_radius`.
 166     ///
 167     /// The test is conservative: a chunk counts as visible when its
 168     /// bounding circle touches the cone, not merely when its centre is
 169     /// inside. A chunk straddling the frustum edge still streams.
 170     pub fn desired_origins_in_view(
 171         &self,
 172         player_x: f32,
 173         player_z: f32,
 174         view: Option<ViewCone>,
 175     ) -> Vec<(f32, f32)> {
 176         let px = if player_x.is_finite() { player_x } else { 0.0 };
 177         let pz = if player_z.is_finite() { player_z } else { 0.0 };
 178         let base_x = (px / self.chunk_size).floor() * self.chunk_size;
 179         let base_z = (pz / self.chunk_size).floor() * self.chunk_size;
 180         // Half-diagonal of a chunk footprint: the bounding circle radius.
 181         let bound = self.chunk_size * std::f32::consts::SQRT_2 * 0.5;
 182 
 183         let mut origins = Vec::with_capacity(((2 * self.radius + 1).pow(2)) as usize);
 184         for dz in -self.radius..=self.radius {
 185             for dx in -self.radius..=self.radius {
 186                 let origin_x = base_x + dx as f32 * self.chunk_size;
 187                 let origin_z = base_z + dz as f32 * self.chunk_size;
 188                 let core = dx.abs() <= self.core_radius && dz.abs() <= self.core_radius;
 189                 if !core && !self.touches_cone(px, pz, origin_x, origin_z, bound, view) {
 190                     continue;
 191                 }
 192                 origins.push((origin_x, origin_z));
 193             }
 194         }
 195         origins.sort_by(|a, b| {
 196             let da = (a.0 + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - px).powi(2)
 197                 + (a.1 + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - pz).powi(2);
 198             let db = (b.0 + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - px).powi(2)
 199                 + (b.1 + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - pz).powi(2);
 200             da.total_cmp(&db)
 201         });
 202         origins
 203     }
 204 
 205     fn touches_cone(
 206         &self,
 207         px: f32,
 208         pz: f32,
 209         origin_x: f32,
 210         origin_z: f32,
 211         bound: f32,
 212         view: Option<ViewCone>,
 213     ) -> bool {
 214         let Some(view) = view else {
 215             return true;
 216         };
 217         let to_x = origin_x + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - px;
 218         let to_z = origin_z + self.chunk_size * 0.5 - pz;
 219         let distance = (to_x * to_x + to_z * to_z).sqrt();
 220         // Inside its own bounding circle the angle is meaningless.
 221         if distance <= bound || !distance.is_finite() {
 222             return true;
 223         }
 224         let cos = (to_x * view.forward.0 + to_z * view.forward.1) / distance;
 225         let angle = cos.clamp(-1.0, 1.0).acos();
 226         // Widen the cone by the chunk's angular radius so a partially
 227         // visible chunk is never dropped.
 228         angle <= view.half_angle + (bound / distance).clamp(-1.0, 1.0).asin()
 229     }
 230 }
 231 
 232 /// A resident chunk: payload plus its world origin and current level of
 233 /// detail (0 = full resolution; higher = coarser, see `ChunkSourcePort`).
 234 #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
 235 pub struct LoadedChunk {
 236     pub origin: (f32, f32),
 237     pub lod: u8,
 238     /// Exact immutable encounter state from which every payload view
 239     /// (collision, SVO, mesh and lighting) was derived.
 240     pub reality: RealitySnapshot,
 241     /// Cached identity for diagnostics and fast rejection paths. Exact
 242     /// equality still uses `reality`, so a hash collision cannot mix worlds.
 243     pub reality_fingerprint: u64,
 244     pub payload: ChunkPayload,
 245 }
 246 
 247 impl LoadedChunk {
 248     pub fn new(
 249         origin: (f32, f32),
 250         lod: u8,
 251         reality: RealitySnapshot,
 252         payload: ChunkPayload,
 253     ) -> Self {
 254         let reality_fingerprint = reality.fingerprint();
 255         Self {
 256             origin,
 257             lod,
 258             reality,
 259             reality_fingerprint,
 260             payload,
 261         }
 262     }
 263 
 264     pub fn is_in_reality(&self, reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> bool {
 265         self.reality_fingerprint == reality.fingerprint() && &self.reality == reality
 266     }
 267 }
 268 
 269 /// Keyed store of resident chunks. Iteration order is the insertion order of
 270 /// keys (tracked separately) so atlas offsets stay deterministic.
 271 #[derive(Debug, Default)]
 272 pub struct ChunkStore {
 273     chunks: HashMap<ChunkKey, LoadedChunk>,
 274     order: Vec<ChunkKey>,
 275 }
 276 
 277 impl ChunkStore {
 278     pub fn new() -> Self {
 279         Self {
 280             chunks: HashMap::new(),
 281             order: Vec::new(),
 282         }
 283     }
 284 
 285     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
 286         self.order.len()
 287     }
 288 
 289     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 290         self.order.is_empty()
 291     }
 292 
 293     pub fn contains(&self, key: ChunkKey) -> bool {
 294         self.chunks.contains_key(&key)
 295     }
 296 
 297     pub fn get(&self, key: ChunkKey) -> Option<&LoadedChunk> {
 298         self.chunks.get(&key)
 299     }
 300 
 301     pub fn insert(&mut self, key: ChunkKey, chunk: LoadedChunk) {
 302         if self.chunks.insert(key, chunk).is_none() {
 303             self.order.push(key);
 304         }
 305     }
 306 
 307     /// Removes every chunk whose key is not in `keep`, returning whether
 308     /// anything changed.
 309     pub fn retain_keys(&mut self, keep: &[ChunkKey]) -> bool {
 310         let before = self.order.len();
 311         self.order.retain(|k| keep.contains(k));
 312         self.chunks.retain(|k, _| keep.contains(k));
 313         before != self.order.len()
 314     }
 315 
 316     /// Chunks in deterministic (insertion) order.
 317     pub fn iter_ordered(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &LoadedChunk> {
 318         self.order.iter().filter_map(|k| self.chunks.get(k))
 319     }
 320 
 321     /// All collision boxes of all resident chunks.
 322     pub fn all_collision_boxes(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &Aabb> {
 323         self.iter_ordered().flat_map(|c| c.payload.collision.iter())
 324     }
 325 
 326     pub fn all_traversal_gates(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &TraversalGate> {
 327         self.iter_ordered()
 328             .flat_map(|c| c.payload.traversal_gates.iter())
 329     }
 330 
 331     pub fn all_supply_items(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &SupplyItem> {
 332         self.iter_ordered()
 333             .flat_map(|c| c.payload.supply_items.iter())
 334     }
 335 
 336     pub fn all_level_exits(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &LevelExit> {
 337         self.iter_ordered()
 338             .flat_map(|c| c.payload.level_exits.iter())
 339     }
 340 
 341     pub fn all_pit_hazards(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &PitHazard> {
 342         self.iter_ordered()
 343             .flat_map(|c| c.payload.pit_hazards.iter())
 344     }
 345 }

 351     #[test]
 352     fn the_ladder_coarsens_monotonically_with_distance() {
 353         let ladder = LodLadder::default();
 354         let mut previous = 0u8;
 355         let mut d = 0.0f32;
 356         while d < ladder.far_distance * 2.0 {
 357             let lod = ladder.lod_at(d);
 358             assert!(
 359                 lod >= previous,
 360                 "detail increased with distance at {d} u: {previous} -> {lod}"
 361             );
 362             previous = lod;
 363             d += 1.0;
 364         }
 365         assert_eq!(previous, 3, "the ladder never reached its cheapest rung");
 366     }
 367 
 368     #[test]
 369     fn each_band_holds_its_own_edge() {
 370         let ladder = LodLadder {
 371             fine_distance: 10.0,
 372             mid_distance: 20.0,
 373             far_distance: 30.0,
 374         };
 375         // Boundaries belong to the finer band: a chunk exactly at the edge
 376         // renders at the better level, never the worse one.
 377         assert_eq!(ladder.lod_at(0.0), 0);
 378         assert_eq!(ladder.lod_at(10.0), 0);
 379         assert_eq!(ladder.lod_at(10.01), 1);
 380         assert_eq!(ladder.lod_at(20.0), 1);
 381         assert_eq!(ladder.lod_at(20.01), 2);
 382         assert_eq!(ladder.lod_at(30.0), 2);
 383         assert_eq!(ladder.lod_at(30.01), 3);
 384     }
 385 
 386     #[test]
 387     fn a_nonsense_distance_falls_to_the_cheapest_rung() {
 388         // Failing toward cheap is the safe direction: a NaN distance that
 389         // resolved to lod 0 would generate the most expensive chunk in the
 390         // engine for a position that does not exist.
 391         let ladder = LodLadder::default();
 392         assert_eq!(ladder.lod_at(f32::NAN), 3);
 393         assert_eq!(ladder.lod_at(f32::INFINITY), 3);
 394     }
 395 
 396     #[test]
 397     fn the_radius_reaches_the_end_of_the_ladder() {
 398         let ladder = LodLadder::default();
 399         // Both chunk profiles must cover the same world distance.
 400         for chunk_size in [10.0f32, 20.0] {
 401             let radius = ladder.radius_in_chunks(chunk_size);
 402             assert!(
 403                 radius as f32 * chunk_size >= ladder.far_distance,
 404                 "radius {radius} of {chunk_size} u chunks falls short of {} u",
 405                 ladder.far_distance
 406             );
 407         }
 408         assert_eq!(ladder.radius_in_chunks(0.0), 1, "a degenerate chunk size");
 409     }

 411     #[test]
 412     fn the_footprint_reaches_past_where_level_zero_can_be_seen() {
 413         // The property the whole ladder exists for. Level 0's fog is
 414         // `exp(-density * (d - start))`; a chunk arriving where less than 8%
 415         // of it survives is not something a player can watch appear.
 416         let ladder = LodLadder::default();
 417         let (fog_start, fog_density) = (12.0f32, 0.018f32);
 418         let transmittance = (-fog_density * (ladder.far_distance - fog_start)).exp();
 419         assert!(
 420             transmittance < 0.08,
 421             "the streaming frontier sits at {:.0}% visibility",
 422             transmittance * 100.0
 423         );
 424     }

 505         let ahead = policy.desired_origins_in_view(0.0, 0.0, Some(ViewCone::from_yaw(0.0, 0.8)));
 506         assert!(

 557     #[test]
 558     fn partially_visible_chunks_are_kept() {
 559         // The point of the bounding-circle test: a chunk whose *centre*
 560         // lies outside the cone is still streamed when part of its
 561         // footprint is inside. Without this, geometry pops in at the
 562         // screen border as the player turns.
 563         let policy = visual_policy(4, 0);
 564         let half_angle = 0.30;
 565         let (px, pz) = (5.0, 5.0);
 566         let view = ViewCone::from_yaw(0.0, half_angle);
 567         let kept = policy.desired_origins_in_view(px, pz, Some(view));
 568 
 569         let centre_outside_cone = kept.iter().any(|&(x, z)| {
 570             let (to_x, to_z) = (x + CHUNK * 0.5 - px, z + CHUNK * 0.5 - pz);
 571             let distance = (to_x * to_x + to_z * to_z).sqrt();
 572             if distance <= f32::EPSILON {
 573                 return false;
 574             }
 575             let cos = (to_x * view.forward.0 + to_z * view.forward.1) / distance;
 576             cos.clamp(-1.0, 1.0).acos() > half_angle
 577         });
 578         assert!(
 579             centre_outside_cone,
 580             "a strict centre-in-cone test would have dropped chunks this kept"
 581         );
 582     }

   1 //! The frame-loop orchestrator: the application's central use case.
   2 //!
   3 //! `Engine::tick` is called once per animation frame by the browser driver
   4 //! with plain data in (`InputFrame`, dt) and drives everything else through
   5 //! ports: chunk loading via [`ChunkSourcePort`], drawing via [`RendererPort`].
   6 //! No browser types appear anywhere in this file, so the whole game loop is
   7 //! natively unit-testable.

  40 /// Static configuration chosen by the composition root.
  41 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
  42 pub struct EngineConfig {
  43     pub seed: u32,
  44     /// World-space chunk side length (must match the generator config).
  45     pub chunk_size: f32,
  46     /// Streaming radius in chunks (1 = 3x3, 2 = 5x5).
  47     pub chunk_radius: i32,
  48     /// Player spawn (eye position).
  49     pub spawn: [f32; 3],
  50     /// Initial yaw, radians. Set by the composition root so the player wakes
  51     /// up looking *down* the main corridor, not at a wall.
  52     pub spawn_yaw: f32,
  53     /// Full-resolution chunk loads per tick. 2 balances streaming latency
  54     /// against frame hitches: one fine chunk costs ~15 ms native (more in
  55     /// wasm), so higher budgets stall the frame visibly. Coarse loads cost
  56     /// a fraction of this budget (see `FINE_LOAD_COST`).
  57     pub max_loads_per_tick: usize,
  58     /// Detail as a function of distance. Its `fine_distance` is the old
  59     /// screen-space-error proxy — a coarse voxel at that range projects to
  60     /// roughly the same pixels as a fine voxel at half of it — and its outer
  61     /// rungs are what let the resident world reach past the fog.
  62     pub lod: LodLadder,
  63     /// Level to boot into (0 = Backrooms, 34 = grassland). Exposed as the
  64     /// `?level=` debug query so any level is reachable in any renderer
  65     /// without waiting on a noclip roll.
  66     pub initial_level: u32,
  67 }

  69 impl Default for EngineConfig {
  70     fn default() -> Self {
  71         Self {
  72             seed: 42,
  73             chunk_size: 10.0,
  74             chunk_radius: 1,
  75             spawn: [5.0, 1.7, 5.0],
  76             spawn_yaw: 0.0,
  77             max_loads_per_tick: 2,
  78             lod: LodLadder::default(),
  79             initial_level: LEVEL_BACKROOMS,
  80         }
  81     }
  82 }

  84 /// One frame's worth of user input, already translated to domain terms by
  85 /// the input adapter.
  86 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
  87 pub struct InputFrame {
  88     pub intent: MoveIntent,
  89     pub look_dx: f32,
  90     pub look_dy: f32,
  91     /// Whether pointer lock is engaged; movement is frozen otherwise.
  92     pub locked: bool,
  93     pub flashlight: bool,
  94     /// Edge-triggered flare drop for this frame (G key / touch button).
  95     pub drop_flare: bool,
  96     /// Edge-triggered deliberate drink of one carried almond water (R key /
  97     /// touch button).
  98     pub drink: bool,
  99     /// Edge-triggered deliberate ration meal (T key / touch button).
 100     pub eat: bool,
 101 }

 103 /// A resolved navigation objective for the route anchor: a real, resident
 104 /// level door. Range is straight-line on the walking plane (there is no
 105 /// route graph, so the presenter labels it RANGE, never PATH).
 106 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 107 pub struct RouteAnchor {
 108     /// Level id on the far side of the door.
 109     pub target_level: u32,
 110     /// Bearing relative to the player's facing, whole degrees 0..=359.
 111     pub bearing_deg: u16,
 112     /// Straight-line range, meters.
 113     pub range_m: f32,
 114 }
