 116 /// Snapshot for the HUD presenter.
 117 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
 118 pub struct HudStats {
 119     pub resident_chunks: usize,
 120     /// Chunks resident at full resolution; the rest are coarse LOD.
 121     pub fine_chunks: usize,
 122     pub atlas_nodes: usize,
 123     pub collision_boxes: usize,
 124     pub resolution_scale: f32,
 125     /// True once the spawn chunk is resident (drives the loading overlay).
 126     pub ready: bool,
 127     /// Session pedometer: resolved horizontal movement in world units
 128     /// (= meters), collision already applied, relocations excluded.
 129     pub distance_m: f32,
 130     /// Survival vitals, normalized 0..=1 for the HUD bars.
 131     pub hydration: f32,
 132     pub satiety: f32,
 133     pub condition: f32,
 134     /// Carried supplies (auto-consumed when the matching vital runs low).
 135     pub almond_bottles: u32,
 136     pub rations: u32,
 137     /// Smoothed ambient temperature at the player, °C.
 138     pub ambient_c: f32,
 139     /// Times the wanderer has succumbed this session.
 140     pub deaths: u32,
 141     /// The active Backrooms level id.
 142     pub level: u32,
 143     /// The embodied telemetry the body trace presents: steps, pulse,
 144     /// signal state, beat prominence. Raw vitals above stay for diagnostics
 145     /// only — the normal HUD never renders them as meters.
 146     pub body: BodyReadout,
 147     /// Present only when a real resident level door is known. `None` is the
 148     /// truthful "route unresolved / beyond field" state.
 149     pub route: Option<RouteAnchor>,
 150 }
 151 
 152 /// The LOD every missing chunk is *first* loaded at, whatever the ladder
 153 /// will eventually want for it.
 154 ///
 155 /// Availability before fidelity: one cheap load makes a chunk visible, and
 156 /// the refinement pass then walks it down the ladder nearest-first. Loading
 157 /// straight to the ladder's answer would spend the whole per-tick budget on
 158 /// the near ring while the far ring stayed a hole in the world.
 159 const INITIAL_LOD: u8 = 1;
 160 /// Chunks this close stay resident whatever the player looks at, so a
 161 /// fast turn never reveals an unloaded chunk.
 162 const VISUAL_CORE_RADIUS: i32 = 2;
 163 /// Half-angle of the streaming view cone. A 90 degree horizontal field of
 164 /// view is 45 degrees each side; the extra margin covers turning between
 165 /// the moment a chunk is requested and the moment it arrives.
 166 const VISUAL_CONE_HALF_ANGLE: f32 = 1.13;
 167 /// Budget units one fine load costs; a coarse load costs 1. Coarse generation
 168 /// touches ~1/8 the voxels but has fixed per-chunk overhead, so 4 (not 8)
 169 /// keeps the worst-case tick cost at the old two-fine-loads level.
 170 const FINE_LOAD_COST: u32 = 4;
 171 
 172 /// Backrooms level ids the engine can noclip between.
 173 const LEVEL_BACKROOMS: u32 = 0;
 174 /// Level 1, the Habitable Zone (physical doors lead here from Level 0).
 175 const LEVEL_HABITABLE: u32 = 1;
 176 const LEVEL_GRASSLAND: u32 = 34;
 177 /// Horizontal reach within which a supply pickup fires.
 178 const PICKUP_REACH: f32 = 0.8;
 179 /// Seconds between level-door transits (re-arming, not gameplay pacing).
 180 const DOOR_COOLDOWN_S: f32 = 2.0;
 181 /// Route-objective reselection cadence. Selection walks the resident exits
 182 /// (a handful at most), so this is bookkeeping hygiene, not a hot path.
 183 const ROUTE_RECOMPUTE_PERIOD_S: f32 = 0.5;
 184 /// Debug-only anomaly awareness radius for the diagnostic aperture, meters.
 185 const AWARENESS_RANGE_M: f32 = 60.0;
 186 /// Where death and Level-1 arrival place the eye, per level.
 187 fn level_spawn(level: u32, config_spawn: [f32; 3]) -> [f32; 3] {
 188     if level == LEVEL_HABITABLE {
 189         [3.0, 1.7, 3.0]
 190     } else {
 191         config_spawn
 192     }
 193 }
 194 /// Keep pushing into a wall this long before a noclip roll happens...
 195 const NOCLIP_PUSH_SECONDS: f32 = 1.2;
 196 /// ...then one roll per second of continued pushing, at this probability.
 197 const NOCLIP_CHANCE: f32 = 0.2;
 198 /// Per-frame intensity gain of one fixture's authored flicker mode.
 199 /// Deterministic in (id, time): every machine shows the same buzz.
 200 /// Mode 1 is a tired ballast — a fast shallow shimmer with slow beats.
 201 /// Mode 2 is a dying tube — mostly lit, with hard sputtering dropouts.
 202 fn fixture_flicker_gain(id: u64, mode: u8, time: f32) -> f32 {
 203     let phase = (id % 977) as f32 * 0.61;
 204     match mode {
 205         1 => {
 206             let t = time * 47.0 + phase;
 207             (0.86 + 0.10 * t.sin() * (t * 0.093).cos() + 0.04 * (time * 3.1 + phase).sin())
 208                 .clamp(0.7, 1.0)
 209         }
 210         2 => {
 211             // Coarse deterministic gate: ~9 decisions per second per tube.
 212             let step = (time * 9.0 + phase) as u64;
 213             let mut h = id ^ step.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
 214             h ^= h >> 31;
 215             h = h.wrapping_mul(0xBF58_476D_1CE4_E5B9);
 216             if (h >> 40) % 100 < 24 { 0.06 } else { 0.92 }
 217         }
 218         _ => 1.0,
 219     }
 220 }
 221 
 222 /// Inside a blackout, drift cells closer than this may still be revealed by
 223 /// a flare or the flashlight cone, so the rear shift never touches them.
 224 /// Blackout ambient is near-black past a few units; 5 u is already beyond
 225 /// anything the player can resolve behind their own shoulder, and the
 226 /// tighter radius lets the dark rearrange almost at the player's heels.
 227 const BLACKOUT_HIDE_DISTANCE: f32 = 5.0;
 228 /// Cadence of the in-blackout rear shift. Aggressive on purpose: the way
 229 /// in is gone the moment it leaves the corner of the eye, so a blackout is
 230 /// almost impossible to back out of. Each firing's rebuild work is still
 231 /// metered by the ordinary install budget.
 232 const BLACKOUT_SHIFT_PERIOD_S: f32 = 0.75;
 233 pub struct Engine {
 234     config: EngineConfig,
 235     player: Player,
 236     policy: StreamingPolicy,
 237     visual_policy: StreamingPolicy,
 238     store: ChunkStore,
 239     pool: AtlasPool,
 240     world: CollisionWorld,
 241     draws: Vec<ChunkDraw>,
 242     atlas_nodes: usize,
 243     governor: PerfGovernor,
 244     artifact_needs: RenderArtifactNeeds,
 245     renderer: Box<dyn RendererPort>,
 246     source: Box<dyn ChunkSourcePort>,
 247     /// Outstanding background loads (async sources only). The complete
 248     /// request is retained so a late completion can neither clear nor replace
 249     /// a newer request for the same spatial chunk.
 250     pending: HashMap<ChunkKey, ChunkRequest>,
 251     /// Finished background loads waiting for install budget. Workers can
 252     /// return several chunks in one tick; installing them all at once (mesh
 253     /// upload + collision rebuild per chunk) is exactly the frame hitch the
 254     /// worker pool exists to avoid, so installs are metered per tick and the
 255     /// overflow waits here. Every entry is re-validated at install time.
 256     completed_backlog: Vec<CompletedChunk>,
 257     /// Monotonic worker-order identity. Kept independent from chunk/LOD so a
 258     /// re-request after eviction is distinguishable from its predecessor.
 259     next_request_id: u32,
 260     /// Immutable encounter state used by every request in the active reality.

 261     /// Traversal/event handling will replace this in a later slice; epoch zero
 262     /// is sufficient to establish the transport and validation contract now.
 263     reality: RealitySnapshot,
 264     /// Resident red-room chunks that may safely rebuild after the player has
 265     /// crossed the occluded inner threshold. Other remaps stay lazy until
 266     /// ordinary eviction, so directly visible pillar/blackout geometry never
 267     /// pops.
 268     forced_reloads: HashSet<ChunkKey>,
 269     /// Peripheral Shift bookkeeping: fabric drift cells the player is (or
 270     /// recently was) near. A cell that leaves the far radius has become
 271     /// genuinely unobserved and its drift epoch advances, so the fabric the
 272     /// player walks back into has lawfully rearranged.
 273     drift_near: HashSet<(i64, i64)>,
 274     /// Seconds until the next in-blackout rear shift may fire.
 275     blackout_shift_cooldown: f32,
 276     /// Debug telemetry for the rear shift: (player inside a blackout,
 277     /// eligible cells at last firing, total cells shifted this session).
 278     blackout_shift_debug: (bool, usize, usize),
 279     /// Last non-hazard eye position used by pit-lattice recovery.
 280     last_safe_position: [f32; 3],
 281     /// Active Backrooms level; chunks are requested for this level.
 282     level: u32,
 283     /// How long the player has been pushing into a wall without moving.
 284     push_seconds: f32,
 285     /// Seconds until the next noclip roll is allowed.
 286     noclip_cooldown: f32,
 287     /// xorshift state for the noclip dice.
 288     rng: u64,
 289     /// Transient dropped-flare state and renderer-light selection.
 290     flares: FlareField,
 291     /// Session pedometer: resolved horizontal movement (world units).
 292     distance_m: f64,
 293     /// The wanderer's embodied telemetry: pedometer, exertion, fatigue,
 294     /// pulse. Advanced once per tick with the collision-resolved movement.
 295     body: Body,
 296     /// Cached navigation objective (a resident level door) plus the
 297     /// recompute cooldown; selection re-runs on a bounded cadence and is
 298     /// invalidated on level switches and reality transitions.
 299     route_target: Option<RouteTarget>,
 300     route_cooldown: f32,
 301     /// Vitals, carried supplies, felt temperature, consumption, and
 302     /// attrition policy form one survival aggregate.
 303     survival: SurvivalInventory,
 304     /// Engine-time seconds used for deterministic CPU-side light flicker.
 305     time_seconds: f64,
 306     /// Seconds until a level door may fire again.
 307     door_cooldown: f32,
 308 }
 309 
 310 impl Engine {
 311     pub fn new(
 312         config: EngineConfig,
 313         renderer: Box<dyn RendererPort>,
 314         source: Box<dyn ChunkSourcePort>,
 315     ) -> Self {
 316         let radius = config.chunk_radius.clamp(0, 2);
 317         let artifact_needs = renderer.artifact_needs();
 318         // Mesh renderers hold their own chunk meshes and have no atlas to
 319         // fit, so their footprint is bounded by the LOD ladder rather than by
 320         // a fixed chunk count: the far ring is cheap enough to reach past the
 321         // fog. The raymarcher cannot — its chunk table is a fixed-size GPU
 322         // array — so it stays on the collision radius.
 323         let visual_radius = if artifact_needs.needs_surface_extraction() {
 324             config.lod.radius_in_chunks(config.chunk_size)
 325         } else {
 326             radius
 327         };
 328         let mut player = Player::new(config.spawn);
 329         player.yaw = config.spawn_yaw;
 330         Self {
 331             player,
 332             // Collision residency is omnidirectional on purpose: it may
 333             // never depend on view direction.
 334             policy: StreamingPolicy::omnidirectional(config.chunk_size, radius),
 335             visual_policy: StreamingPolicy {
 336                 chunk_size: config.chunk_size,
 337                 radius: visual_radius,
 338                 core_radius: VISUAL_CORE_RADIUS.min(visual_radius),
 339             },
 340             store: ChunkStore::new(),
 341             pool: AtlasPool::new(),
 342             world: CollisionWorld::new(),
 343             draws: Vec::new(),
 344             atlas_nodes: 0,
 345             governor: PerfGovernor::new(),
 346             artifact_needs,
 347             renderer,
 348             source,
 349             pending: HashMap::new(),
 350             completed_backlog: Vec::new(),
 351             next_request_id: 1,
 352             reality: RealitySnapshot::default(),
 353             forced_reloads: HashSet::new(),
 354             drift_near: HashSet::new(),
 355             blackout_shift_cooldown: 0.0,
 356             blackout_shift_debug: (false, 0, 0),
 357             last_safe_position: config.spawn,
 358             level: config.initial_level,
 359             push_seconds: 0.0,
 360             noclip_cooldown: 0.0,
 361             rng: (config.seed as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15) | 1,
 362             flares: FlareField::default(),
 363             distance_m: 0.0,
 364             body: Body::default(),
 365             route_target: None,
 366             route_cooldown: 0.0,
 367             survival: SurvivalInventory::new(thermal::dark_baseline_c(config.initial_level)),
 368             time_seconds: 0.0,
 369             door_cooldown: 0.0,
 370             config,
 371         }
 372     }
 373 
 374     /// Switches the active level: drop every resident chunk so the streamer
 375     /// rebuilds the world from the new level's generator, then optionally
 376     /// relocate the player to an arrival point in the new coordinate space.
 377     fn switch_level(&mut self, target: u32, arrival: Option<[f32; 3]>) {
 378         self.level = target;
 379         self.store.retain_keys(&[]);
 380         // In-flight loads are for the old level; their completions will be
 381         // rejected by the level check, and clearing pending lets the new
 382         // level re-request the same keys immediately.
 383         self.pending.clear();
 384         self.completed_backlog.clear();
 385         self.forced_reloads.clear();
 386         // The whole world is regenerated: drop the pool so the next stream
 387         // pass relayouts and re-uploads from scratch.
 388         self.pool = AtlasPool::new();
 389         self.renderer.clear_surfaces();
 390         self.world.rebuild([].iter());
 391         self.draws.clear();
 392         self.push_seconds = 0.0;
 393         // Flares are world objects of the level they were lit in.
 394         self.flares.clear();
 395         self.abandon_all_watched_drift_cells();
 396         if let Some(arrival) = arrival {
 397             self.player.relocate(arrival);
 398         }
 399         self.last_safe_position = self.player.position;
 400         // Telemetry from the departed level must never survive the door.
 401         self.invalidate_route();
 402         // The felt air snaps toward the new level's baseline over the
 403         // ordinary inertia; no need to reset it here.
 404         self.door_cooldown = DOOR_COOLDOWN_S;
 405     }
 406 
 407     /// The active Backrooms level id.
 408     pub fn level(&self) -> u32 {
 409         self.level
 410     }
 411 
 412     /// Per-level atmosphere shared by every renderer: the grassland is an
 413     /// open daylight plane, Level 1 carries its canonical low fog, and
 414     /// everything else keeps the interior palette.
 415     pub fn environment(&self) -> Environment {
 416         match self.level {
 417             LEVEL_GRASSLAND => Environment::daylight(),
 418             LEVEL_HABITABLE => Environment::habitable(),
 419             _ => Environment::interior(),
 420         }
 421     }
 422 
 423     /// Survival vitals (read-only view for presenters/tests).
 424     pub fn vitals(&self) -> PlayerVitals {
 425         self.survival.vitals()
 426     }
 427 
 428     /// Test-only vitals override, for exercising attrition paths without
 429     /// simulating twenty real minutes.
 430     #[cfg(test)]
 431     pub(crate) fn set_vitals_for_test(&mut self, vitals: PlayerVitals) {
 432         self.survival.set_vitals_for_test(vitals);
 433     }
 434 
 435     /// Immutable encounter-state snapshot currently used to key generation.
 436     /// A later traversal layer will own safe snapshot transitions; exposing
 437     /// the current value here does not itself mutate or remap the world.
 438     pub fn reality_snapshot(&self) -> &RealitySnapshot {
 439         &self.reality
 440     }
 441 
 442     /// Advances the simulation one frame and issues the draw.
 443     pub fn tick(&mut self, dt_seconds: f32, input: &InputFrame) {
 444         // Clamp dt so a background-tab hitch can't teleport the player.
 445         let dt = dt_seconds.clamp(0.0, 0.1);
 446         self.governor.update(dt_seconds * 1000.0);
 447         self.time_seconds += dt as f64;
 448 
 449         let old_pos = self.player.position;
 450         // The body's bounded movement multiplier from the *previous* tick's
 451         // state degrades acceleration and sustainable speed together;
 452         // collision resolution itself is untouched.
 453         let effort = self.body.movement_factor();
 454         // Resolved walking distance of this tick only; feeds the pedometer
 455         // and the exertion model.
 456         let mut walked_m = 0.0f32;
 457         if input.locked {
 458             self.player.apply_look(input.look_dx, input.look_dy);
 459             self.player
 460                 .step_with_effort(dt, &input.intent, &self.world, effort);
 461 
 462             // Pedometer: measured here — immediately after the one
 463             // collision-resolved integration step — so relocations that
 464             // happen later in the tick (pit recovery, noclip, red-loop
 465             // handling) and out-of-band teleports can never inflate it.
 466             // Look input contributes nothing: only position deltas count.
 467             let dx = self.player.position[0] - old_pos[0];
 468             let dz = self.player.position[2] - old_pos[2];
 469             let step = (dx * dx + dz * dz).sqrt();
 470             // Anything faster than sprint speed in one frame is a
 471             // discontinuity, not walking.
 472             if step < 1.0 {
 473                 self.distance_m += step as f64;
 474                 walked_m = step;
 475             }
 476         }
 477         self.update_flares(dt, input);
 478         self.update_anomalies(old_pos);
 479         self.update_provisions(dt);
 480         self.update_peripheral_shift(dt);
 481         self.update_noclip(dt, input, old_pos);
 482 
 483         self.stream_chunks();
 484 
 485         let mut scene_lights = select_scene_lights(
 486             self.store
 487                 .iter_ordered()
 488                 .flat_map(|chunk| chunk.payload.lights.iter()),
 489             self.player.position,
 490         );
 491         // Fluorescent flicker is applied here, once, CPU-side — exactly like
 492         // flare flicker — so every renderer sees the same fluctuating world
 493         // and no shader needs a clock.
 494         let flicker_time = self.time_seconds as f32;
 495         for light in &mut scene_lights {
 496             light.intensity *= fixture_flicker_gain(light.id, light.flicker_mode, flicker_time);
 497         }
 498 
 499         // Survival: the lit scene *is* the heat source. The felt ambient
 500         // chases the instantaneous value with thermal inertia, then the
 501         // vitals advance under it (heat accelerates thirst).
 502         let instantaneous_c = thermal::ambient_celsius(
 503             self.level,
 504             self.player.position,
 505             &scene_lights,
 506             self.world
 507                 .count_centers_within_xz(self.player.position, thermal::ENCLOSURE_RADIUS),
 508         );
 509         self.survival.advance_vitals(dt, instantaneous_c);
 510 
 511         // OPTIMIZATION: bound the fixtures a production renderer evaluates
 512         // per fragment. Thermal already consumed the full ranked list above;
 513         // `select_scene_lights` sorts nearest/most-important first, so this
 514         // keeps ordinary rooms visually identical while capping the
 515         // pathological case of a fixture-dense layout across the whole
 516         // streaming neighborhood. See `MAX_ANALYTIC_SCENE_LIGHTS_PER_FRAME`.
 517         scene_lights.truncate(MAX_ANALYTIC_SCENE_LIGHTS_PER_FRAME);
 518 
 519         // Consumption is deliberate; the survival aggregate also owns the
 520         // optional accessibility policy that acts after explicit choices.
 521         self.survival.consume(ConsumptionIntent {
 522             drink: input.drink,
 523             eat: input.eat,
 524         });
 525         // The body listens to the same survival state the vitals own; the
 526         // resolved walking distance is the only movement it ever sees.
 527         let survival = self.survival.readout();
 528         self.body.advance(
 529             dt,
 530             walked_m,
 531             BodyContext {
 532                 hydration: survival.vitals.hydration,
 533                 satiety: survival.vitals.satiety,
 534                 condition: survival.vitals.condition,
 535                 ambient_c: survival.ambient_c,
 536             },
 537         );
 538         self.update_route(dt);
 539         if self.survival.succumb_if_dead() {
 540             self.respawn_after_attrition();
 541         }
 542         // Strain: mismanagement in either direction raises the reality's
 543         // delirium tier, and chunks generated from here on carry more
 544         // anomalous infill, sealed doorways, shut corridor mouths, and
 545         // thinner provisions. Resident chunks are untouched — the world
 546         // worsens as it streams, never as a visible pop. Dehydration bands
 547         // punish the underconsumer; the excess meter (wasted supplies)
 548         // punishes the overconsumer with the very same tiers.
 549         let tier = self.survival.advance_strain(dt);
 550         if tier != self.reality.delirium() {
 551             self.reality = self.reality.with_delirium(tier);
 552         }
 553 
 554         let flare_lights = self
 555             .flares
 556             .lights(self.player.position, self.time_seconds as f32);
 557         let frame = FrameParams {
 558             camera_pos: self.player.position,
 559             yaw: self.player.yaw,
 560             pitch: self.player.pitch,

 561             flashlight: input.flashlight,
 562             dynamic_lights: flare_lights.lights,
 563             dynamic_light_count: flare_lights.count,
 564             scene_lights,
 565             environment: self.environment(),
 566             supply_sprites: self.collect_supply_sprites(),
 567         };
 568         self.renderer.draw(&frame, &self.draws);
 569     }
 570 
 571     /// Supplies player intent and collision context to the flare lifecycle.
 572     fn update_flares(&mut self, dt: f32, input: &InputFrame) {
 573         self.flares.advance(dt);
 574         if !(input.drop_flare && input.locked) {
 575             return;
 576         }
 577         let eye = self.player.position;
 578         let forward = self.player.forward();
 579         self.flares.drop_from(eye, forward, &self.world);
 580     }
 581 
 582     /// Active flares (world-space runtime state), oldest first.
 583     pub fn flares(&self) -> &[Flare] {
 584         self.flares.active()
 585     }
 586 
 587     /// Session pedometer reading in meters.
 588     pub fn distance_m(&self) -> f32 {
 589         self.distance_m as f32
 590     }
 591 
 592     /// Squared distance from the player to the nearest point of a chunk's
 593     /// 2D footprint; 0 inside the chunk. Drives the fine/coarse LOD choice.
 594     /// The LOD the ladder wants for the chunk at this origin.
 595     fn desired_lod(&self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32) -> u8 {
 596         self.config.lod.lod_at(self.chunk_dist2(origin_x, origin_z).sqrt())
 597     }
 598 
 599     fn chunk_dist2(&self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32) -> f32 {
 600         let cs = self.config.chunk_size;
 601         let (px, pz) = (self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]);
 602         let dx = (origin_x - px).max(px - (origin_x + cs)).max(0.0);
 603         let dz = (origin_z - pz).max(pz - (origin_z + cs)).max(0.0);
 604         dx * dx + dz * dz
 605     }
 606 
 607     fn update_anomalies(&mut self, old_pos: [f32; 3]) {
 608         if self.level != LEVEL_BACKROOMS {
 609             self.last_safe_position = self.player.position;
 610             return;
 611         }
 612 
 613         let hazards: Vec<_> = self.store.all_pit_hazards().copied().collect();
 614         if let Some(hazard) = hazards
 615             .iter()
 616             .find(|h| h.contains(self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]))
 617         {
 618             let authored = [
 619                 hazard.recovery.x,
 620                 self.player.position[1],
 621                 hazard.recovery.z,
 622             ];
 623             let recovery = if self.world.collides(authored) {
 624                 self.last_safe_position
 625             } else {
 626                 authored
 627             };
 628             self.player.relocate(recovery);
 629             self.last_safe_position = recovery;
 630             return;
 631         }
 632 
 633         let mut gates: Vec<_> = self.store.all_traversal_gates().copied().collect();
 634         gates.sort_by_key(|g| g.id);
 635         gates.dedup_by_key(|g| g.id);
 636         for gate in gates {
 637             let Some(direction) = gate.crossing(
 638                 [old_pos[0], old_pos[2]],
 639                 [self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]],
 640             ) else {
 641                 continue;
 642             };
 643             if gate.kind == TraversalGateKind::RedThreshold && direction != gate.forward {
 644                 continue;
 645             }
 646             let next_reality = self.reality.with_advanced_gate(&gate, direction);
 647             if next_reality == self.reality {
 648                 continue;
 649             }
 650             self.reality = next_reality;
 651             // A reality transition retires every cached telemetry selection:
 652             // the route must reselect against the new address, never mix.
 653             self.invalidate_route();
 654 
 655             if gate.anomaly_kind == AnomalyKind::RedRoom {
 656                 // A committed Red Room selects another infinite Level 0
 657                 // address. Every resident chunk belongs to the old address,
 658                 // so replacing only the vestibule would splice two realities
 659                 // at an arbitrary streaming boundary.
 660                 let targets: Vec<_> = self
 661                     .store
 662                     .iter_ordered()
 663                     .map(|chunk| chunk_key(chunk.origin.0, chunk.origin.1))
 664                     .collect();
 665                 for key in targets {
 666                     // A pre-threshold refinement for this key is no longer
 667                     // authoritative; its late completion cannot clear the new
 668                     // exact request identity.
 669                     self.force_rebuild(key);
 670                 }
 671             }
 672         }
 673         self.last_safe_position = self.player.position;
 674     }
 675 
 676     /// Supply pickups and level doors, both exported by generation beside
 677     /// the geometry. Pickups fold into the reality snapshot (a consumed
 678     /// bottle never regenerates); doors switch the streamed level.
 679     fn update_provisions(&mut self, dt: f32) {
 680         self.door_cooldown = (self.door_cooldown - dt).max(0.0);
 681         let (px, pz) = (self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]);
 682 
 683         // -- pickups ---------------------------------------------------------
 684         // Halo overlap can surface the same item from two chunks; dedupe by
 685         // id so one bottle never quenches twice.
 686         let mut grabbed: Vec<_> = self
 687             .store
 688             .all_supply_items()
 689             .filter(|item| {
 690                 item.within_reach(px, pz, PICKUP_REACH) && !self.reality.supply_consumed(item.id)
 691             })
 692             .copied()
 693             .collect();
 694         grabbed.sort_by_key(|item| item.id);
 695         grabbed.dedup_by_key(|item| item.id);
 696         for item in grabbed {
 697             // Pickups stock the pockets; drinking and eating are deliberate
 698             // acts. Full pockets leave the item standing in the world instead
 699             // of force-feeding the wanderer — walking past a bottle is never
 700             // gluttony by itself.
 701             if !self.survival.try_pickup(item.kind) {
 702                 continue;
 703             }
 704             self.reality = self.reality.with_supply_consumed(item.id);
 705             // Rebuild the chunk holding the marker under the advanced
 706             // reality so the bottle visibly leaves the world.
 707             let cs = self.config.chunk_size;
 708             let key = chunk_key(
 709                 (item.position.x / cs).floor() * cs,
 710                 (item.position.z / cs).floor() * cs,
 711             );
 712             self.force_rebuild(key);
 713         }
 714 
 715         // -- level doors ------------------------------------------------------
 716         if self.door_cooldown > 0.0 {
 717             return;
 718         }
 719         let transit = self
 720             .store
 721             .all_level_exits()
 722             .find(|exit| exit.contains(px, pz))
 723             .copied();
 724         if let Some(exit) = transit {
 725             let arrival = [exit.arrival.x, self.player.position[1], exit.arrival.z];
 726             self.switch_level(exit.target_level, Some(arrival));
 727         }
 728     }
 729 
 730     /// The nearest unconsumed supply labels, ready for billboard drawing.
 731     /// Labels float a little above the marker so the logo reads over the
 732     /// bottle/tin voxels.
 733     pub fn collect_supply_sprites(&self) -> Vec<crate::application::ports::SupplySprite> {
 734         use crate::application::ports::{MAX_SUPPLY_SPRITES, SupplySprite};
 735         const LABEL_CULL: f32 = 14.0;
 736         let (px, pz) = (self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]);
 737         let mut near: Vec<(f32, SupplySprite)> = self
 738             .store
 739             .all_supply_items()
 740             .filter(|item| !self.reality.supply_consumed(item.id))
 741             .filter_map(|item| {
 742                 let dx = item.position.x - px;
 743                 let dz = item.position.z - pz;
 744                 let d2 = dx * dx + dz * dz;
 745                 (d2 < LABEL_CULL * LABEL_CULL).then_some((
 746                     d2,
 747                     SupplySprite {
 748                         position: [item.position.x, item.rest_y + 0.62, item.position.z],
 749                         atlas_row: match item.kind {
 750                             SupplyKind::AlmondWater => 0,
 751                             SupplyKind::Ration => 1,
 752                         },
 753                     },
 754                 ))
 755             })
 756             .collect();
 757         near.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.total_cmp(&b.0));
 758         // Halo overlap can list one item twice; identical positions dedupe.
 759         near.dedup_by(|a, b| a.1 == b.1);
 760         near.truncate(MAX_SUPPLY_SPRITES);
 761         near.into_iter().map(|(_, sprite)| sprite).collect()
 762     }
 763 
 764     /// Death by attrition: the wanderer wakes at the level's arrival point
 765     /// after the survival aggregate has reset vitals and pockets. The world —
 766     /// drift, consumed supplies, sealed rooms — remembers everything; only
 767     /// the body's strain resets (the session pedometer keeps its count).
 768     fn respawn_after_attrition(&mut self) {
 769         self.body.reset_strain();
 770         let spawn = level_spawn(self.level, self.config.spawn);
 771         self.player.relocate(spawn);
 772         self.last_safe_position = spawn;
 773         self.invalidate_route();
 774     }
 775 
 776     /// Accessibility option: automatic consumption of carried supplies.
 777     pub fn set_assisted_consumption(&mut self, enabled: bool) {
 778         self.survival.set_assisted_consumption(enabled);
 779     }
 780 
 781     fn make_request_for(
 782         &mut self,
 783         origin_x: f32,
 784         origin_z: f32,
 785         lod: u8,
 786         reality: RealitySnapshot,
 787     ) -> ChunkRequest {
 788         let request_id = self.next_request_id;
 789         self.next_request_id = self.next_request_id.wrapping_add(1);
 790         if self.next_request_id == 0 {
 791             self.next_request_id = 1;
 792         }
 793         ChunkRequest {
 794             request_id,
 795             origin_x,
 796             origin_z,
 797             level: self.level,
 798             lod,
 799             artifacts: self.artifact_needs,
 800             reality,
 801         }
 802     }
 803 
 804     fn make_request(&mut self, origin_x: f32, origin_z: f32, lod: u8) -> ChunkRequest {
 805         self.make_request_for(origin_x, origin_z, lod, self.reality.clone())
 806     }
 807 
 808     /// Installs finished background loads, discarding stale work: a result
 809     /// for the wrong level (noclip happened), for a chunk that left the
 810     /// streaming footprint, or for a LOD no better than what is already
 811     /// resident. Refinement stays monotonic exactly like the sync path.
 812     ///
 813     /// Installs are metered by the same per-tick cost budget as synchronous
 814     /// loads (coarse = 1, fine = `FINE_LOAD_COST`): when a burst of worker
 815     /// results lands in one frame, the overflow waits in
 816     /// `completed_backlog` instead of stacking mesh uploads and collision
 817     /// rebuilds into a single frame.
 818     fn install_completed(
 819         &mut self,
 820         keep: &[ChunkKey],
 821         loaded: &mut Vec<ChunkKey>,
 822         changed: &mut bool,
 823     ) {
 824         // A transport failure is not a completion, but it must retire the
 825         // exact pending order or that chunk can never be scheduled again.
 826         // Old worker callbacks cannot cancel a newer retry because request
 827         // identity includes the engine-assigned monotonic id and reality.
 828         for failed in self.source.poll_failed_requests() {
 829             let key = chunk_key(failed.origin_x, failed.origin_z);
 830             let is_current = self
 831                 .pending
 832                 .get(&key)
 833                 .is_some_and(|pending| pending.is_same_request(&failed));
 834             if is_current {
 835                 self.pending.remove(&key);
 836             }
 837         }
 838 
 839         let fresh = self.source.poll_completed();
 840         self.completed_backlog.extend(fresh);
 841         let mut budget = (self.config.max_loads_per_tick as u32 * FINE_LOAD_COST).max(1);
 842         let mut deferred: Vec<CompletedChunk> = Vec::new();
 843         for done in self.completed_backlog.drain(..).collect::<Vec<_>>() {
 844             let install_cost = if done.request.lod == 0 {
 845                 FINE_LOAD_COST
 846             } else {
 847                 1
 848             };
 849             if budget < install_cost {
 850                 deferred.push(done);
 851                 continue;
 852             }
 853             let req = &done.request;
 854             let key = chunk_key(req.origin_x, req.origin_z);
 855             // A completion is authoritative only while the exact order it
 856             // echoes is still pending. In particular, an old result for the
 857             // same chunk must not remove a newer pending request.
 858             let is_current = self
 859                 .pending
 860                 .get(&key)
 861                 .is_some_and(|pending| pending.is_same_request(req));
 862             if !is_current {
 863                 continue;
 864             }
 865             self.pending.remove(&key);
 866             if req.level != self.level || !keep.contains(&key) {
 867                 continue;
 868             }
 869             let is_forced = self.forced_reloads.contains(&key);
 870             let improves = match self.store.get(key) {
 871                 None => true,
 872                 // LOD is monotonic only inside one exact reality. A chunk
 873                 // from a replaced reality is replaced even if its old LOD was
 874                 // finer; comparing their LODs would preserve stale geometry.
 875                 Some(resident) if resident.is_in_reality(&req.reality) => req.lod < resident.lod,
 876                 Some(_) => is_forced,
 877             };
 878             if !improves {
 879                 continue;
 880             }
 881             if is_forced {
 882                 let player = player_aabb(self.player.position);
 883                 if done
 884                     .payload
 885                     .collision
 886                     .iter()
 887                     .any(|solid| solid.intersects(&player))
 888                 {
 889                     // Safety beats the effect: keep the old resident reality
 890                     // but do not abandon the transition. Defer this chunk and
 891                     // restore its pending status so we try again next tick.
 892                     self.pending.insert(key, req.clone());
 893                     deferred.push(done);
 894                     continue;
 895                 }
 896             }
 897             budget -= install_cost;
 898             self.store.insert(
 899                 key,
 900                 LoadedChunk::new(

 901                     (req.origin_x, req.origin_z),
 902                     req.lod,
 903                     req.reality.clone(),
 904                     done.payload,
 905                 ),
 906             );
 907             if !loaded.contains(&key) {
 908                 loaded.push(key);
 909             }
 910             *changed = true;
 911             self.forced_reloads.remove(&key);
 912         }
 913         self.completed_backlog = deferred;
 914         // Drop pending entries that left the footprint so their slots free
 915         // up; a late completion for them is discarded by the keep check.
 916         self.pending
 917             .retain(|key, request| keep.contains(key) && request.level == self.level);
 918     }
 919 
 920     /// Tops up the background request queue: coarse availability for every
 921     /// missing chunk (nearest first), then at most one fine refinement in
 922     /// flight at a time, mirroring the sync path's priorities.
 923     fn issue_requests(&mut self, desired: &[(f32, f32)], desired_visual: &[(f32, f32)]) {
 924         // Generation concurrency and installation cost are separate budgets:
 925         // saturate the source's worker pool here, then time-slice completed
 926         // payload installation elsewhere so 32 workers never imply a frame
 927         // with 32 atlas uploads.
 928         let max_pending = self
 929             .source
 930             .max_concurrent_requests()
 931             .max(self.config.max_loads_per_tick * 2)
 932             .max(4);
 933 
 934         let forced: Vec<_> = self
 935             .forced_reloads
 936             .iter()
 937             .filter_map(|&key| {
 938                 self.store
 939                     .get(key)
 940                     .map(|chunk| (key, chunk.origin.0, chunk.origin.1, chunk.lod))
 941             })
 942             .collect();
 943         for (key, ox, oz, lod) in forced {
 944             if self.pending.len() >= max_pending {
 945                 break;
 946             }
 947             if !self.pending.contains_key(&key) {
 948                 let request = self.make_request(ox, oz, lod);
 949                 self.pending.insert(key, request.clone());
 950                 self.source.request(request);
 951             }
 952         }
 953 
 954         for &(ox, oz) in desired_visual {
 955             if self.pending.len() >= max_pending {
 956                 break;
 957             }
 958             let key = chunk_key(ox, oz);
 959             if !self.store.contains(key) && !self.pending.contains_key(&key) {
 960                 let request = self.make_request(ox, oz, INITIAL_LOD);
 961                 self.pending.insert(key, request.clone());
 962                 self.source.request(request);
 963             }
 964         }
 965 
 966         let fine_in_flight = self.pending.values().any(|request| request.lod == 0);
 967         if fine_in_flight || self.pending.len() >= max_pending {
 968             return;
 969         }
 970         // Refine the nearest chunk held coarser than the ladder wants.
 971         // `desired` is already sorted nearest-first, so this spends the
 972         // budget where the error is largest.
 973         let target = desired.iter().copied().find_map(|(ox, oz)| {
 974             let key = chunk_key(ox, oz);
 975             let want = self.desired_lod(ox, oz);
 976             (!self.pending.contains_key(&key)
 977                 && self.store.get(key).is_some_and(|c| c.lod > want))
 978             .then_some((ox, oz, want))
 979         });
 980         if let Some((ox, oz, want)) = target {
 981             let key = chunk_key(ox, oz);
 982             let resident_reality = self.store.get(key).unwrap().reality.clone();
 983             let request = self.make_request_for(ox, oz, want, resident_reality);
 984             self.pending.insert(key, request.clone());
 985             self.source.request(request);
 986         }
 987     }
 988 
 989     /// Progressive, error-driven chunk streaming.
 990     ///
 991     /// Availability first: every missing chunk (nearest first) loads at the
 992     /// cheap coarse LOD, so the whole footprint renders before any chunk is
 993     /// refined. Refinement second: with leftover budget, the nearest
 994     /// resident coarse chunk within `fine_distance` reloads at full
 995     /// resolution in place. Chunks beyond `fine_distance` stay coarse — at
 996     /// that range a coarse voxel projects to about a fine voxel's pixels —
 997     /// and refinement is monotonic while resident, so there is no flapping.
 998     ///
 999     /// Both phases share one per-tick cost budget (coarse = 1 unit, fine =
1000     /// `FINE_LOAD_COST`), keeping the worst-case tick at the old cost of
1001     /// `max_loads_per_tick` fine loads. Newly loaded and refined chunks
1002     /// upload only their own atlas slot rows; a full re-upload only happens
1003     /// on pool relayouts (first load, bigger chunks, level switch) or on
1004     /// back ends without partial-update support.
1005     fn stream_chunks(&mut self) {
1006         let surface_renderer = self.artifact_needs.needs_surface_extraction();
1007         let desired = self
1008             .policy
1009             .desired_origins(self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]);
1010         // Visibility streaming: beyond the core radius, only chunks the
1011         // player could actually see are worth generating. In a corridor
1012         // world the square footprint is mostly behind walls and behind the
1013         // player.
1014         let desired_visual = self.visual_policy.desired_origins_in_view(
1015             self.player.position[0],
1016             self.player.position[2],
1017             Some(ViewCone::from_yaw(self.player.yaw, VISUAL_CONE_HALF_ANGLE)),
1018         );
1019         let keep: Vec<_> = desired_visual
1020             .iter()
1021             .map(|&(x, z)| chunk_key(x, z))
1022             .collect();
1023 
1024         // Free the atlas slots of chunks about to be evicted.
1025         let evicted: Vec<ChunkKey> = self
1026             .store
1027             .iter_ordered()
1028             .map(|c| chunk_key(c.origin.0, c.origin.1))
1029             .filter(|k| !keep.contains(k))
1030             .collect();
1031         let mut changed = self.store.retain_keys(&keep);
1032         self.forced_reloads.retain(|key| keep.contains(key));
1033         if surface_renderer {
1034             if !evicted.is_empty() {
1035                 self.renderer.remove_surfaces(&evicted);
1036             }
1037         } else {
1038             for key in evicted {
1039                 self.pool.release(key);
1040             }
1041         }
1042 
1043         let mut loaded: Vec<ChunkKey> = Vec::new();
1044         if self.source.is_async() {
1045             // Background pipeline: install validated completions, then top
1046             // up the request queue. The frame never blocks on generation.
1047             self.install_completed(&keep, &mut loaded, &mut changed);
1048             self.issue_requests(&desired, &desired_visual);
1049         } else {
1050             let mut budget = self.config.max_loads_per_tick as u32 * FINE_LOAD_COST;
1051 
1052             // Red-room closure is a semantic transition, not ordinary LOD
1053             // work. Rebuild the small affected set first and install each
1054             // complete payload atomically across its geometry/collision/light
1055             // views. The threshold bend keeps this set out of direct sight.
1056             let forced: Vec<_> = self
1057                 .forced_reloads
1058                 .iter()
1059                 .filter_map(|&key| {
1060                     self.store
1061                         .get(key)
1062                         .map(|c| (key, c.origin.0, c.origin.1, c.lod))
1063                 })
1064                 .collect();
1065             for (key, ox, oz, lod) in forced {
1066                 let payload = self.source.load_with_artifacts(
1067                     ox,
1068                     oz,
1069                     self.level,
1070                     lod,
1071                     &self.reality,
1072                     self.artifact_needs,
1073                 );
1074                 let player = player_aabb(self.player.position);
1075                 if payload
1076                     .collision
1077                     .iter()
1078                     .any(|solid| solid.intersects(&player))
1079                 {
1080                     self.forced_reloads.remove(&key);
1081                     continue;
1082                 }
1083                 self.store.insert(
1084                     key,
1085                     LoadedChunk::new((ox, oz), lod, self.reality.clone(), payload),
1086                 );
1087                 self.forced_reloads.remove(&key);
1088                 loaded.push(key);
1089                 changed = true;
1090             }
1091 
1092             // Phase 1 — availability: missing chunks come in coarse, nearest
1093             // first. Only a leftover budget flows into refinement, so a moving
1094             // player always fills holes before sharpening anything.
1095             for &(ox, oz) in &desired_visual {
1096                 if budget == 0 {
1097                     break;
1098                 }
1099                 let key = chunk_key(ox, oz);
1100                 if !self.store.contains(key) {
1101                     let payload = self.source.load_with_artifacts(
1102                         ox,
1103                         oz,
1104                         self.level,
1105                         INITIAL_LOD,
1106                         &self.reality,
1107                         self.artifact_needs,
1108                     );
1109                     self.store.insert(
1110                         key,
1111                         LoadedChunk::new((ox, oz), INITIAL_LOD, self.reality.clone(), payload),
1112                     );
1113                     loaded.push(key);
1114                     budget -= 1;
1115                     changed = true;
1116                 }
1117             }
1118 
1119             // Phase 2 — refinement: nearest chunk held coarser than the
1120             // ladder wants it.
1121             while budget >= FINE_LOAD_COST {
1122                 let target = desired.iter().copied().find_map(|(ox, oz)| {
1123                     let want = self.desired_lod(ox, oz);
1124                     self.store
1125                         .get(chunk_key(ox, oz))
1126                         .is_some_and(|c| c.lod > want)
1127                         .then_some((ox, oz, want))
1128                 });
1129                 let Some((ox, oz, want)) = target else { break };
1130                 let key = chunk_key(ox, oz);
1131                 let resident_reality = self.store.get(key).unwrap().reality.clone();
1132                 let payload = self.source.load_with_artifacts(
1133                     ox,
1134                     oz,
1135                     self.level,
1136                     want,
1137                     &resident_reality,
1138                     self.artifact_needs,
1139                 );
1140                 self.store.insert(
1141                     key,
1142                     LoadedChunk::new((ox, oz), want, resident_reality, payload),
1143                 );
1144                 if !loaded.contains(&key) {
1145                     loaded.push(key);
1146                 }
1147                 budget -= FINE_LOAD_COST;
1148                 changed = true;
1149             }
1150         }
1151 
1152         if !changed {
1153             return;
1154         }
1155 
1156         // Raster strategies upload only changed/replaced surface artifacts.
1157         // Collision stays resident as neutral AABBs; unrequested serialized
1158         // SVO nodes never enter the payload or atlas.
1159         if surface_renderer {
1160             let surface_updates: Vec<SurfaceChunk<'_>> = loaded
1161                 .iter()
1162                 .filter_map(|&key| {
1163                     self.store.get(key).map(|chunk| SurfaceChunk {
1164                         key,
1165                         origin: [chunk.origin.0, 0.0, chunk.origin.1],
1166                         mesh: &chunk.payload.surface,
1167                     })
1168                 })
1169                 .collect();
1170             if !surface_updates.is_empty() {
1171                 self.renderer.upload_surfaces(&surface_updates);
1172             }
1173 
1174             self.draws.clear();
1175             for chunk in self.store.iter_ordered() {
1176                 self.draws.push(ChunkDraw {
1177                     origin: [chunk.origin.0, 0.0, chunk.origin.1],
1178                     root_index: 0,
1179                     world_size: chunk.payload.world_size,
1180                     voxel_size: chunk.payload.voxel_size,
1181                     svo_depth: chunk.payload.svo_depth,
1182                 });
1183             }
1184             self.draws.truncate(MAX_CHUNKS);
1185             self.atlas_nodes = self
1186                 .store
1187                 .iter_ordered()
1188                 .map(|c| c.payload.nodes.len() / 4)
1189                 .sum();
1190             self.world.rebuild(self.store.all_collision_boxes());
1191             self.flares.extinguish_buried(self.world.boxes());
1192             return;
1193         }
1194 
1195         // Size the pool for the streaming footprint and the largest chunk.
1196         let num_slots = ((2 * self.policy.radius + 1).pow(2) as usize).min(MAX_CHUNKS);
1197         let rows = self
1198             .store
1199             .iter_ordered()
1200             .map(|c| payload_rows(&c.payload))
1201             .max()
1202             .unwrap_or(1)
1203             .max(1);
1204         let brick_rows = self
1205             .store
1206             .iter_ordered()
1207             .map(|c| payload_brick_rows(&c.payload))
1208             .max()
1209             .unwrap_or(0);
1210         let mut need_full = self
1211             .pool
1212             .ensure_layout_with_bricks(num_slots, rows, brick_rows);
1213 
1214         if !need_full {
1215             for &key in &loaded {
1216                 let uploaded = match self.pool.assign(key) {
1217                     Some(slot) => {
1218                         let payload = &self.store.get(key).expect("just inserted").payload;
1219                         let block = self.pool.rebased_block(slot, payload);
1220                         let first_row = self.pool.slot_first_row(slot) as u32;
1221                         let nodes_uploaded = self.renderer.upload_atlas_rows(first_row, &block);
1222                         // A node block is meaningless without the voxels its
1223                         // brick pointers name -- patch both incrementally
1224                         // (when the back end supports it) or fall back to a
1225                         // full reupload rather than let them disagree for a
1226                         // frame. Skipped entirely when nothing resident
1227                         // holds bricks: `brick_slot_words()` is then 0.
1228                         let bricks_uploaded = if self.pool.brick_slot_words() == 0 {
1229                             true
1230                         } else {
1231                             let brick_block = self.pool.rebased_brick_block(payload);
1232                             let brick_first_row = self.pool.brick_slot_first_row(slot) as u32;
1233                             self.renderer
1234                                 .upload_brick_voxels_rows(brick_first_row, &brick_block)
1235                         };
1236                         nodes_uploaded && bricks_uploaded
1237                     }
1238                     None => false,
1239                 };
1240                 if !uploaded {
1241                     need_full = true;
1242                     break;
1243                 }
1244             }
1245         }
1246 
1247         if need_full {
1248             let keys: Vec<ChunkKey> = self
1249                 .store
1250                 .iter_ordered()
1251                 .map(|c| chunk_key(c.origin.0, c.origin.1))
1252                 .collect();
1253             for key in keys {
1254                 let _ = self.pool.assign(key);
1255             }
1256             let texels = self
1257                 .pool
1258                 .full_texels(|k| self.store.get(k).map(|c| &c.payload));
1259             self.renderer.upload_atlas(&texels);
1260             if brick_rows > 0 {

1261                 let words = self
1262                     .pool
1263                     .full_brick_words(|k| self.store.get(k).map(|c| &c.payload));
1264                 self.renderer.upload_brick_voxels(&words);
1265             }
1266         }
1267 
1268         self.draws.clear();
1269         for chunk in self.store.iter_ordered() {
1270             let key = chunk_key(chunk.origin.0, chunk.origin.1);
1271             if let Some(offset) = self.pool.node_offset_of(key) {
1272                 self.draws.push(ChunkDraw {
1273                     origin: [chunk.origin.0, 0.0, chunk.origin.1],
1274                     root_index: (offset + chunk.payload.root as usize) as i32,
1275                     world_size: chunk.payload.world_size,
1276                     voxel_size: chunk.payload.voxel_size,
1277                     svo_depth: chunk.payload.svo_depth,
1278                 });
1279             }
1280         }
1281         self.draws.truncate(MAX_CHUNKS);
1282         self.atlas_nodes = self
1283             .store
1284             .iter_ordered()
1285             .map(|c| c.payload.nodes.len() / 4)
1286             .sum();
1287 
1288         self.world.rebuild(self.store.all_collision_boxes());
1289         self.flares.extinguish_buried(self.world.boxes());
1290     }
1291 
1292     /// Forces one chunk to rebuild on its next streaming pass, dropping any
1293     /// in-flight request for it first so a late completion under the old
1294     /// identity can't clear the new one. The shared primitive behind every
1295     /// "this chunk's world just changed out from under it" event: RedRoom
1296     /// threshold crossings, a consumed supply item, and Peripheral Shift's
1297     /// blackout rear-shift all reach for exactly this, not a bespoke pair
1298     /// of map operations each time.
1299     fn force_rebuild(&mut self, key: ChunkKey) {
1300         self.pending.remove(&key);
1301         self.forced_reloads.insert(key);
1302     }

1392     fn pickup_stocks_and_drinking_is_deliberate() {
1393         let mut engine = provisioned_engine();
1394         let input = InputFrame::default();
1395         // Tick 1 streams the spawn chunk; tick 2 grabs the bottle at reach.
1396         engine.tick(1.0 / 60.0, &input);
1397         engine.tick(1.0 / 60.0, &input);
1398         assert!(engine.reality_snapshot().supply_consumed(41));
1399         // A pickup always stocks the pockets; nothing is force-drunk.
1400         assert_eq!(engine.stats().almond_bottles, 1);
1401 
1402         // Low thirst alone changes nothing: consumption is a choice.
1403         engine.set_vitals_for_test(PlayerVitals {
1404             hydration: 0.2,
1405             satiety: 0.9,
1406             condition: 0.9,
1407         });
1408         engine.tick(1.0 / 60.0, &input);
1409         assert_eq!(engine.stats().almond_bottles, 1, "no silent auto-drink");
1410         assert!(engine.vitals().hydration < 0.3);
1411 
1412         // The deliberate drink input spends the bottle and quenches.
1413         let drink = InputFrame {
1414             drink: true,
1415             ..InputFrame::default()
1416         };
1417         engine.tick(1.0 / 60.0, &drink);
1418         assert_eq!(engine.stats().almond_bottles, 0);
1419         assert!(engine.vitals().hydration > 0.5, "drink restored thirst");
1420     }

Now I have the core of engine.rs verified:
- `stream_chunks` at 1005: `desired` O(N log N) (collision policy, radius ≤2 → ≤25) and `desired_visual` O(N log N) (visual radius up to 16 → 1089) — every frame.
- `keep` Vec, `evicted` filter `!keep.contains(k)` at 1025-1030 — O(M·N).
- `retain_keys(&keep)` at 1031 — O(N·M).
- `install_completed` keep.contains at 866, 917.
- `world.rebuild` + `flares.extinguish_buried(self.world.boxes())` at 1190-1191, 1288-1289 — on every `changed` tick. This is O(B) rebuild + O(F×B) extinguish.
- `select_scene_lights` per frame at 485.
- `update_anomalies` gates sort at 633-635.
- `update_provisions` grabbed sort at 686-695.
- `collect_supply_sprites` at 733-762 — per frame sort O(S log S).
- `issue_requests` — `fine_in_flight` O(P) at 966; forced collect at 934; refinement find_map O(N).
- Sync path forced reload loop at 1056-1090 — unbudgeted: each `load_with_artifacts` blocking, loop over ALL forced_reloads without budget check. Actually looking at the code: the forced loop doesn't decrement budget at all! Line 1065-1090: for each forced key, load and install — NO budget check. So after RedRoom threshold crossing, EVERY resident chunk is force-rebuilt in ONE frame synchronously — that could be 1089 chunks × ~10ms+ = 10+ seconds of blocking! Wait — the code: `for (key, ox, oz, lod) in forced { let payload = self.source.load_with_artifacts(...); ... }` — yes, unbudgeted. But wait — is the sync path used in production? The browser uses WorkerChunkSource (async). Sync path is for native/tests. Still, in the sync path this is a real issue.

Also `draws.truncate(MAX_CHUNKS)` at 1184 and 1281: MAX_CHUNKS=25 — surface renderer's draws truncated to 25! For surface renderer, the draws list includes ALL resident chunks (up to 1089), then truncates to 25. The comment says the surface renderer ignores ChunkDraw. Need to check how renderer.draw uses chunks — the surface renderer uses meshes uploaded separately, so draws may be irrelevant. But the diagnostic `resident_chunks` etc. Let me not go too deep here — check ports.rs and rendering/mod.rs.

1572     #[derive(Default)]
1573     struct RecordingRenderer {
1574         uploads: Rc<RefCell<Vec<usize>>>,
1575         row_uploads: Rc<RefCell<Vec<u32>>>,
1576         brick_uploads: Rc<RefCell<Vec<usize>>>,
1577         brick_row_uploads: Rc<RefCell<Vec<u32>>>,
1578         draws: Rc<RefCell<Vec<usize>>>,
1579         light_counts: Rc<RefCell<Vec<usize>>>,
1580         /// When true the renderer accepts partial row updates like the GPU
1581         /// driver; when false it forces the full-upload fallback.
1582         supports_rows: bool,
1583         /// When true the renderer also accepts partial *brick* row updates,
1584         /// like the WebGL2 driver; when false (WebGPU's default: it only
1585         /// ever replaces its whole brick buffer) any resident bricks force
1586         /// the full-upload fallback even if `supports_rows` is set.
1587         supports_brick_rows: bool,
1588     }
1589 
1590     impl RendererPort for RecordingRenderer {
1591         fn upload_atlas(&mut self, texels: &[u32]) {
1592             self.uploads.borrow_mut().push(texels.len());
1593         }
1594         fn upload_atlas_rows(&mut self, first_row: u32, _texels: &[u32]) -> bool {
1595             if self.supports_rows {
1596                 self.row_uploads.borrow_mut().push(first_row);
1597             }
1598             self.supports_rows
1599         }
1600         fn upload_brick_voxels(&mut self, words: &[u32]) {
1601             self.brick_uploads.borrow_mut().push(words.len());
1602         }
1603         fn upload_brick_voxels_rows(&mut self, first_row: u32, _words: &[u32]) -> bool {
1604             if self.supports_brick_rows {
1605                 self.brick_row_uploads.borrow_mut().push(first_row);
1606             }
1607             self.supports_brick_rows
1608         }
1609         fn draw(&mut self, frame: &FrameParams, chunks: &[ChunkDraw]) {
1610             self.draws.borrow_mut().push(chunks.len());
1611             self.light_counts
1612                 .borrow_mut()
1613                 .push(frame.scene_lights.len());
1614         }
1615     }

1658                         radius: 8.0,
1659                         intensity: 2.0,
1660                         kind: crate::application::ports::LightKind::CeilingPanel,
1661                         flicker_mode: 0,
1662                         enabled: true,
1663                     }
1664                 })
1665                 .collect();
1666             ChunkPayload {
1667                 root: 0,
1668                 nodes: [1u32, 0, 0, 0].repeat(1024),
1669                 brick_voxels: Vec::new(),
1670                 world_size: 12.8,
1671                 voxel_size: 0.2,
1672                 svo_depth: 6,
1673                 surface: crate::application::ports::SurfaceMeshPayload::empty(0),

1739     /// Like `FlatChunkSource`, but every chunk holds one brick node pointing
1740     /// at one real brick's worth of voxel words -- `payload_brick_rows` > 0,
1741     /// exercising the incremental brick-row path in `stream_chunks`.
1742     struct BrickedChunkSource;
1743 
1744     impl ChunkSourcePort for BrickedChunkSource {
1745         fn load(&self, origin_x: f32, _origin_z: f32, _level: u32, _lod: u8) -> ChunkPayload {
1746             ChunkPayload {
1747                 root: 0,
1748                 // NODE_KIND_BRICK = 2, word_base = 0: one padded row where

 296     /// Raymarch-specific pipeline counters, upstream to downstream: what the
 297     /// payloads carry, whether it reached the atlas pool, and whether it
 298     /// reached the GPU-visible draw table. Reading resident/drawn together
 299     /// pinpoints which stage lost a chunk -- something otherwise invisible
 300     /// because every stage before the screen looks the same from outside.
 301     /// Only meaningful when `artifact_needs.needs_node_arena()` is true, and
 302     /// only ever shown there (see [`Self::diagnostic_text`]).
 303     pub fn raymarch_debug_text(&self) -> String {
 304         let mut out = String::with_capacity(256);
 305         // A resident chunk that never reaches `draws` never appears on
 306         // screen, whatever generation and streaming already did for it --
 307         // `draws` requires both a store entry *and* a pool slot
 308         // (`AtlasPool::node_offset_of`). When `resident` climbs but `drawn`
 309         // stalls, the fault is downstream of streaming: the atlas pool is
 310         // either full or the upload it needed failed. That split is
 311         // otherwise invisible -- the two counts read identically from
 312         // outside the engine.
 313         let _ = writeln!(
 314             out,
 315             "drawn {} of {} resident | atlas pool {}/{} slot(s) occupied",
 316             self.draws.len(),
 317             self.store.len(),
 318             self.pool.occupied_slots(),
 319             self.pool.slot_count(),
 320         );
 321         // Splits the brick pipeline itself: this counts what the *payloads*
 322         // actually carry, straight from `ChunkStore`, upstream of the pool,
 323         // the atlas texture, and the shader entirely. If a brick node reads
 324         // as air in the render, this line says whether there was ever
 325         // anything there to read -- zero brick words with brick nodes
 326         // present is a pooling/upload fault; brick words present but still
 327         // rendering as air is a GPU sampling fault, and the console's
 328         // "brick arena upload rejected"/"brick arena WxH..." lines (driver
 329         // logging, not this panel) say which.
 330         let (brick_nodes, brick_words) =
 331             self.store
 332                 .iter_ordered()
 333                 .fold((0usize, 0usize), |(nodes, words), chunk| {
 334                     let kind_brick = chunk
 335                         .payload
 336                         .nodes
 337                         .chunks_exact(4)
 338                         .filter(|node| node[0] == 2)
 339                         .count();
 340                     (nodes + kind_brick, words + chunk.payload.brick_voxels.len())
 341                 });
 342         let _ = writeln!(
 343             out,
 344             "brick nodes {brick_nodes} | brick arena {brick_words} word(s) in payloads",
 345         );
 346         let _ = writeln!(out, "atlas node texels {}", self.atlas_nodes);
 347         out
 348     }

   1 //! Prepare the immutable fixture list consumed by a render frame.
   2 //!
   3 //! Chunk payloads overlap on purpose, so the same ceiling panel can arrive
   4 //! from several neighboring halos. Selection belongs here, before any GPU
   5 //! driver: all renderers must see the same deduplicated physical scene.
   6 
   7 use std::collections::HashMap;
   8 
   9 use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
  10 
  11 /// Collects every finite, enabled fixture and orders it by conservative
  12 /// contribution at `camera_position`.
  13 ///
  14 /// The ordering is not a budget: no fixture is discarded. It keeps the hero
  15 /// shadow choice stable and makes output independent of hash-map/chunk arrival
  16 /// order. Projected emitter area and authored intensity raise importance while
  17 /// squared distance lowers it.
  18 pub fn select_scene_lights<'a>(
  19     lights: impl Iterator<Item = &'a LightSource>,
  20     camera_position: [f32; 3],
  21 ) -> Vec<LightSource> {
  22     let mut unique = HashMap::<u64, LightSource>::new();
  23     for light in lights.copied() {
  24         if light.enabled && valid(&light) {
  25             unique.entry(light.id).or_insert(light);
  26         }
  27     }
  28 
  29     let mut ranked: Vec<(LightSource, f32)> = unique
  30         .into_values()
  31         .map(|light| {
  32             let delta = [
  33                 light.position[0] - camera_position[0],
  34                 light.position[1] - camera_position[1],
  35                 light.position[2] - camera_position[2],
  36             ];
  37             let distance_squared = delta.into_iter().map(|v| v * v).sum::<f32>();
  38             let area = (4.0 * light.half_size[0] * light.half_size[1]).max(0.01);
  39             let importance = light.intensity * area / (distance_squared + area);
  40             (light, importance)
  41         })
  42         .collect();
  43     ranked.sort_by(|(a, a_score), (b, b_score)| {
  44         b_score.total_cmp(a_score).then_with(|| a.id.cmp(&b.id))
  45     });
  46 
  47     ranked.into_iter().map(|(light, _)| light).collect()
  48 }
  49 
  50 fn valid(light: &LightSource) -> bool {
  51     light.position.into_iter().all(f32::is_finite)
  52         && light.color.into_iter().all(f32::is_finite)
  53         && light
  54             .half_size
  55             .into_iter()
  56             .all(|v| v.is_finite() && v >= 0.0)
  57         && light.radius.is_finite()
  58         && light.radius > 0.0
  59         && light.intensity.is_finite()
  60         && light.intensity > 0.0
  61 }

   1 //! Dropped-flare lifecycle and per-frame light selection.
   2 //!
   3 //! Flares are transient world objects rather than chunk data. This module
   4 //! owns their age, insertion order, collision-aware placement, retirement,
   5 //! and clockless renderer payload. The engine only supplies player/world
   6 //! context and the shared simulation time.
   7 
   8 use crate::application::collision::{Aabb, CollisionWorld};
   9 use crate::application::ports::{DynamicLight, MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS};
  10 
  11 /// Flare lifetime in seconds; intensity fades during the final tenth.
  12 const FLARE_LIFETIME_S: f32 = 90.0;
  13 /// Global active-flare cap. A new drop retires the oldest flare at the cap.
  14 const FLARE_CAP: usize = 12;
  15 /// Flares farther than this horizontal distance do not light the frame.
  16 const FLARE_CULL_DISTANCE: f32 = 40.0;
  17 /// Local warm glow radius of one flare.
  18 const FLARE_LIGHT_RADIUS: f32 = 9.0;
  19 /// Horizontal distance from the player at which a drop is attempted.
  20 const FLARE_DROP_DISTANCE: f32 = 0.9;
  21 /// Flare flame height above the floor slab.
  22 const FLARE_HEIGHT: f32 = 0.3;
  23 /// Height above the flame used to detect geometry remapped over a flare.
  24 const BURIED_PROBE_HEIGHT: f32 = 0.2;
  25 
  26 /// One dropped flare: pure runtime world-space state. Never serialized into
  27 /// chunks, never part of the reality snapshot, and preserved untouched by
  28 /// ordinary chunk streaming.
  29 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
  30 pub struct Flare {
  31     pub position: [f32; 3],
  32     pub age_seconds: f32,
  33     /// Monotonic drop order; doubles as the deterministic flicker phase.
  34     pub sequence: u64,
  35 }
  36 
  37 impl Flare {
  38     pub fn remaining_seconds(&self) -> f32 {
  39         (FLARE_LIFETIME_S - self.age_seconds).max(0.0)
  40     }
  41 }
  42 
  43 /// Fixed renderer payload and the meaningful prefix length.
  44 pub(crate) struct FlareLightSet {
  45     pub(crate) lights: [DynamicLight; MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS],
  46     pub(crate) count: u8,
  47 }
  48 
  49 /// Active flare collection, kept oldest first.
  50 #[derive(Debug, Default)]
  51 pub(crate) struct FlareField {
  52     active: Vec<Flare>,
  53     sequence: u64,
  54 }
  55 
  56 impl FlareField {
  57     /// Advances every flare and retires those whose lifetime has elapsed.
  58     pub(crate) fn advance(&mut self, dt_seconds: f32) {
  59         for flare in &mut self.active {
  60             flare.age_seconds += dt_seconds;
  61         }
  62         self.active
  63             .retain(|flare| flare.age_seconds < FLARE_LIFETIME_S);
  64     }
  65 
  66     /// Drops a flare slightly ahead of the player unless that placement
  67     /// would collide, in which case the known-valid player position wins.
  68     pub(crate) fn drop_from(
  69         &mut self,
  70         eye: [f32; 3],
  71         forward: [f32; 3],
  72         collision: &CollisionWorld,
  73     ) {
  74         let ahead = [
  75             eye[0] + forward[0] * FLARE_DROP_DISTANCE,
  76             eye[1],
  77             eye[2] + forward[2] * FLARE_DROP_DISTANCE,
  78         ];
  79         let spot = if collision.collides(ahead) {
  80             eye
  81         } else {
  82             ahead
  83         };
  84 
  85         if self.active.len() >= FLARE_CAP {
  86             self.active.remove(0);
  87         }
  88         self.sequence += 1;
  89         self.active.push(Flare {
  90             position: [spot[0], FLARE_HEIGHT, spot[2]],
  91             age_seconds: 0.0,
  92             sequence: self.sequence,
  93         });
  94     }
  95 
  96     /// Extinguishes flares covered by newly installed collision geometry.
  97     /// The inclusive point test intentionally matches the former engine
  98     /// policy at box faces.
  99     pub(crate) fn extinguish_buried(&mut self, boxes: &[Aabb]) {
 100         self.active.retain(|flare| {
 101             let probe = [
 102                 flare.position[0],
 103                 flare.position[1] + BURIED_PROBE_HEIGHT,
 104                 flare.position[2],
 105             ];
 106             !boxes.iter().any(|bounds| point_in_aabb(probe, bounds))
 107         });
 108     }
 109 
 110     /// Builds the nearest-light payload once. Selection, count, fade, and
 111     /// deterministic flicker therefore cannot disagree within a frame.
 112     pub(crate) fn lights(&self, camera: [f32; 3], time_seconds: f32) -> FlareLightSet {
 113         let nearest = self.nearest(camera);
 114         let count = nearest.len() as u8;
 115         let mut lights = [DynamicLight::default(); MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS];
 116 
 117         for (slot, flare) in nearest.into_iter().enumerate() {
 118             let fade = (flare.remaining_seconds() / (FLARE_LIFETIME_S * 0.1)).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 119             let phase = time_seconds * 13.0 + flare.sequence as f32 * 1.7;
 120             let flicker = 0.85 + 0.15 * phase.sin() * (phase * 0.37).cos();
 121             lights[slot] = DynamicLight {
 122                 position: flare.position,
 123                 color: [1.0, 0.45, 0.18],
 124                 radius: FLARE_LIGHT_RADIUS,
 125                 intensity: 1.6 * fade * flicker,
 126             };
 127         }
 128 
 129         FlareLightSet { lights, count }
 130     }
 131 
 132     /// Removes active flares without rewinding their monotonic identity.
 133     pub(crate) fn clear(&mut self) {
 134         self.active.clear();
 135     }
 136 
 137     pub(crate) fn active(&self) -> &[Flare] {
 138         &self.active
 139     }
 140 
 141     pub(crate) fn len(&self) -> usize {
 142         self.active.len()
 143     }
 144 
 145     fn nearest(&self, camera: [f32; 3]) -> Vec<&Flare> {
 146         let cull_distance_squared = FLARE_CULL_DISTANCE * FLARE_CULL_DISTANCE;
 147         let distance_squared = |flare: &Flare| {
 148             let dx = flare.position[0] - camera[0];
 149             let dz = flare.position[2] - camera[2];
 150             dx * dx + dz * dz
 151         };
 152         let mut nearest: Vec<_> = self
 153             .active
 154             .iter()
 155             .filter(|flare| distance_squared(flare) < cull_distance_squared)
 156             .collect();
 157         nearest.sort_by(|a, b| {
 158             distance_squared(a)
 159                 .total_cmp(&distance_squared(b))
 160                 .then_with(|| a.sequence.cmp(&b.sequence))
 161         });
 162         nearest.truncate(MAX_DYNAMIC_LIGHTS);
 163         nearest
 164     }
 165 }
 166 
 167 fn point_in_aabb(point: [f32; 3], bounds: &Aabb) -> bool {
 168     point[0] >= bounds.min[0]
 169         && point[0] <= bounds.max[0]
 170         && point[1] >= bounds.min[1]
 171         && point[1] <= bounds.max[1]
 172         && point[2] >= bounds.min[2]
 173         && point[2] <= bounds.max[2]
 174 }
