   1 //! Axis-aligned collision primitives and the sliding-collision world.
   2 //!
   3 //! Collision geometry is *derived from the SVO itself* (solid leaf nodes of
   4 //! type WALL / RED_WALL become world-space boxes), so the physical world and
   5 //! the rendered world can never drift apart.
   6 
   7 use std::collections::HashMap;
   8 
   9 /// Axis-aligned bounding box in world space.
  10 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
  11 pub struct Aabb {
  12     pub min: [f32; 3],
  13     pub max: [f32; 3],
  14 }
  15 
  16 impl Aabb {
  17     pub fn new(min: [f32; 3], max: [f32; 3]) -> Self {
  18         Self { min, max }
  19     }
  20 
  21     pub fn intersects(&self, other: &Aabb) -> bool {
  22         self.max[0] > other.min[0]
  23             && self.min[0] < other.max[0]
  24             && self.max[1] > other.min[1]
  25             && self.min[1] < other.max[1]
  26             && self.max[2] > other.min[2]
  27             && self.min[2] < other.max[2]
  28     }
  29 }
  30 
  31 /// Player capsule approximated as an AABB, matching the original client:
  32 /// radius 0.35 around the eye, extending 1.65 below and 0.1 above eye level.
  33 pub const PLAYER_RADIUS: f32 = 0.35;
  34 pub const PLAYER_EYE_TO_FEET: f32 = 1.65;
  35 pub const PLAYER_EYE_TO_HEAD: f32 = 0.1;
  36 
  37 /// Builds the player's AABB from an eye-level position.
  38 pub fn player_aabb(eye_pos: [f32; 3]) -> Aabb {
  39     Aabb::new(
  40         [
  41             eye_pos[0] - PLAYER_RADIUS,
  42             eye_pos[1] - PLAYER_EYE_TO_FEET,
  43             eye_pos[2] - PLAYER_RADIUS,
  44         ],
  45         [
  46             eye_pos[0] + PLAYER_RADIUS,
  47             eye_pos[1] + PLAYER_EYE_TO_HEAD,
  48             eye_pos[2] + PLAYER_RADIUS,
  49         ],
  50     )
  51 }
  52 
  53 type SpatialCell = (i64, i64);
  54 
  55 const SPATIAL_CELL_SIZE: f32 = 4.0;
  56 const MAX_CELLS_PER_BOX: usize = 256;
  57 
  58 /// The set of solid boxes the player can collide with.
  59 ///
  60 /// Boxes remain canonical in insertion order for diagnostics. Two derived
  61 /// X/Z indexes serve the hot queries: occupied cells for exact collision and
  62 /// center cells for thermal enclosure. Rebuilding is event-driven when the
  63 /// resident chunk set changes; steady-state frames only query the hashes.
  64 #[derive(Debug)]
  65 pub struct CollisionWorld {
  66     boxes: Vec<Aabb>,
  67     occupied_cells: HashMap<SpatialCell, Vec<usize>>,
  68     center_cells: HashMap<SpatialCell, Vec<usize>>,
  69     fallback: Vec<usize>,
  70 }
  71 
  72 impl CollisionWorld {
  73     pub fn new() -> Self {
  74         Self {
  75             boxes: Vec::new(),
  76             occupied_cells: HashMap::new(),
  77             center_cells: HashMap::new(),
  78             fallback: Vec::new(),
  79         }
  80     }
  81 
  82     pub fn rebuild<'a, I: IntoIterator<Item = &'a Aabb>>(&mut self, boxes: I) {
  83         self.boxes.clear();
  84         self.boxes.extend(boxes.into_iter().copied());
  85         self.occupied_cells.clear();
  86         self.center_cells.clear();
  87         self.fallback.clear();
  88 
  89         for (index, aabb) in self.boxes.iter().enumerate() {
  90             let Some((min_cell, max_cell)) = cells_for_bounds(aabb.min, aabb.max) else {
  91                 self.fallback.push(index);
  92                 continue;
  93             };
  94             let width = cell_count(min_cell.0, max_cell.0).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
  95             let depth = cell_count(min_cell.1, max_cell.1).unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
  96             if width.saturating_mul(depth) > MAX_CELLS_PER_BOX {
  97                 self.fallback.push(index);
  98                 continue;
  99             }
 100 
 101             for cell_z in min_cell.1..=max_cell.1 {
 102                 for cell_x in min_cell.0..=max_cell.0 {
 103                     self.occupied_cells
 104                         .entry((cell_x, cell_z))
 105                         .or_default()
 106                         .push(index);
 107                 }
 108             }
 109 
 110             let center_x = (aabb.min[0] + aabb.max[0]) * 0.5;
 111             let center_z = (aabb.min[2] + aabb.max[2]) * 0.5;
 112             self.center_cells
 113                 .entry(spatial_cell(center_x, center_z))
 114                 .or_default()
 115                 .push(index);
 116         }
 117     }
 118 
 119     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
 120         self.boxes.len()
 121     }
 122 
 123     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 124         self.boxes.is_empty()
 125     }
 126 
 127     pub fn boxes(&self) -> &[Aabb] {
 128         &self.boxes
 129     }
 130 
 131     /// True if a player standing at `eye_pos` overlaps any solid box.
 132     pub fn collides(&self, eye_pos: [f32; 3]) -> bool {
 133         self.intersects(&player_aabb(eye_pos))
 134     }
 135 
 136     /// Counts box centers within an X/Z radius without scanning distant
 137     /// chunks. This preserves the thermal model's exact center-distance rule.
 138     pub fn count_centers_within_xz(&self, point: [f32; 3], radius: f32) -> usize {
 139         if !point[0].is_finite() || !point[2].is_finite() || !radius.is_finite() || radius < 0.0 {
 140             return 0;
 141         }
 142         let min = spatial_cell(point[0] - radius, point[2] - radius);
 143         let max = spatial_cell(point[0] + radius, point[2] + radius);
 144         let radius_squared = radius * radius;
 145         let mut count = 0;
 146         for cell_z in min.1..=max.1 {
 147             for cell_x in min.0..=max.0 {
 148                 let Some(indices) = self.center_cells.get(&(cell_x, cell_z)) else {
 149                     continue;
 150                 };
 151                 count += indices
 152                     .iter()
 153                     .filter(|&&index| center_within_xz(self.boxes[index], point, radius_squared))
 154                     .count();
 155             }
 156         }
 157         count
 158             + self
 159                 .fallback
 160                 .iter()
 161                 .filter(|&&index| center_within_xz(self.boxes[index], point, radius_squared))
 162                 .count()
 163     }
 164 
 165     fn intersects(&self, query: &Aabb) -> bool {
 166         let indexed_hit = cells_for_bounds(query.min, query.max).is_some_and(|(min, max)| {
 167             (min.1..=max.1).any(|cell_z| {
 168                 (min.0..=max.0).any(|cell_x| {
 169                     self.occupied_cells
 170                         .get(&(cell_x, cell_z))
 171                         .is_some_and(|indices| {
 172                             indices
 173                                 .iter()
 174                                 .any(|&index| query.intersects(&self.boxes[index]))
 175                         })
 176                 })
 177             })
 178         });
 179         indexed_hit
 180             || self
 181                 .fallback
 182                 .iter()
 183                 .any(|&index| query.intersects(&self.boxes[index]))
 184     }
 185 }
 186 
 187 impl Default for CollisionWorld {
 188     fn default() -> Self {
 189         Self::new()
 190     }
 191 }
 192 
 193 fn spatial_cell(x: f32, z: f32) -> SpatialCell {
 194     (
 195         (x / SPATIAL_CELL_SIZE).floor() as i64,
 196         (z / SPATIAL_CELL_SIZE).floor() as i64,
 197     )
 198 }
 199 
 200 fn cells_for_bounds(min: [f32; 3], max: [f32; 3]) -> Option<(SpatialCell, SpatialCell)> {
 201     if ![min[0], min[2], max[0], max[2]]
 202         .into_iter()
 203         .all(f32::is_finite)
 204         || max[0] < min[0]
 205         || max[2] < min[2]
 206     {
 207         return None;
 208     }
 209     Some((spatial_cell(min[0], min[2]), spatial_cell(max[0], max[2])))
 210 }
 211 
 212 fn cell_count(first: i64, last: i64) -> Option<usize> {
 213     last.checked_sub(first)
 214         .and_then(|distance| distance.checked_add(1))
 215         .and_then(|count| usize::try_from(count).ok())
 216 }
 217 
 218 fn center_within_xz(aabb: Aabb, point: [f32; 3], radius_squared: f32) -> bool {
 219     let center_x = (aabb.min[0] + aabb.max[0]) * 0.5;
 220     let center_z = (aabb.min[2] + aabb.max[2]) * 0.5;
 221     let dx = center_x - point[0];
 222     let dz = center_z - point[2];
 223     dx * dx + dz * dz <= radius_squared
 224 }

 230     #[test]
 231     fn aabb_intersection_is_exclusive_on_touching_faces() {
 232         let a = Aabb::new([0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]);

collision.rs analysis:
- `rebuild` (82-117): O(B × cells_per_box) — event-driven, only when the resident chunk set changes.
- `collides` (132-134) → `intersects` (165-184): spatial hash lookup, O(cells in query × boxes per cell). Worst case fallback O(F_fallback). Good.
- `count_centers_within_xz` (138-163): O(cells × boxes per cell). Good.

Collision queries are fine. The world.rebuild is the expensive one but event-driven.

Now thermal.rs, perf_governor.rs, quality.rs, render_settings.rs, atlas.rs.
   1 //! Ambient temperature felt by the player, derived from the lit scene.
   2 //!
   3 //! The Backrooms' heat *is* its lighting: fluorescent tubes bake the air,
   4 //! so standing under working fixtures warms the wanderer while darkness
   5 //! (blackouts, dead bays, Level 1's failing grid) lets the air fall back to
   6 //! the level's unlit baseline. Enclosure matters too — a lit closet cooks
   7 //! faster than a lit atrium — approximated here by how much collision mass
   8 //! crowds the player. Everything is pure math over the same deduplicated,
   9 //! flicker-scaled fixture list every renderer sees: a sputtering tube that
  10 //! is dark this instant radiates nothing this instant.
  11 
  12 use crate::application::ports::LightSource;
  13 
  14 /// Unlit-air baseline per level, °C. Level 0's dark corners still hold the
  15 /// building's stale warmth; Level 1's raw concrete is genuinely cold.
  16 pub fn dark_baseline_c(level: u32) -> f32 {
  17     match level {
  18         0 => 24.0,
  19         1 => 13.0,
  20         _ => 21.0,
  21     }
  22 }
  23 
  24 /// Maximum heating the fixture field can add above the baseline, °C.
  25 const MAX_LIGHT_HEAT_C: f32 = 13.0;
  26 /// Scales summed fixture irradiance into °C before the cap.
  27 const HEAT_PER_IRRADIANCE: f32 = 9.0;
  28 /// Enclosure raises effective heating by up to this factor.
  29 const ENCLOSURE_GAIN: f32 = 0.6;
  30 /// Radius probed for enclosing collision mass.
  31 pub const ENCLOSURE_RADIUS: f32 = 6.0;
  32 /// Collision-box count that reads as "fully enclosed".
  33 const ENCLOSURE_SATURATION: f32 = 36.0;
  34 
  35 /// The instantaneous ambient temperature at the player position.
  36 ///
  37 /// `lights` must already carry this frame's flicker gain so failing tubes
  38 /// heat exactly as much as they shine. The result is *unsmoothed*; the
  39 /// engine applies thermal inertia so doorways don't flip the rate per frame.
  40 pub fn ambient_celsius(
  41     level: u32,
  42     player: [f32; 3],
  43     lights: &[LightSource],
  44     enclosing_collision_boxes: usize,
  45 ) -> f32 {
  46     let mut irradiance = 0.0f32;
  47     for light in lights {
  48         let dx = light.position[0] - player[0];
  49         let dy = light.position[1] - player[1];
  50         let dz = light.position[2] - player[2];
  51         let distance = (dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz).sqrt();
  52         let range = light.radius.max(0.01);
  53         let falloff = (1.0 - distance / range).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  54         irradiance += light.intensity * falloff * falloff;
  55     }
  56 
  57     let enclosure = (enclosing_collision_boxes as f32 / ENCLOSURE_SATURATION).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
  58 
  59     let heat = (irradiance * HEAT_PER_IRRADIANCE).min(MAX_LIGHT_HEAT_C)
  60         * (1.0 + ENCLOSURE_GAIN * enclosure);
  61     dark_baseline_c(level) + heat.min(MAX_LIGHT_HEAT_C * (1.0 + ENCLOSURE_GAIN))
  62 }
  63 
  64 #[cfg(test)]
  65 mod tests {
  66     use super::*;
  67     use crate::application::collision::Aabb;
  68     use crate::application::ports::LightKind;

  70     fn fixture(position: [f32; 3], intensity: f32) -> LightSource {
  71         LightSource {
  72             id: 1,
  73             position,
  74             half_size: [0.5, 0.5],
  75             color: [1.0, 1.0, 1.0],
  76             radius: 16.0,
  77             intensity,
  78             kind: LightKind::CeilingPanel,
  79             flicker_mode: 0,
  80             enabled: true,
  81         }
  82     }
  83 
  84     fn walls_around(count: usize) -> Vec<Aabb> {
  85         (0..count)
  86             .map(|i| {
  87                 let angle = i as f32;
  88                 Aabb::new(
  89                     [angle.cos() * 2.0, 0.0, angle.sin() * 2.0],
  90                     [angle.cos() * 2.0 + 0.4, 3.0, angle.sin() * 2.0 + 0.4],
  91                 )
  92             })
  93             .collect()
  94     }
  95 
  96     fn nearby_wall_count(player: [f32; 3], walls: &[Aabb]) -> usize {
  97         walls
  98             .iter()
  99             .filter(|wall| {
 100                 let center_x = (wall.min[0] + wall.max[0]) * 0.5;
 101                 let center_z = (wall.min[2] + wall.max[2]) * 0.5;
 102                 let dx = center_x - player[0];
 103                 let dz = center_z - player[2];
 104                 dx * dx + dz * dz <= ENCLOSURE_RADIUS * ENCLOSURE_RADIUS
 105             })
 106             .count()
 107     }

   1 //! Adaptive internal-resolution policy, independent of renderer and browser.
   2 
   3 /// Adaptive internal-resolution governor. Low-spec machines get fewer rays
   4 /// per frame by rendering at a reduced backing-store resolution; the driver
   5 /// applies the scale to the canvas. Hysteresis + cooldown prevent flapping.
   6 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
   7 pub struct PerfGovernor {
   8     ema_frame_ms: f32,
   9     scale: f32,
  10     cooldown_frames: u32,
  11     /// Frames since the last scale-up attempt (saturating).
  12     frames_since_raise: u32,
  13     /// While positive, scale-ups are locked out because a recent raise
  14     /// immediately overloaded the GPU and had to be reverted (anti-flap).
  15     raise_lockout_frames: u32,
  16 }
  17 
  18 impl PerfGovernor {
  19     const SCALES: [f32; 4] = [0.5, 0.65, 0.8, 1.0];
  20     /// A drop this soon after a raise counts as a failed raise.
  21     const RAISE_PROBE_FRAMES: u32 = 600;
  22     /// How long a failed raise blocks further raise attempts (~1 min).
  23     const RAISE_LOCKOUT_FRAMES: u32 = 3600;
  24 
  25     pub fn new() -> Self {
  26         Self {
  27             ema_frame_ms: 16.0,
  28             scale: 0.8,
  29             cooldown_frames: 0,
  30             frames_since_raise: u32::MAX,
  31             raise_lockout_frames: 0,
  32         }
  33     }
  34 
  35     pub fn scale(&self) -> f32 {
  36         self.scale
  37     }
  38 
  39     pub fn update(&mut self, frame_ms: f32) {
  40         self.ema_frame_ms = self.ema_frame_ms * 0.95 + frame_ms.clamp(0.0, 100.0) * 0.05;
  41         self.frames_since_raise = self.frames_since_raise.saturating_add(1);
  42         self.raise_lockout_frames = self.raise_lockout_frames.saturating_sub(1);
  43         if self.cooldown_frames > 0 {
  44             self.cooldown_frames -= 1;
  45             return;
  46         }
  47         let idx = Self::SCALES
  48             .iter()
  49             .position(|&s| s == self.scale)
  50             .unwrap_or(2);
  51         if self.ema_frame_ms > 33.0 && idx > 0 {
  52             // Sustained under ~30 fps: drop one resolution step. If this
  53             // happens right after a raise, the raise failed — lock raises
  54             // out for a while so the scale doesn't oscillate.
  55             if self.frames_since_raise < Self::RAISE_PROBE_FRAMES {
  56                 self.raise_lockout_frames = Self::RAISE_LOCKOUT_FRAMES;
  57             }
  58             self.scale = Self::SCALES[idx - 1];
  59             self.cooldown_frames = 120;
  60         } else if self.ema_frame_ms < 17.5
  61             && idx + 1 < Self::SCALES.len()
  62             && self.raise_lockout_frames == 0
  63         {
  64             // Holding 60Hz vsync (rAF EMA floors at ~16.7 ms, so a lower
  65             // threshold would never fire): probe one resolution step up.
  66             self.scale = Self::SCALES[idx + 1];
  67             self.cooldown_frames = 240;
  68             self.frames_since_raise = 0;
  69         }
  70     }
  71 }
  72 
  73 #[cfg(test)]
  74 mod tests {
  75     use super::*;
  76 
  77     #[test]
  78     fn governor_drops_resolution_under_sustained_load() {
  79         let mut governor = PerfGovernor::new();
  80         for _ in 0..200 {
  81             governor.update(50.0); // 20 fps
  82         }
  83         assert!(governor.scale() < 0.8);
  84     }
  85 
  86     #[test]
  87     fn governor_raises_resolution_when_holding_60hz_vsync() {
  88         let mut governor = PerfGovernor::new();
  89         // rAF on a 60Hz display floors at ~16.7ms even with GPU headroom.
  90         for _ in 0..600 {
  91             governor.update(16.7);
  92         }
  93         assert_eq!(governor.scale(), 1.0, "must reach native res under vsync");
  94     }
  95 
  96     #[test]
  97     fn governor_locks_out_raises_after_a_failed_probe() {
  98         let mut governor = PerfGovernor::new();
  99         for _ in 0..300 {
 100             governor.update(16.7); // raises to 1.0 almost immediately
 101         }
 102         assert_eq!(governor.scale(), 1.0);
 103         for _ in 0..600 {
 104             governor.update(40.0); // raise fails: overloaded at 1.0
 105         }
 106         assert!(governor.scale() < 1.0);
 107         let settled = governor.scale();
 108         for _ in 0..600 {
 109             governor.update(16.7); // healthy again, but inside the lockout
 110         }
 111         assert_eq!(governor.scale(), settled, "raise must stay locked out");
 112     }
 113 }

perf_governor.rs is fine (O(1) per frame, small).

Now atlas.rs, quality.rs, render_settings.rs.
   1 //! Pooled SVO node atlas: stable, fixed-size chunk slots inside one shared
   2 //! four-word-per-node storage stream.
   3 //!
   4 //! This is the raymarcher's analog of "vertex pooling" in mesh-based voxel
   5 //! engines. The naive approach (concatenate every resident chunk's node
   6 //! array and re-upload the whole GPU buffer on any change) makes every chunk
   7 //! load cost O(world) in CPU copies and transfer bandwidth. The pool instead
   8 //! gives each chunk a fixed row-aligned slot: loading a chunk rebases and
   9 //! uploads *only that slot's rows*, and evicting a chunk is free (its slot is
  10 //! simply reused later; stale nodes are never referenced by the draw table).
  11 //!
  12 //! Every chunk's node array is padded to whole 1024-node rows by the
  13 //! core `OctreeGpuSerializer`, so slots stay row-aligned by construction.
  14 //!
  15 //! `slots` remains the authority for iteration order (`full_texels`,
  16 //! `full_brick_words` walk it slot-by-slot to build one contiguous upload),
  17 //! but `assign`/`release`/`*_offset_of` no longer scan it: `index` and
  18 //! `free` turn "which slot holds this key" and "which slot is free" from an
  19 //! O(n) scan into an O(1) lookup and a stack pop, the first step toward
  20 //! lifting `MAX_CHUNKS` from a hardcoded 25 to a size picked by an actual
  21 //! GPU/storage budget (out-of-core streaming, `VOXEL_RESEARCH_STEAL_LIST.txt`
  22 //! item 3). Raising the cap itself is a separate change: `application::
  23 //! engine`'s per-frame `draws` table and the WebGL2 shader's fixed
  24 //! `uChunkOrigins[25]`-style uniform arrays are their own ceiling on
  25 //! resident chunk count, independent of this pool's slot budget.
  26 
  27 use std::collections::HashMap;
  28 
  29 use crate::application::ports::ChunkPayload;
  30 use crate::application::streaming::ChunkKey;
  31 
  32 /// The raymarch pass's fixed per-frame chunk-table capacity.
  33 pub const MAX_CHUNKS: usize = 25;
  34 
  35 /// SVO nodes per atlas row. Must match the raymarch upload offset and the
  36 /// core serializer's row padding.
  37 pub const ROW_TEXELS: usize = 1024;
  38 
  39 /// One air-leaf texel (type flag 1, voxel type 0): what free space decodes to.
  40 const AIR_LEAF: [u32; 4] = [1, 0, 0, 0];
  41 
  42 /// Brick voxel words per slot row. The dense arena pools on the same slot
  43 /// index as the node arena, so one `assign` places a chunk in both.
  44 pub const BRICK_ROW_WORDS: usize = 1024;
  45 
  46 #[derive(Debug, Default)]
  47 pub struct AtlasPool {
  48     /// Rows per slot. Grows (forcing a relayout) when a chunk won't fit.
  49     slot_rows: usize,
  50     /// Rows per slot in the brick voxel arena, sized independently: a chunk
  51     /// that is mostly uniform has many nodes and few bricks, and vice versa.
  52     brick_slot_rows: usize,
  53     /// Slot occupancy; index is the slot number. `full_texels`/
  54     /// `full_brick_words` are the only readers left that need this instead
  55     /// of `index` -- they must walk every slot, occupied or not, to build
  56     /// one contiguous upload.
  57     slots: Vec<Option<ChunkKey>>,
  58     /// Reverse of `slots`, kept in sync by `assign`/`release`/relayout.
  59     index: HashMap<ChunkKey, usize>,
  60     /// Free slot indices, ascending-index-first like the scan `assign` used
  61     /// to do (`(0..len).rev()` so the smallest index is on top).
  62     free: Vec<usize>,
  63 }
  64 
  65 impl AtlasPool {
  66     pub fn new() -> Self {
  67         Self::default()
  68     }
  69 
  70     /// Nodes (texels) per slot.
  71     pub fn slot_nodes(&self) -> usize {
  72         self.slot_rows * ROW_TEXELS
  73     }
  74 
  75     /// Total rows in the pooled texture.
  76     pub fn total_rows(&self) -> usize {
  77         self.slot_rows * self.slots.len()
  78     }
  79 
  80     /// Total slots the pool currently holds, occupied or not -- the hard
  81     /// ceiling on chunks that can reach `draws` in one frame.
  82     pub fn slot_count(&self) -> usize {
  83         self.slots.len()
  84     }
  85 
  86     /// Occupied slots: chunks with both a store entry and a place in the
  87     /// pool. Below `slot_count`, this is exactly `draws.len()`'s ceiling.
  88     pub fn occupied_slots(&self) -> usize {
  89         self.index.len()
  90     }
  91 
  92     /// Ensures the pool holds at least `num_slots` slots of at least `rows`
  93     /// rows each. Returns `true` when the layout changed — every slot
  94     /// assignment is then dropped and the caller must reassign all resident
  95     /// chunks and re-upload the whole pool.
  96     pub fn ensure_layout(&mut self, num_slots: usize, rows: usize) -> bool {
  97         self.ensure_layout_with_bricks(num_slots, rows, 0)
  98     }
  99 
 100     /// As [`Self::ensure_layout`], additionally sizing the brick voxel
 101     /// arena. Either arena outgrowing its slot relayouts both, so the two
 102     /// stay addressable from one slot index.
 103     pub fn ensure_layout_with_bricks(
 104         &mut self,
 105         num_slots: usize,
 106         rows: usize,
 107         brick_rows: usize,
 108     ) -> bool {
 109         let changed = rows > self.slot_rows
 110             || brick_rows > self.brick_slot_rows
 111             || num_slots > self.slots.len();
 112         if changed {
 113             self.slot_rows = self.slot_rows.max(rows);
 114             self.brick_slot_rows = self.brick_slot_rows.max(brick_rows);
 115             let len = self.slots.len().max(num_slots);
 116             self.slots.clear();
 117             self.slots.resize(len, None);
 118             self.index.clear();
 119             self.free = (0..len).rev().collect();
 120         }
 121         changed
 122     }
 123 
 124     /// Brick voxel words per slot.
 125     pub fn brick_slot_words(&self) -> usize {
 126         self.brick_slot_rows * BRICK_ROW_WORDS
 127     }
 128 
 129     /// Word offset of `key`'s brick block within the pooled voxel arena.
 130     pub fn brick_offset_of(&self, key: ChunkKey) -> Option<usize> {
 131         self.index.get(&key).map(|&i| i * self.brick_slot_words())
 132     }
 133 
 134     /// Assigns (or finds) the slot for `key`. Returns `None` when the pool
 135     /// is full — the caller sized it for the streaming radius, so that is a
 136     /// logic error handled by falling back to a full relayout.
 137     pub fn assign(&mut self, key: ChunkKey) -> Option<usize> {
 138         if let Some(&i) = self.index.get(&key) {
 139             return Some(i);
 140         }
 141         let slot = self.free.pop()?;
 142         self.slots[slot] = Some(key);
 143         self.index.insert(key, slot);
 144         Some(slot)
 145     }
 146 
 147     pub fn release(&mut self, key: ChunkKey) {
 148         if let Some(slot) = self.index.remove(&key) {
 149             self.slots[slot] = None;
 150             self.free.push(slot);
 151         }
 152     }
 153 
 154     /// First texture row of a slot.
 155     pub fn slot_first_row(&self, slot: usize) -> usize {
 156         slot * self.slot_rows
 157     }
 158 
 159     /// First brick-arena row of a slot.
 160     pub fn brick_slot_first_row(&self, slot: usize) -> usize {
 161         slot * self.brick_slot_rows
 162     }
 163 
 164     /// Node offset of `key`'s slot within the pooled atlas.
 165     pub fn node_offset_of(&self, key: ChunkKey) -> Option<usize> {
 166         self.index.get(&key).map(|&i| i * self.slot_nodes())
 167     }
 168 
 169     /// Whether `payload` fits in the current slot size.
 170     pub fn fits(&self, payload: &ChunkPayload) -> bool {
 171         payload.nodes.len() / 4 <= self.slot_nodes()
 172     }
 173 
 174     /// The slot-sized texel block for one chunk: child pointers rebased to
 175     /// the slot's node offset, tail padded with air leaves.
 176     pub fn rebased_block(&self, slot: usize, payload: &ChunkPayload) -> Vec<u32> {
 177         let node_offset = (slot * self.slot_nodes()) as u32;
 178         let brick_offset = (slot * self.brick_slot_words()) as u32;
 179         let mut block = Vec::with_capacity(self.slot_nodes() * 4);
 180         block.extend_from_slice(&payload.nodes);
 181         // Internal nodes (type flag 0) store child indices local to the
 182         // chunk, and brick nodes (type flag 2) a word offset into the
 183         // chunk's own voxel arena; shift both into pool space. Leaf and
 184         // uniform nodes (flag 1) hold values, not pointers, and must not
 185         // be touched -- their payload word is a voxel type.
 186         for i in 0..(payload.nodes.len() / 4) {
 187             match block[i * 4] {
 188                 0 => block[i * 4 + 1] += node_offset,
 189                 2 => block[i * 4 + 1] += brick_offset,
 190                 _ => {}
 191             }
 192         }
 193         while block.len() < self.slot_nodes() * 4 {
 194             block.extend_from_slice(&AIR_LEAF);
 195         }
 196         block
 197     }
 198 
 199     /// The slot-sized brick word block for one chunk. Unlike `rebased_block`,
 200     /// voxel words carry no pointers, so there is nothing to rebase -- just
 201     /// pad the tail with zero, which decodes as air (see [`Self::
 202     /// full_brick_words`] for why nothing ever reads that padding).
 203     pub fn rebased_brick_block(&self, payload: &ChunkPayload) -> Vec<u32> {
 204         let mut block = payload.brick_voxels.clone();
 205         block.resize(self.brick_slot_words(), 0);
 206         block
 207     }
 208 
 209     /// The whole pool as one texel stream (initial upload, relayouts, and
 210     /// back ends without partial-update support). `lookup` resolves a slot's
 211     /// chunk key to its payload.
 212     pub fn full_texels<'a>(
 213         &self,
 214         lookup: impl Fn(ChunkKey) -> Option<&'a ChunkPayload>,
 215     ) -> Vec<u32> {
 216         let mut texels = Vec::with_capacity(self.total_rows() * ROW_TEXELS * 4);
 217         for (slot, occupant) in self.slots.iter().enumerate() {
 218             match occupant.and_then(&lookup) {
 219                 Some(payload) => texels.extend_from_slice(&self.rebased_block(slot, payload)),
 220                 None => {
 221                     for _ in 0..self.slot_nodes() {
 222                         texels.extend_from_slice(&AIR_LEAF);
 223                     }
 224                 }
 225             }
 226         }
 227         texels
 228     }
 229 
 230     /// The whole brick voxel arena as one word stream, laid out on the same
 231     /// slots as [`Self::full_texels`]. Unoccupied slots and the tail of each
 232     /// occupied one are zero, which decodes as air -- but nothing ever reads
 233     /// there, because a voxel is only reachable through a word offset some
 234     /// brick node handed out.
 235     pub fn full_brick_words<'a>(
 236         &self,
 237         lookup: impl Fn(ChunkKey) -> Option<&'a ChunkPayload>,
 238     ) -> Vec<u32> {
 239         let stride = self.brick_slot_words();
 240         let mut words = vec![0u32; stride * self.slots.len()];
 241         if stride == 0 {
 242             return words;
 243         }
 244         for (slot, occupant) in self.slots.iter().enumerate() {
 245             if let Some(payload) = occupant.and_then(&lookup) {
 246                 let base = slot * stride;
 247                 words[base..base + payload.brick_voxels.len()]
 248                     .copy_from_slice(&payload.brick_voxels);
 249             }
 250         }
 251         words
 252     }
 253 }
 254 
 255 /// Rows needed to hold a payload's node array.
 256 pub fn payload_rows(payload: &ChunkPayload) -> usize {
 257     (payload.nodes.len() / 4).div_ceil(ROW_TEXELS)
 258 }
 259 
 260 /// Rows needed to hold a payload's brick voxel arena.
 261 pub fn payload_brick_rows(payload: &ChunkPayload) -> usize {
 262     payload.brick_voxels.len().div_ceil(BRICK_ROW_WORDS)
 263 }

 289     fn slots_are_stable_across_unrelated_evictions() {
 290         let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
 291         pool.ensure_layout(4, 2);
 292         let (a, b, c) = (
 293             chunk_key(0.0, 0.0),

 296         );
 297         let slot_a = pool.assign(a).unwrap();
 298         let slot_b = pool.assign(b).unwrap();
 299         pool.release(a);
 300         let slot_c = pool.assign(c).unwrap();
 301         // b never moved; c reused a's freed slot.
 302         assert_eq!(pool.node_offset_of(b), Some(slot_b * pool.slot_nodes()));

 382     /// Interleaves assign/release across every slot several times over,
 383     /// checking `index` and `slots` never disagree -- the failure mode an
 384     /// O(1) reverse-index refactor risks that a linear scan structurally
 385     /// cannot: a stale `index` entry pointing at a slot `slots` disagrees
 386     /// with, or a freed slot handed out twice.
 387     #[test]
 388     fn index_and_slots_stay_consistent_under_churn() {
 389         let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
 390         pool.ensure_layout(5, 1);
 391         let keys: Vec<ChunkKey> = (0..12)
 392             .map(|i| chunk_key(i as f32 * 10.0, 0.0))
 393             .collect();
 394         let mut resident: Vec<ChunkKey> = Vec::new();
 395 
 396         for (round, &key) in keys.iter().enumerate() {
 397             if let Some(slot) = pool.assign(key) {
 398                 assert_eq!(pool.node_offset_of(key), Some(slot * pool.slot_nodes()));
 399                 resident.push(key);
 400             }
 401             if round % 3 == 2 {
 402                 if let Some(evict) = resident.pop() {
 403                     pool.release(evict);
 404                     assert_eq!(pool.node_offset_of(evict), None);
 405                 }
 406             }
 407             // Every still-resident key must resolve to a distinct slot.
 408             let mut offsets: Vec<usize> = resident
 409                 .iter()
 410                 .filter_map(|&k| pool.node_offset_of(k))
 411                 .collect();
 412             offsets.sort_unstable();
 413             offsets.dedup();
 414             assert_eq!(
 415                 offsets.len(),
 416                 resident.iter().filter(|&&k| pool.node_offset_of(k).is_some()).count(),
 417                 "no two resident keys share a slot"
 418             );
 419         }
 420     }
 421 
 422     #[test]
 423     fn full_texels_covers_every_slot() {
 424         let mut pool = AtlasPool::new();
 425         pool.ensure_layout(3, 1);
 426         let key = chunk_key(0.0, 0.0);
 427         let slot = pool.assign(key).unwrap();
 428         let p = payload(0, 4);
 429         let texels = pool.full_texels(|k| (k == key).then_some(&p));
 430         assert_eq!(texels.len(), 3 * pool.slot_nodes() * 4);
 431         // Unassigned slots are air.
 432         let other_slot = (slot + 1) % 3;
 433         let base = other_slot * pool.slot_nodes() * 4;
 434         assert_eq!(&texels[base..base + 4], &AIR_LEAF);
 435     }

   1 //! One quality decision shared by world generation and renderer profiles.
   2 //!
   3 //! The URL adapter parses `?spec=` into this application-owned value once.
   4 //! Generation and presentation then derive their independent concrete
   5 //! settings from the same decision, preventing case or fallback drift.
   6 
   7 use std::{error::Error, fmt, str::FromStr};
   8 
   9 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Default)]
  10 pub enum QualityProfile {
  11     /// Standard workloads intended for integrated and mobile-class GPUs.
  12     #[default]
  13     Low,
  14     /// Finer generation and larger rendering workloads for high-end systems.
  15     High,
  16 }
  17 
  18 impl QualityProfile {
  19     pub const ALL: [Self; 2] = [Self::Low, Self::High];
  20 
  21     /// Parses the stable `low`/`high` vocabulary case-insensitively.
  22     pub fn parse(value: &str) -> Option<Self> {
  23         let value = value.trim();
  24         Self::ALL
  25             .into_iter()
  26             .find(|quality| value.eq_ignore_ascii_case(quality.query_value()))
  27     }
  28 
  29     pub const fn query_value(self) -> &'static str {
  30         match self {
  31             Self::Low => "low",
  32             Self::High => "high",
  33         }
  34     }
  35 
  36     pub const fn label(self) -> &'static str {
  37         match self {
  38             Self::Low => "Standard",
  39             Self::High => "High",
  40         }
  41     }
  42 }
  43 
  44 impl fmt::Display for QualityProfile {
  45     fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
  46         formatter.write_str(self.query_value())
  47     }
  48 }
  49 
  50 impl FromStr for QualityProfile {
  51     type Err = ParseQualityProfileError;
  52 
  53     fn from_str(value: &str) -> Result<Self, Self::Err> {
  54         Self::parse(value).ok_or(ParseQualityProfileError)
  55     }
  56 }
  57 
  58 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  59 pub struct ParseQualityProfileError;
  60 
  61 impl fmt::Display for ParseQualityProfileError {
  62     fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
  63         formatter.write_str("expected quality profile `low` or `high`")
  64     }
  65 }
  66 
  67 impl Error for ParseQualityProfileError {}
  68 
  69 #[cfg(test)]
  70 mod tests {
  71     use super::*;
  72 
  73     #[test]
  74     fn stable_quality_vocabulary_is_case_insensitive() {
  75         for quality in QualityProfile::ALL {
  76             let value = quality.query_value();
  77             assert_eq!(QualityProfile::parse(value), Some(quality));
  78             assert_eq!(
  79                 QualityProfile::parse(&value.to_ascii_uppercase()),
  80                 Some(quality)
  81             );
  82             assert_eq!(value.parse(), Ok(quality));
  83         }
  84         assert_eq!(QualityProfile::parse("ultra"), None);
  85     }
  86 }

   1 //! Renderer optimization toggles — one switch per labeled optimization.
   2 //!
   3 //! Every renderer in the engine (GPU surfaces, GPU face splats, the SVO
   4 //! raymarcher, and the CPU splatter) is written as a *correct, simple
   5 //! reference path* plus a set of clearly labeled optimizations layered on
   6 //! top. Each optimization can be disabled at runtime, which serves three
   7 //! purposes:
   8 //!
   9 //! 1. **Debugging** — when a frame looks wrong, binary-search the toggles to
  10 //!    find which optimization broke it.
  11 //! 2. **Benchmarking** — measure exactly what each optimization buys on a
  12 //!    given machine (the HUD shows frame times).
  13 //! 3. **Documentation** — the toggle list *is* the catalog of every shortcut
  14 //!    the pipeline takes.
  15 //!
  16 //! The struct is plain data with no browser dependencies, so it is natively
  17 //! unit-tested. It crosses the wasm boundary as a bitfield (one `AtomicU32`
  18 //! in `lib.rs`). Each browser driver snapshots it once at the frame boundary;
  19 //! platform-free render code receives the snapshot by value.
  20 //!
  21 //! URL controls: `?rt_hiz=0&rt_shadows=0` … (`rt_<name>=0|1`). The settings
  22 //! menu calls the `set_render_toggle(name, enabled)` wasm export with the
  23 //! same names.
  24 
  25 /// One on/off switch per optimization, across all render paths.
  26 ///
  27 /// Correctness-preserving switches default on. The approximate diffuse-fill
  28 /// bake defaults off: first boot uses the strict analytic-light image, while
  29 /// `rt_bake=1` opts into the quantized field explicitly.
  30 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  31 pub struct RenderToggles {
  32     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  33     // CPU splatter (SoftwareRasterizer)
  34     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  35     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): 8x8-tile coarse hierarchical z-buffer. Rejects a
  36     /// whole octree subtree with a handful of tile reads when something
  37     /// nearer already covers its screen bounds. Off = every node is tested
  38     /// per-pixel by the fine z-buffer only.
  39     pub hierarchical_z: bool,
  40     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU + splat + raymarch): near-to-far traversal,
  41     /// submission, or resident-chunk selection. Maximizes early exits and
  42     /// z-rejection. Off retains each strategy's deterministic reference order.
  43     pub front_to_back: bool,
  44     /// OPTIMIZATION (raymarch): jump across the complete empty SVO leaf
  45     /// containing the current sample. Off = diagnostic finest-voxel DDA;
  46     /// both paths use the same exact point lookup and must report the same
  47     /// nearest hit/material/normal.
  48     pub empty_space_skip: bool,
  49     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): coarse-to-fine LOD — a subtree whose projection
  50     /// fits in ~a pixel is drawn as one MIP-filtered splat instead of being
  51     /// descended. Off = full descent to leaves regardless of distance, except
  52     /// for the renderer's non-optional malformed/workload safety cap.
  53     pub mip_lod: bool,
  54     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): the flashlight's occlusion ray (one SVO trace per
  55     /// shaded splat while the flashlight is on). This is a *quality*
  56     /// optimization: off means the beam shines through walls but shading
  57     /// gets cheaper.
  58     pub flashlight_occlusion: bool,
  59     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU): query the fine depth buffer before evaluating
  60     /// fixture, hero, and flashlight radiance. Off = shade every projected
  61     /// splat and let the ordinary write-time depth test reject it. The image
  62     /// is identical; only hidden-splat shading work changes.
  63     pub deferred_shading: bool,
  64     /// APPROXIMATION (CPU): sibling-count ambient occlusion. Off is the
  65     /// material/lighting reference with unit ambient visibility.
  66     pub ambient_occlusion: bool,
  67     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  68     // GPU paths (surface / splat / raymarch)
  69     // ------------------------------------------------------------------
  70     /// Direct-light visibility. Raster strategies use a hero-fixture depth
  71     /// map; raymarch traces finite SVO segments to analytic emitter samples.
  72     /// Off keeps otherwise-identical unoccluded direct lighting.
  73     pub shadow_pass: bool,
  74     /// OPTIMIZATION (splat): per-cell instance-range culling. Face instances
  75     /// are grouped into spatial cells; invisible cells are skipped and
  76     /// visible neighbors coalesce into one instanced draw. Off = every
  77     /// resident face is drawn every frame.
  78     pub cell_culling: bool,
  79     /// OPTIMIZATION (splat): stop submitting whole far chunks after the
  80     /// profile's face budget is exhausted. Off = draw every visible face;
  81     /// useful as the correctness/reference path when diagnosing pop-out.
  82     pub face_budget: bool,
  83     /// OPTIMIZATION (CPU + GPU): range rejection for every strategy, plus
  84     /// conservative camera visibility for raster paths. Raymarch filters
  85     /// complete chunk bounds before its resident-set cap. Off keeps all
  86     /// resident chunks eligible.
  87     pub distance_cull: bool,
  88     /// Dither/grain/banding-noise post effects (GPU). A visual feature more
  89     /// than a speedup; toggle to isolate its contribution to the image.
  90     pub dither: bool,
  91     /// Optional quantized diffuse fill in the CPU, indexed-surface, and splat
  92     /// strategies. Analytic fixtures remain authoritative; raymarch stays on
  93     /// analytic lighting because its stored bake is face-independent.
  94     pub baked_lighting: bool,
  95 }
  96 
  97 impl Default for RenderToggles {
  98     fn default() -> Self {
  99         Self {
 100             hierarchical_z: true,
 101             front_to_back: true,
 102             empty_space_skip: true,
 103             mip_lod: true,
 104             flashlight_occlusion: true,
 105             deferred_shading: true,
 106             ambient_occlusion: true,
 107             shadow_pass: true,
 108             cell_culling: true,
 109             face_budget: true,
 110             distance_cull: true,
 111             dither: true,
 112             baked_lighting: false,
 113         }
 114     }
 115 }
 116 
 117 impl RenderToggles {
 118     /// Baseline used when a renderer profile admits only a named subset of
 119     /// the global switchboard.
 120     pub const fn disabled() -> Self {
 121         Self {
 122             hierarchical_z: false,
 123             front_to_back: false,
 124             empty_space_skip: false,
 125             mip_lod: false,
 126             flashlight_occlusion: false,
 127             deferred_shading: false,
 128             ambient_occlusion: false,
 129             shadow_pass: false,
 130             cell_culling: false,
 131             face_budget: false,
 132             distance_cull: false,
 133             dither: false,
 134             baked_lighting: false,
 135         }
 136     }
 137 }

 139 /// Canonical query-name/bit ordering used by parsing and bitfield round trips.
 140 const TOGGLE_BITS: [(&str, u32); 13] = [
 141     ("hiz", 1 << 0),
 142     ("f2b", 1 << 1),
 143     ("mips", 1 << 2),
 144     ("beam_occlusion", 1 << 3),
 145     ("shadows", 1 << 4),
 146     ("cells", 1 << 5),
 147     ("budget", 1 << 6),
 148     ("cull", 1 << 7),
 149     ("dither", 1 << 8),
 150     ("skip", 1 << 9),
 151     ("bake", 1 << 10),
 152     ("deferred", 1 << 11),
 153     ("ao", 1 << 12),
 154 ];
 155 
 156 impl RenderToggles {
 157     fn field_mut(&mut self, name: &str) -> Option<&mut bool> {
 158         Some(match name {
 159             "hiz" => &mut self.hierarchical_z,
 160             "f2b" => &mut self.front_to_back,
 161             "skip" => &mut self.empty_space_skip,
 162             "mips" => &mut self.mip_lod,
 163             "beam_occlusion" => &mut self.flashlight_occlusion,
 164             "deferred" => &mut self.deferred_shading,
 165             "ao" => &mut self.ambient_occlusion,
 166             "shadows" => &mut self.shadow_pass,
 167             "cells" => &mut self.cell_culling,
 168             "budget" => &mut self.face_budget,
 169             "cull" => &mut self.distance_cull,
 170             "dither" => &mut self.dither,
 171             "bake" => &mut self.baked_lighting,
 172             _ => return None,
 173         })
 174     }
 175 
 176     fn field(&self, name: &str) -> Option<bool> {
 177         let mut copy = *self;
 178         copy.field_mut(name).map(|b| *b)
 179     }
 180 
 181     /// Sets one toggle by its short name. Unknown names are ignored (the
 182     /// settings menu and old URLs must never crash the engine).
 183     pub fn set(&mut self, name: &str, enabled: bool) {
 184         if let Some(field) = self.field_mut(name) {
 185             *field = enabled;
 186         }
 187     }
 188 
 189     /// Reads one toggle by its short name. Returning `None` for unknown
 190     /// names keeps diagnostics and browser tests on the same catalog as the
 191     /// parser and setter.
 192     pub fn enabled(&self, name: &str) -> Option<bool> {
 193         self.field(name)
 194     }
 195 
 196     /// Packs the toggles into a bitfield for the atomic global in `lib.rs`.
 197     pub fn to_bits(self) -> u32 {
 198         let mut bits = 0;
 199         for (name, bit) in TOGGLE_BITS {
 200             if self.field(name).expect("table names match fields") {
 201                 bits |= bit;
 202             }
 203         }
 204         bits
 205     }
 206 
 207     /// Inverse of [`Self::to_bits`].
 208     pub fn from_bits(bits: u32) -> Self {
 209         let mut toggles = Self::default();
 210         for (name, bit) in TOGGLE_BITS {
 211             toggles.set(name, bits & bit != 0);
 212         }
 213         toggles
 214     }
 215 }
 216 
 217 /// Applies `rt_<name>=0|1` pairs from a URL query (with or without the
 218 /// leading `?`) on top of the defaults. Unknown keys and malformed values
 219 /// are ignored, matching the generation-knob parser's tolerance.
 220 pub fn parse_render_toggles(query: &str) -> RenderToggles {
 221     let mut toggles = RenderToggles::default();
 222     for pair in query.trim_start_matches('?').split('&') {
 223         let Some((key, value)) = pair.split_once('=') else {
 224             continue;
 225         };
 226         let Some(name) = key.strip_prefix("rt_") else {
 227             continue;
 228         };
 229         match value {
 230             "0" | "false" | "off" => toggles.set(name, false),
 231             "1" | "true" | "on" => toggles.set(name, true),
 232             _ => {}
 233         }
 234     }
 235     toggles
 236 }

quality.rs and render_settings.rs are fine. Now the critical one: chunk_archive.rs — the RecordKey level issue. And generation_worker_policy.rs. And ports.rs.
   1 //! An append-only archive of generated chunks, and the index over it.
   2 //!
   3 //! Generating a chunk costs 42 ms at full resolution; decoding one from
   4 //! bytes costs 0.46 ms. Two orders of magnitude. Everything here follows
   5 //! from that single measurement: once a chunk has been generated, spending
   6 //! 42 ms to produce it a second time is pure waste, and a store that turns
   7 //! revisits into 0.46 ms reads lets the streaming frontier move faster than
   8 //! a player can walk instead of racing them.
   9 //!
  10 //! Append-only, deliberately. Updating a record in place means holes, a free
  11 //! list, and a file that can be corrupted by a crash halfway through a write.
  12 //! Appending means the only mutation is "make the file longer", the newest
  13 //! record for a key wins, and a torn tail costs exactly the one record that
  14 //! was being written — [`ChunkArchive::open`] stops at the first incomplete
  15 //! record rather than trusting a length it cannot verify.
  16 //!
  17 //! # Staleness is the whole risk
  18 //!
  19 //! A cache of generated geometry is only correct while the thing that
  20 //! generated it is unchanged. Serving a chunk built by last week's generator
  21 //! is far worse than regenerating it: the world silently disagrees with
  22 //! itself, half from disk and half from code, and nothing reports an error.
  23 //!
  24 //! So identity is checked at two levels and neither is optional:
  25 //!
  26 //! * The **file** carries an [`ArchiveIdentity`] — format version, seed,
  27 //!   level, chunk size, voxel scale, and a generator build id. Any mismatch
  28 //!   discards the entire archive rather than trying to salvage it.
  29 //! * Each **record** carries its LOD and a hash of the [`RealitySnapshot`]
  30 //!   it was generated against, because Peripheral Shift makes the same
  31 //!   coordinates a different world at a different drift epoch.
  32 //!
  33 //! The storage itself is a port: a real file natively, an OPFS handle in the
  34 //! browser. This module never names either, so it is unit-tested natively at
  35 //! full speed against a vector of bytes.
  36 
  37 use std::collections::HashMap;
  38 
  39 use crate::application::streaming::ChunkKey;
  40 use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
  41 
  42 /// Magic at the head of the file, and at the head of every record.
  43 ///
  44 /// Repeating it per record is what makes a torn tail detectable: a record
  45 /// that does not begin with this is not a record, whatever the previous
  46 /// length field claimed.
  47 const FILE_MAGIC: u32 = 0x5643_4B41; // "VCKA"
  48 const RECORD_MAGIC: u32 = 0x5643_4B52; // "VCKR"
  49 
  50 /// Bumped whenever the record framing changes.
  51 ///
  52 /// This is *not* a substitute for [`ArchiveIdentity::generator_id`]: the
  53 /// framing can be stable while the geometry it frames changes completely.
  54 const ARCHIVE_FORMAT_VERSION: u32 = 2;
  55 
  56 pub const HEADER_BYTES: usize = 32;
  57 /// magic + chunk x/z + lod + artifacts + padding + reality hash + checksum
  58 /// + payload length.
  59 const RECORD_HEADER_BYTES: usize = 4 + 8 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 8 + 8 + 4;
  60 
  61 /// What an archive was built by. Any difference invalidates every record.
  62 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  63 pub struct ArchiveIdentity {
  64     pub seed: u32,
  65     pub level: u32,
  66     /// Bit patterns, not floats: this is an equality check, and `NaN != NaN`
  67     /// would make an archive silently never match itself.
  68     pub chunk_size_bits: u32,
  69     pub voxel_scale_bits: u32,
  70     /// Identity of the code and parameters that generate geometry.
  71     ///
  72     /// Always folded together with [`build_id`] by [`new`](Self::new), so a
  73     /// caller cannot forget to invalidate archives when the generator itself
  74     /// changes. That mistake is not recoverable at runtime: the archive would
  75     /// keep serving last build's geometry, and nothing downstream can tell
  76     /// that a wall is in the wrong place.
  77     pub generator_id: u64,
  78 }
  79 
  80 /// Identity of this build, folded into every [`ArchiveIdentity`].
  81 ///
  82 /// `VACKROOMS_BUILD_ID` is set by `scripts/build-wasm.mjs` to the same source
  83 /// digest that stamps `static/pkg/.source-sha256`, so any change to generator
  84 /// source produces a different id and orphans every archive written by the
  85 /// previous build.
  86 ///
  87 /// Without it — a plain `cargo build`, or an editor running tests — this
  88 /// falls back to the crate version, which does *not* change per build. In
  89 /// that case a persistent archive can outlive a code change, so
  90 /// [`is_build_id_pinned`] reports whether the guarantee is real and callers
  91 /// that persist across builds should refuse to when it is not.
  92 pub fn build_id() -> u64 {
  93     fnv64(
  94         option_env!("VACKROOMS_BUILD_ID")
  95             .unwrap_or(concat!("unpinned-", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")))
  96             .as_bytes(),
  97     )
  98 }
  99 
 100 /// Whether this build carries a real source digest (see [`build_id`]).
 101 pub fn is_build_id_pinned() -> bool {
 102     option_env!("VACKROOMS_BUILD_ID").is_some()
 103 }
 104 
 105 impl ArchiveIdentity {
 106     pub fn new(seed: u32, level: u32, chunk_size: f32, voxel_scale: f32, generator_id: u64) -> Self {
 107         Self {
 108             seed,
 109             level,
 110             chunk_size_bits: chunk_size.to_bits(),
 111             voxel_scale_bits: voxel_scale.to_bits(),
 112             // Mixed, not stored raw: the caller's id describes the world's
 113             // parameters, `build_id` describes the code that reads them, and
 114             // an archive is only valid when both match.
 115             generator_id: generator_id ^ build_id().rotate_left(17),
 116         }
 117     }
 118 
 119     fn to_bytes(self) -> [u8; HEADER_BYTES] {
 120         let mut out = [0u8; HEADER_BYTES];
 121         out[0..4].copy_from_slice(&FILE_MAGIC.to_le_bytes());
 122         out[4..8].copy_from_slice(&ARCHIVE_FORMAT_VERSION.to_le_bytes());
 123         out[8..12].copy_from_slice(&self.seed.to_le_bytes());
 124         out[12..16].copy_from_slice(&self.level.to_le_bytes());
 125         out[16..20].copy_from_slice(&self.chunk_size_bits.to_le_bytes());
 126         out[20..24].copy_from_slice(&self.voxel_scale_bits.to_le_bytes());
 127         out[24..32].copy_from_slice(&self.generator_id.to_le_bytes());
 128         out
 129     }
 130 
 131     fn from_bytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<Self> {
 132         if bytes.len() < HEADER_BYTES
 133             || u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[0..4].try_into().ok()?) != FILE_MAGIC
 134             || u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[4..8].try_into().ok()?) != ARCHIVE_FORMAT_VERSION
 135         {
 136             return None;
 137         }
 138         Some(Self {
 139             seed: u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[8..12].try_into().ok()?),
 140             level: u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[12..16].try_into().ok()?),
 141             chunk_size_bits: u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[16..20].try_into().ok()?),
 142             voxel_scale_bits: u32::from_le_bytes(bytes[20..24].try_into().ok()?),
 143             generator_id: u64::from_le_bytes(bytes[24..32].try_into().ok()?),
 144         })
 145     }
 146 }
 147 
 148 /// Which chunk, at which detail, built for which renderer, in which epoch of
 149 /// the world.
 150 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
 151 pub struct RecordKey {
 152     pub chunk: ChunkKey,
 153     pub lod: u8,
 154     /// The artifact bits the record was generated for.
 155     ///
 156     /// Part of the key, not something inferred from the payload afterwards.
 157     /// A record built for the splat renderer holds face instances and no
 158     /// vertices; one built for the mesh renderer holds the reverse. Both
 159     /// answer `needs_surface_extraction()`, so any attempt to recognise them
 160     /// by which fields came back non-empty gets it wrong in one direction or
 161     /// the other — and the failure is silent, because a renderer handed the
 162     /// wrong products draws nothing rather than reporting an error.
 163     pub artifacts: u8,
 164     /// Hash of the [`RealitySnapshot`] the chunk was generated against.
 165     /// Without this, a chunk cached before a Peripheral Shift would be
 166     /// served after it, and the world would not drift where the player had
 167     /// already been — which is precisely where drift is supposed to happen.
 168     pub reality: u64,
 169 }
 170 
 171 impl RecordKey {
 172     pub fn new(chunk: ChunkKey, lod: u8, artifacts: u8, reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> Self {
 173         Self {
 174             chunk,
 175             lod,
 176             artifacts,
 177             reality: hash_reality(reality),
 178         }
 179     }
 180 }
 181 
 182 /// FNV-1a over bytes. Used for the payload checksum and the reality hash.
 183 fn fnv64(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
 184     let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
 185     for &byte in bytes {
 186         h ^= byte as u64;
 187         h = h.wrapping_mul(0x1000_0000_01b3);
 188     }
 189     h
 190 }
 191 
 192 /// FNV-1a over the snapshot's transport words.
 193 ///
 194 /// A hash, not the words themselves: snapshots are variable length and this
 195 /// only has to distinguish epochs, not reconstruct them. A collision would
 196 /// serve one epoch's geometry in another — at 64 bits, across the handful of
 197 /// epochs a session produces, that is not a risk worth a larger key.
 198 pub fn hash_reality(reality: &RealitySnapshot) -> u64 {
 199     let words = reality.to_words();
 200     let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(words.len() * 4);
 201     for word in words {
 202         bytes.extend_from_slice(&word.to_le_bytes());
 203     }
 204     fnv64(&bytes)
 205 }
 206 
 207 /// Where a record's payload lives in the file.
 208 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
 209 pub struct Extent {
 210     pub offset: u64,
 211     pub len: u32,
 212     /// FNV-1a of the payload, verified on every read.
 213     ///
 214     /// Without it a flipped bit decodes into *plausible* geometry — a wall
 215     /// in the wrong place, a light with an absurd radius — and nothing ever
 216     /// reports a problem. Regenerating a chunk costs 42 ms; rendering a
 217     /// corrupt one costs a bug nobody can reproduce.
 218     pub checksum: u64,
 219 }
 220 
 221 /// Byte storage behind an archive. A file natively; an OPFS access handle in
 222 /// the browser.
 223 pub trait ArchiveStorage {
 224     fn len(&self) -> u64;
 225     fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 226         self.len() == 0
 227     }
 228     /// Exactly `len` bytes at `offset`, or `None` if they are not all there.
 229     fn read_at(&self, offset: u64, len: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>>;
 230     /// Appends and returns the offset written to, or `None` if the write
 231     /// failed (a full disk, an exceeded browser quota).
 232     fn append(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<u64>;
 233     /// Discards everything. Used when the identity does not match.
 234     fn reset(&mut self);
 235     /// Shortens the storage to `len` bytes. Used to drop a torn tail before
 236     /// appending over it.
 237     fn truncate(&mut self, len: u64);
 238 }
 239 
 240 /// An index over an append-only chunk log.
 241 pub struct ChunkArchive {
 242     identity: ArchiveIdentity,
 243     index: HashMap<RecordKey, Extent>,
 244     /// Bytes that were scanned and indexed. A torn tail beyond this is
 245     /// overwritten by the next append rather than being read.
 246     end: u64,
 247     hits: u64,
 248     misses: u64,
 249     stored: u64,
 250     corrupt: u64,
 251 }
 252 
 253 impl ChunkArchive {
 254     /// Opens an archive over `storage`, rebuilding the index by replaying it.
 255     ///
 256     /// Resets the storage when it is empty, unreadable, or was written by a
 257     /// different generator — see the module note on why salvage is not
 258     /// attempted.
 259     pub fn open(storage: &mut dyn ArchiveStorage, identity: ArchiveIdentity) -> Self {
 260         let existing = storage
 261             .read_at(0, HEADER_BYTES)
 262             .and_then(|bytes| ArchiveIdentity::from_bytes(&bytes));
 263         let mut archive = Self {
 264             identity,
 265             index: HashMap::new(),
 266             end: HEADER_BYTES as u64,
 267             hits: 0,
 268             misses: 0,
 269             stored: 0,
 270             corrupt: 0,
 271         };
 272         if existing == Some(identity) {
 273             archive.replay(storage);
 274         } else {
 275             storage.reset();
 276             storage.append(&identity.to_bytes());
 277         }
 278         archive
 279     }
 280 
 281     /// Rebuilds the index by walking records from the header to the first one
 282     /// that is not wholly present.
 283     fn replay(&mut self, storage: &dyn ArchiveStorage) {
 284         let total = storage.len();
 285         let mut offset = HEADER_BYTES as u64;
 286         while offset + RECORD_HEADER_BYTES as u64 <= total {
 287             let Some(header) = storage.read_at(offset, RECORD_HEADER_BYTES) else {
 288                 break;
 289             };
 290             if u32::from_le_bytes(header[0..4].try_into().expect("4 bytes")) != RECORD_MAGIC {
 291                 // Not a record boundary: the tail is torn. Everything before
 292                 // it is still good, and the next append overwrites this.
 293                 break;
 294             }
 295             let chunk_x = i64::from_le_bytes(header[4..12].try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
 296             let chunk_z = i64::from_le_bytes(header[12..20].try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
 297             let lod = header[20];
 298             let artifacts = header[21];
 299             let reality = u64::from_le_bytes(header[24..32].try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
 300             let checksum = u64::from_le_bytes(header[32..40].try_into().expect("8 bytes"));
 301             let len = u32::from_le_bytes(header[40..44].try_into().expect("4 bytes"));
 302 
 303             let payload_at = offset + RECORD_HEADER_BYTES as u64;
 304             if payload_at + len as u64 > total {
 305                 break; // Truncated payload: the record never finished.
 306             }
 307             // A later record for the same key shadows an earlier one, which
 308             // is what makes an append-only log support rewrites at all.
 309             self.index.insert(
 310                 RecordKey {
 311                     chunk: (chunk_x, chunk_z),
 312                     lod,
 313                     artifacts,
 314                     reality,
 315                 },
 316                 Extent {
 317                     offset: payload_at,
 318                     len,
 319                     checksum,
 320                 },
 321             );
 322             offset = payload_at + len as u64;
 323         }
 324         self.end = offset;
 325     }
 326 
 327     pub fn identity(&self) -> ArchiveIdentity {
 328         self.identity
 329     }
 330 
 331     pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
 332         self.index.len()
 333     }
 334 
 335     pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
 336         self.index.is_empty()
 337     }
 338 
 339     /// Reads (hits, misses, stored) since opening.
 340     pub fn stats(&self) -> (u64, u64, u64) {
 341         (self.hits, self.misses, self.stored)
 342     }
 343 
 344     /// Records rejected by their checksum. Any non-zero value means the
 345     /// storage under this archive is damaging data.
 346     pub fn corrupt_records(&self) -> u64 {
 347         self.corrupt
 348     }
 349 
 350     pub fn contains(&self, key: RecordKey) -> bool {

 351         self.index.contains_key(&key)
 352     }
 353 
 354     /// The stored payload bytes for a key, if this archive has them.
 355     pub fn get(&mut self, storage: &dyn ArchiveStorage, key: RecordKey) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
 356         let extent = *self.index.get(&key)?;
 357         match storage.read_at(extent.offset, extent.len as usize) {
 358             Some(bytes) if fnv64(&bytes) == extent.checksum => {
 359                 self.hits += 1;
 360                 Some(bytes)
 361             }
 362             Some(_) => {
 363                 // Right length, wrong bytes. Drop the record and regenerate:
 364                 // corrupt geometry that renders is far worse than a cache
 365                 // miss, because nothing downstream can tell it is wrong.
 366                 self.index.remove(&key);
 367                 self.corrupt += 1;
 368                 self.misses += 1;
 369                 None
 370             }
 371             None => {
 372                 // Indexed but unreadable: the file shrank under us. Forget it
 373                 // rather than returning a short read as if it were geometry.
 374                 self.index.remove(&key);
 375                 self.misses += 1;
 376                 None
 377             }
 378         }
 379     }
 380 
 381     /// Appends a payload for a key. A failed write is not an error the
 382     /// caller has to handle — the chunk was generated and is usable; it just
 383     /// will not be there next time.
 384     pub fn put(&mut self, storage: &mut dyn ArchiveStorage, key: RecordKey, payload: &[u8]) {
 385         let mut record = Vec::with_capacity(RECORD_HEADER_BYTES + payload.len());
 386         record.extend_from_slice(&RECORD_MAGIC.to_le_bytes());
 387         record.extend_from_slice(&key.chunk.0.to_le_bytes());
 388         record.extend_from_slice(&key.chunk.1.to_le_bytes());
 389         record.push(key.lod);
 390         record.push(key.artifacts);
 391         record.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 2]); // pad to keep the hashes aligned
 392         record.extend_from_slice(&key.reality.to_le_bytes());
 393         let checksum = fnv64(payload);
 394         record.extend_from_slice(&checksum.to_le_bytes());
 395         record.extend_from_slice(&(payload.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
 396         record.extend_from_slice(payload);
 397 
 398         // Drop anything past the last record the replay could verify.
 399         // Appending *after* a torn tail leaves the garbage in the log, and
 400         // the next replay then reads a corrupt length, walks off the record
 401         // boundary, and loses every record written after it — turning one
 402         // bad write into the loss of a whole session.
 403         if storage.len() != self.end {
 404             storage.truncate(self.end);
 405         }
 406         if let Some(offset) = storage.append(&record) {
 407             let payload_at = offset + RECORD_HEADER_BYTES as u64;
 408             self.index.insert(
 409                 key,
 410                 Extent {
 411                     offset: payload_at,
 412                     len: payload.len() as u32,
 413                     checksum,
 414                 },
 415             );
 416             self.end = payload_at + payload.len() as u64;
 417             self.stored += 1;
 418         }
 419     }
 420 
 421     /// Counts a generation that bypassed the archive, for the hit rate.
 422     pub fn note_miss(&mut self) {
 423         self.misses += 1;
 424     }
 425 
 426     /// Bytes the archive currently occupies.
 427     pub fn bytes(&self) -> u64 {
 428         self.end
 429     }
 430 
 431     /// Drops every record and starts the log again.
 432     ///
 433     /// An append-only log cannot free one record, so a bounded archive
 434     /// discards all of them at once. That is crude — it throws away chunks
 435     /// the player is standing next to along with ones they left an hour ago —
 436     /// but it is correct, it is O(1), and the cost of being wrong is one
 437     /// regeneration. A reuse-ordered eviction would need either a rewritten
 438     /// log or an index of holes, which is the complexity this format exists
 439     /// to avoid.
 440     pub fn clear(&mut self, storage: &mut dyn ArchiveStorage) {
 441         storage.reset();
 442         storage.append(&self.identity.to_bytes());
 443         self.index.clear();
 444         self.end = HEADER_BYTES as u64;
 445     }
 446 }
 447 
 448 /// An in-memory [`ArchiveStorage`], for tests and for a browser session that
 449 /// has no persistent storage available.
 450 #[derive(Debug, Default)]
 451 pub struct MemoryStorage {
 452     bytes: Vec<u8>,
 453 }
 454 
 455 impl MemoryStorage {
 456     pub fn new() -> Self {
 457         Self::default()
 458     }
 459 
 460     pub fn from_bytes(bytes: Vec<u8>) -> Self {
 461         Self { bytes }
 462     }
 463 
 464     pub fn bytes(&self) -> &[u8] {
 465         &self.bytes
 466     }
 467 
 468     /// Simulates a torn write: the tail is lost, the header is not.
 469     pub fn truncate(&mut self, len: usize) {
 470         self.bytes.truncate(len);
 471     }
 472 }
 473 
 474 impl ArchiveStorage for MemoryStorage {
 475     fn len(&self) -> u64 {
 476         self.bytes.len() as u64
 477     }
 478 
 479     fn read_at(&self, offset: u64, len: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
 480         let start = usize::try_from(offset).ok()?;
 481         let end = start.checked_add(len)?;
 482         self.bytes.get(start..end).map(<[u8]>::to_vec)
 483     }
 484 
 485     fn append(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<u64> {
 486         let offset = self.bytes.len() as u64;
 487         self.bytes.extend_from_slice(bytes);
 488         Some(offset)
 489     }
 490 
 491     fn reset(&mut self) {
 492         self.bytes.clear();
 493     }
 494 
 495     fn truncate(&mut self, len: u64) {
 496         if let Ok(len) = usize::try_from(len) {
 497             self.bytes.truncate(len);
 498         }
 499     }
 500 }

 519     #[test]

 521         let mut storage = MemoryStorage::new();
 522         let mut archive = ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 523         archive.put(&mut storage, key(0, 0, 0), b"the geometry");
 524         assert_eq!(

 528         assert_eq!(archive.get(&storage, key(1, 0, 0)), None);

 531     #[test]
 532     fn the_index_survives_reopening() {
 533         // The point of a file: a later session must find what an earlier one
 534         // wrote, without regenerating anything to discover it.
 535         let mut storage = MemoryStorage::new();
 536         {
 537             let mut archive = ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 538             archive.put(&mut storage, key(0, 0, 0), b"first");
 539             archive.put(&mut storage, key(3, -4, 2), b"second");
 540         }
 541         let mut reopened = ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 542         assert_eq!(reopened.len(), 2);
 543         assert_eq!(
 544             reopened.get(&storage, key(3, -4, 2)).as_deref(),
 545             Some(b"second".as_slice())
 546         );
 547     }

 549     #[test]
 550     fn the_newest_record_for_a_key_wins() {
 551         let mut storage = MemoryStorage::new();
 552         let mut archive = ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 553         archive.put(&mut storage, key(0, 0, 0), b"stale");
 554         archive.put(&mut storage, key(0, 0, 0), b"fresh");
 555         assert_eq!(
 556             archive.get(&storage, key(0, 0, 0)).as_deref(),
 557             Some(b"fresh".as_slice())
 558         );
 559         let mut reopened = ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 560         assert_eq!(
 561             reopened.get(&storage, key(0, 0, 0)).as_deref(),
 562             Some(b"fresh".as_slice()),
 563             "replaying the log must end on the newest record, not the first"
 564         );
 565     }

 571         // nothing.

 586     #[test]

 630     #[test]
 631     fn a_torn_tail_costs_only_the_record_being_written() {
 632         // A crash, a closed tab, or an exceeded quota mid-append. Everything
 633         // written before it must still be readable, because the alternative
 634         // is losing an entire session's generation to one bad write.
 635         let mut storage = MemoryStorage::new();
 636         {
 637             let mut archive = ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 638             archive.put(&mut storage, key(0, 0, 0), b"complete");
 639             archive.put(&mut storage, key(1, 1, 0), b"interrupted halfway");
 640         }
 641         let full = storage.bytes().len();
 642         storage.truncate(full - 8);
 643 
 644         let mut archive = ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 645         assert_eq!(
 646             archive.get(&storage, key(0, 0, 0)).as_deref(),
 647             Some(b"complete".as_slice()),
 648             "an earlier complete record was lost to a later torn one"
 649         );
 650         assert_eq!(archive.get(&storage, key(1, 1, 0)), None);
 651 
 652         // And the archive stays writable: the next append lands on the torn
 653         // boundary and reopening finds it.
 654         archive.put(&mut storage, key(2, 2, 0), b"after recovery");
 655         let mut reopened = ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 656         assert_eq!(
 657             reopened.get(&storage, key(2, 2, 0)).as_deref(),
 658             Some(b"after recovery".as_slice())
 659         );
 660     }

 674     #[test]
 675     fn a_failed_append_is_survivable() {
 676         // A browser that has run out of quota must degrade to "generate every
 677         // time", not to a broken index that hands out offsets nothing wrote.
 678         struct FullDisk(MemoryStorage);
 679         impl ArchiveStorage for FullDisk {
 680             fn len(&self) -> u64 {
 681                 self.0.len()
 682             }
 683             fn read_at(&self, offset: u64, len: usize) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
 684                 self.0.read_at(offset, len)
 685             }
 686             fn append(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<u64> {
 687                 // The header write succeeds; every record write fails.
 688                 if self.0.len() == 0 {
 689                     self.0.append(bytes)
 690                 } else {
 691                     None
 692                 }
 693             }
 694             fn reset(&mut self) {
 695                 self.0.reset();
 696             }
 697             fn truncate(&mut self, len: u64) {
 698                 self.0.truncate(len as usize);
 699             }
 700         }
 701 
 702         let mut storage = FullDisk(MemoryStorage::new());
 703         let mut archive = ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 704         archive.put(&mut storage, key(0, 0, 0), b"never lands");
 705         assert!(archive.is_empty());
 706         assert_eq!(archive.get(&storage, key(0, 0, 0)), None);
 707     }

 761     #[test]
 762     fn a_corrupted_payload_is_refused_rather_than_rendered() {
 763         // A flipped bit decodes into plausible geometry — a wall in the wrong
 764         // place — and nothing downstream can tell. A miss costs 42 ms; a
 765         // corrupt hit costs a bug nobody can reproduce.
 766         let mut storage = MemoryStorage::new();
 767         let mut archive = ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 768         archive.put(&mut storage, key(0, 0, 0), b"honest geometry");
 769 
 770         // Flip a bit inside the payload, leaving every length intact.
 771         let mut bytes = storage.bytes().to_vec();
 772         let last = bytes.len() - 1;
 773         bytes[last] ^= 0b0000_1000;
 774         let mut damaged = MemoryStorage::from_bytes(bytes);
 775 
 776         let mut archive = ChunkArchive::open(&mut damaged, identity());
 777         assert_eq!(archive.get(&damaged, key(0, 0, 0)), None);
 778         assert_eq!(archive.corrupt_records(), 1);
 779         // And the bad record is forgotten, so it is not re-read every frame.
 780         assert!(!archive.contains(key(0, 0, 0)));
 781     }

 783     #[test]
 784     fn an_older_format_is_never_read_as_the_current_one() {
 785         // Adding the artifact byte and the checksum moved every field. An
 786         // archive from before that must be discarded, not reinterpreted.
 787         let mut storage = MemoryStorage::new();
 788         {
 789             let mut archive = ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 790             archive.put(&mut storage, key(0, 0, 0), b"geometry");
 791         }
 792         // Rewrite the header's version word to the previous format.
 793         let mut bytes = storage.bytes().to_vec();
 794         bytes[4..8].copy_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes());
 795         let mut old = MemoryStorage::from_bytes(bytes);
 796 
 797         let archive = ChunkArchive::open(&mut old, identity());
 798         assert!(archive.is_empty(), "a v1 archive was read as v2");
 799     }

 801     #[test]
 802     fn arbitrary_bytes_never_panic_and_never_become_geometry() {
 803         // An archive is read from a file the process does not control: a
 804         // half-synced OPFS handle, a copied save, a disk that lied. Opening
 805         // one must never panic and must never manufacture a record, whatever
 806         // the bytes are. Lengths are attacker-shaped here on purpose —
 807         // u32::MAX payload lengths and offsets past the end.
 808         let mut state: u64 = 0x1234_5678_9abc_def0;
 809         let mut next = || {
 810             state ^= state << 13;
 811             state ^= state >> 7;
 812             state ^= state << 17;
 813             state
 814         };
 815         for case in 0..300 {
 816             let len = (next() % 512) as usize;
 817             let mut bytes: Vec<u8> = (0..len).map(|_| (next() & 0xFF) as u8).collect();
 818             // Half the cases wear a valid file header, so the replay actually
 819             // walks into the garbage instead of rejecting it up front.
 820             if case % 2 == 0 {
 821                 let mut storage = MemoryStorage::new();
 822                 ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 823                 let mut framed = storage.bytes().to_vec();
 824                 framed.append(&mut bytes);
 825                 bytes = framed;
 826             }
 827             let mut storage = MemoryStorage::from_bytes(bytes);
 828             let mut archive = ChunkArchive::open(&mut storage, identity());
 829             // Whatever it made of that, no key may resolve to geometry.
 830             assert_eq!(archive.get(&storage, key(0, 0, 0)), None, "case {case}");
 831         }
 832     }
