chunk_archive.rs confirmed:
- `RecordKey` (lines 150-169): fields chunk, lod, artifacts, reality — NO level field. The record header (RECORD_HEADER_BYTES at line 59: magic + chunk x/z + lod + artifacts + padding + reality hash + checksum + payload length) also has no level.
- `ArchiveIdentity` DOES include level (line 64: `pub level: u32`, set in `new` at 106-117, written at 124). But identity is checked only at `open()` (line 272: `if existing == Some(identity)`).

Now I need to verify how ArchivedChunkSource uses this — whether the `level` parameter in `load_with_artifacts`/`fetch` is passed to RecordKey. Let me read archived_chunk_source.rs and generation_worker_policy.rs, and check lib.rs worker_entry. Also check the worker_source.rs fetch path and where ArchivedChunkSource::fetch is used.
chunk_archive.rs confirmed — RecordKey has no level. Now verify the ArchivedChunkSource data flow.
   1 //! A [`ChunkSourcePort`] that reads from a [`ChunkArchive`] first and
   2 //! generates only what the archive does not have — writing back whatever it
   3 //! had to generate.
   4 //!
   5 //! The measurement this exists for, on one 10 u chunk:
   6 //!
   7 //! ```text
   8 //!            generate    decode from archive
   9 //! lod 0      42.0 ms     0.46 ms      (92x)
  10 //! lod 2       6.5 ms     0.04 ms     (150x)
  11 //! ```
  12 //!
  13 //! Two orders of magnitude changes what streaming *is*. Generation-bound, the
  14 //! frontier races the player and the LOD ladder has to be sized against how
  15 //! much can be produced per tick. Archive-bound, a chunk costs less than a
  16 //! frame's slack, and revisiting somewhere is free — so a player can turn
  17 //! around, backtrack, or circle a floor they have already walked without the
  18 //! engine doing any architectural work at all.
  19 //!
  20 //! What it does *not* buy is residency. A square mile is 25600 chunks:
  21 //! 8.8 GB archived at full resolution, 0.9 GB at lod 2. The archive removes
  22 //! the cost of *producing* geometry, never the cost of *holding* it — that
  23 //! is still the LOD ladder's job.
  24 //!
  25 //! Writes are best-effort throughout. A full disk or an exceeded browser
  26 //! quota makes a session slower, never wrong: every miss is generated, and a
  27 //! failed append is dropped.
  28 
  29 use std::cell::RefCell;
  30 
  31 use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
  32 use vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig;
  33 use vackrooms::use_cases::ports::NoiseProvider;
  34 
  35 use crate::adapters::chunk_codec::{decode_chunk_payload, encode_chunk_payload};
  36 use crate::adapters::local_chunk_source::LocalChunkSource;
  37 use crate::adapters::surface_mesh::SurfelDensity;
  38 use crate::application::chunk_archive::{
  39     ArchiveIdentity, ArchiveStorage, ChunkArchive, RecordKey,
  40 };
  41 use crate::application::ports::{
  42     ChunkPayload, ChunkSourcePort, RenderArtifactNeeds,
  43 };
  44 use crate::application::streaming::chunk_key;
  45 
  46 /// Default ceiling on one archive, bytes.
  47 ///
  48 /// 64 MB holds roughly 500 full-resolution 10 u chunks or 2000 at the
  49 /// ladder's mid rung — far more than the rolling window ever has resident, so
  50 /// a player pacing an area never sees a clear. A worker pool multiplies this,
  51 /// which is why the pool shards the world rather than each worker archiving
  52 /// all of it.
  53 pub const DEFAULT_ARCHIVE_BYTES: u64 = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
  54 
  55 pub struct ArchivedChunkSource<N: NoiseProvider> {
  56     inner: LocalChunkSource<N>,
  57     // `RefCell` because the port loads through `&self`: reading an archive
  58     // updates its index and counters, which is bookkeeping, not state the
  59     // caller can observe.
  60     archive: RefCell<ChunkArchive>,
  61     storage: RefCell<Box<dyn ArchiveStorage>>,
  62     max_bytes: u64,
  63     clears: RefCell<u64>,
  64 }
  65 
  66 impl<N: NoiseProvider> ArchivedChunkSource<N> {
  67     /// Wraps a generating source with an archive over `storage`.
  68     ///
  69     /// `generator_id` must change whenever generated geometry would — a
  70     /// build hash or source digest. Getting this wrong is the one failure
  71     /// mode that matters: an archive keyed to a generator it does not match
  72     /// serves a world that is half disk and half code.
  73     pub fn new(
  74         noise: N,
  75         seed: u32,
  76         config: GeneratorConfig,
  77         storage: Box<dyn ArchiveStorage>,
  78         generator_id: u64,
  79     ) -> Self {
  80         Self::with_budget(
  81             noise,
  82             seed,
  83             config,
  84             storage,
  85             generator_id,
  86             DEFAULT_ARCHIVE_BYTES,
  87         )
  88     }
  89 
  90     /// As [`new`](Self::new), with an explicit ceiling on the archive.
  91     pub fn with_budget(
  92         noise: N,
  93         seed: u32,
  94         config: GeneratorConfig,
  95         mut storage: Box<dyn ArchiveStorage>,
  96         generator_id: u64,
  97         max_bytes: u64,
  98     ) -> Self {
  99         let identity = ArchiveIdentity::new(
 100             seed,
 101             config.level,
 102             config.chunk_size,
 103             config.voxel_scale,
 104             generator_id,
 105         );
 106         let archive = ChunkArchive::open(storage.as_mut(), identity);
 107         Self {
 108             inner: LocalChunkSource::new(noise, seed, config),
 109             archive: RefCell::new(archive),
 110             storage: RefCell::new(storage),
 111             max_bytes,
 112             clears: RefCell::new(0),
 113         }
 114     }
 115 
 116     /// Sets how finely the surfel artifact samples the surface. The archive
 117     /// needs no invalidation for this: `generator_id` already folds in the
 118     /// query string that carries the density.
 119     pub fn with_surfel_density(mut self, density: SurfelDensity) -> Self {
 120         self.inner = self.inner.with_surfel_density(density);
 121         self
 122     }
 123 
 124     /// How many times the archive has been emptied to stay inside its budget.
 125     /// A session that keeps climbing is thrashing and wants a larger budget.
 126     pub fn clears(&self) -> u64 {
 127         *self.clears.borrow()
 128     }
 129 
 130     /// (hits, misses, stored) since opening.
 131     pub fn stats(&self) -> (u64, u64, u64) {
 132         self.archive.borrow().stats()
 133     }
 134 
 135     /// Records rejected by their checksum. Non-zero means the storage under
 136     /// this archive is damaging data.
 137     pub fn corrupt_records(&self) -> u64 {
 138         self.archive.borrow().corrupt_records()
 139     }
 140 
 141     /// Chunks currently indexed.
 142     pub fn archived_chunks(&self) -> usize {
 143         self.archive.borrow().len()
 144     }
 145 
 146     fn fetch(
 147         &self,
 148         origin_x: f32,
 149         origin_z: f32,
 150         level: u32,
 151         lod: u8,
 152         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 153         artifacts: RenderArtifactNeeds,
 154     ) -> ChunkPayload {
 155         let key = RecordKey::new(
 156             chunk_key(origin_x, origin_z),
 157             lod,
 158             artifacts.bits(),
 159             reality,
 160         );
 161 
 162         let stored = {
 163             let storage = self.storage.borrow();
 164             self.archive.borrow_mut().get(storage.as_ref(), key)
 165         };
 166         if let Some(bytes) = stored
 167             && let Some(payload) = decode_chunk_payload(&bytes)
 168         {
 169             return payload;
 170         }
 171         // Absent, corrupt, or archived for a different renderer — the
 172         // artifact bits are part of the key, so a record built for the splat
 173         // renderer is simply not found by a mesh renderer rather than being
 174         // handed over with the wrong products.
 175         self.archive.borrow_mut().note_miss();
 176 
 177         let payload = self
 178             .inner
 179             .load_with_artifacts(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, reality, artifacts);
 180         let encoded = encode_chunk_payload(&payload);
 181         let mut storage = self.storage.borrow_mut();
 182         let mut archive = self.archive.borrow_mut();
 183         // Bound the log before growing it. An append-only file cannot free
 184         // one record, so staying inside a budget means emptying it — see
 185         // `ChunkArchive::clear` for why that trade is the right one here.
 186         if archive.bytes() + encoded.len() as u64 > self.max_bytes {
 187             archive.clear(storage.as_mut());
 188             *self.clears.borrow_mut() += 1;
 189         }
 190         archive.put(storage.as_mut(), key, &encoded);
 191         drop(archive);
 192         payload
 193     }
 194 }
 195

 236     }
 237 }

 256     #[test]
 257     fn an_archived_chunk_is_identical_to_the_generated_one() {
 258         // The load-bearing property. An archive that returns *nearly* the
 259         // right geometry is worse than no archive: the world would differ
 260         // depending on whether you had been somewhere before.
 261         let direct = LocalChunkSource::new(
 262             SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
 263             42,
 264             GeneratorConfig::low_spec(),
 265         );
 266         let archived = source(Box::new(MemoryStorage::new()));
 267         for (ox, oz) in [(0.0, 30.0), (10.0, 10.0), (-40.0, 80.0)] {
 268             let expected = direct.load_with_artifacts(
 269                 ox,
 270                 oz,
 271                 0,
 272                 0,
 273                 &RealitySnapshot::default(),
 274                 RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE,
 275             );
 276             // First call generates and writes; second reads back.
 277             for pass in 0..2 {
 278                 let got = archived.load_with_artifacts(
 279                     ox,
 280                     oz,
 281                     0,
 282                     0,
 283                     &RealitySnapshot::default(),
 284                     RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE,
 285                 );
 286                 assert_eq!(got.collision, expected.collision, "pass {pass} at ({ox},{oz})");
 287                 assert_eq!(
 288                     got.surface.vertices.len(),
 289                     expected.surface.vertices.len(),
 290                     "pass {pass} at ({ox},{oz})"
 291                 );
 292                 assert_eq!(got.lights.len(), expected.lights.len(), "pass {pass}");
 293             }
 294         }
 295         let (hits, _, stored) = archived.stats();
 296         assert_eq!(stored, 3, "each chunk should be written exactly once");
 297         assert_eq!(hits, 3, "the second pass should have been served from disk");
 298     }

 300     #[test]
 301     fn revisiting_is_dramatically_cheaper_than_generating() {
 302         // The number the whole design rests on. Deliberately a loose bound —
 303         // this asserts an order of magnitude, not a benchmark, so it does not
 304         // become flaky on a loaded machine.
 305         let archived = source(Box::new(MemoryStorage::new()));
 306         let load = |ox: f32| {
 307             archived.load_with_artifacts(
 308                 ox,
 309                 0.0,
 310                 0,
 311                 0,
 312                 &RealitySnapshot::default(),
 313                 RenderArtifactNeeds::SURFACE,
 314             )
 315         };
 316         let cold = Instant::now();
 317         for i in 0..4 {
 318             load(i as f32 * 10.0);
 319         }
 320         let cold = cold.elapsed();

Confirmed the critical finding:
- `ArchivedChunkSource::fetch` (lines 146-193) receives `level` but `RecordKey::new` (line 155-160) does NOT include level. So a chunk generated for level 0 at (0,0) will be served for a level 1 request at (0,0) — provided the payload difference is real (config.with_level(level) → level_generator differs per level, per prior analysis line 13848).
- The archive identity includes level only at open time (`with_budget` line 99-105, `config.level`). The worker is initialized with a level from the URL query and stays there. When the engine switches levels (door transit, noclip), it requests chunks at the new level; the worker's `fetch` honors the `level` argument for generation but uses the level-agnostic key → cross-level cache hits.

Also note that this is per-worker: each worker has its own archive shard (pool shards the world). So the archive in a worker for chunk (0,0) was written when the player was at level 0 (the initial level). After door transit to level 1, the arrival chunk is (0,0) at level 1 → same key → wrong-level record served. CRITICAL.

Wait — need to double check: when switch_level happens, does the engine clear `pending` and the workers' archives remain? Yes, workers' archives persist across level switches (no re-init). And `RecordKey` reality hash: `RealitySnapshot` is not reset by switch_level — same hash. But note: chunk (0,0) at level 0 was generated with reality default; at level 1 the reality may have stamps from Level 0 gates... `reality` is preserved across switch_level (only cleared on respawn? no — respawn doesn't reset reality either; reality changes only via gate traversal and delirium). So keys collide.

Let me now verify the worker side: generation_worker_policy.rs, generation_worker_requests.rs, worker_source.rs, and lib.rs worker_entry. Also check `LocalChunkSource::load_with_artifacts` passes `config.with_level(level)` so generation differs per level.
   1 //! Select concurrency for the browser's chunk-generation worker pool.
   2 //!
   3 //! This policy configures world generation and streaming only. The software
   4 //! splat renderer remains on the browser's main thread. Keeping query parsing
   5 //! and hardware clamping here makes the contract natively testable and keeps
   6 //! browser APIs out of the application layer.
   7 
   8 /// Safety ceiling for generation workers — not a target. `Auto` should use
   9 /// every hardware thread the browser reports (minus one reserved for the
  10 /// main/render thread), including on high-core-count machines; this only
  11 /// guards against a browser misreporting an absurd `hardwareConcurrency`
  12 /// value and spawning an unreasonable number of Worker instances (each one
  13 /// duplicates the WASM module and atlas-building scratch memory).
  14 pub const MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS: u8 = 32;
  15 
  16 #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  17 pub enum GenerationWorkerPreference {
  18     /// Reserve one reported hardware thread for the browser/render loop.
  19     Auto,
  20     /// Generate synchronously through `LocalChunkSource` on the main thread.
  21     Disabled,
  22     /// Request an explicit number, still bounded by reported hardware.
  23     Fixed(u8),
  24 }
  25 
  26 impl Default for GenerationWorkerPreference {
  27     fn default() -> Self {
  28         Self::Auto
  29     }
  30 }
  31 
  32 impl GenerationWorkerPreference {
  33     /// Resolve a safe pool size from `Navigator.hardwareConcurrency`.
  34     /// Unknown/invalid reports use the conservative historical fallback of
  35     /// two hardware threads; automatic selection therefore uses one worker.
  36     pub fn resolve(self, hardware_concurrency: f64) -> usize {
  37         if self == Self::Disabled {
  38             return 0;
  39         }
  40 
  41         let reported_threads = if hardware_concurrency.is_finite() && hardware_concurrency >= 1.0 {
  42             hardware_concurrency.floor().min(u32::MAX as f64) as u32
  43         } else {
  44             2
  45         };
  46         let auto_workers = reported_threads
  47             .saturating_sub(1)
  48             .clamp(1, u32::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)) as u8;
  49         let fixed_worker_ceiling =
  50             reported_threads.clamp(1, u32::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)) as u8;
  51         match self {
  52             Self::Auto => auto_workers,
  53             Self::Fixed(requested) => requested.clamp(1, fixed_worker_ceiling),
  54             Self::Disabled => 0,
  55         }
  56         .into()
  57     }
  58 }
  59 
  60 /// Parses the last exact `workers` query pair. Canonical values are `auto`,
  61 /// `0`, and positive integers; oversized integers clamp to the product cap.
  62 /// Missing or malformed values safely restore automatic selection.
  63 pub fn parse_generation_worker_preference(query: &str) -> GenerationWorkerPreference {
  64     let mut preference = GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto;
  65     for (key, value) in query
  66         .trim_start_matches('?')
  67         .split('&')
  68         .filter_map(|pair| pair.split_once('='))
  69     {
  70         if key != "workers" {
  71             continue;
  72         }
  73         preference = match value {
  74             "auto" => GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto,
  75             "0" => GenerationWorkerPreference::Disabled,
  76             _ => value
  77                 .parse::<u32>()
  78                 .ok()
  79                 .filter(|requested| *requested > 0)
  80                 .map(|requested| {
  81                     GenerationWorkerPreference::Fixed(
  82                         requested.min(u32::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)) as u8,
  83                     )
  84                 })
  85                 .unwrap_or(GenerationWorkerPreference::Auto),
  86         };
  87     }
  88     preference
  89 }
  90

   1 //! Exact in-flight request bookkeeping for the generation-worker pool.
   2 //!
   3 //! Browser callbacks can arrive after a worker has failed or after the engine
   4 //! has already retried a chunk. This small ledger gives every callback one
   5 //! deterministic operation: finish the exact request it echoes, fail the
   6 //! oldest request after a malformed reply, or drain a failed worker.
   7 
   8 use std::collections::VecDeque;
   9 
  10 use crate::application::ports::ChunkRequest;
  11 use crate::application::streaming::ChunkKey;
  12 
  13 #[derive(Debug)]
  14 struct WorkerRequests {
  15     accepting_work: bool,
  16     in_flight: VecDeque<ChunkRequest>,
  17 }
  18 
  19 /// Per-worker request ownership. Request identity is always checked through
  20 /// [`ChunkRequest::is_same_request`], never by chunk coordinates alone.
  21 #[derive(Debug)]
  22 pub(crate) struct GenerationWorkerRequests {
  23     workers: Vec<WorkerRequests>,
  24 }
  25 
  26 impl GenerationWorkerRequests {
  27     pub(crate) fn new(worker_count: usize) -> Self {
  28         assert!(
  29             worker_count > 0,
  30             "a worker ledger needs at least one worker"
  31         );
  32         Self {
  33             workers: (0..worker_count)
  34                 .map(|_| WorkerRequests {
  35                     accepting_work: true,
  36                     in_flight: VecDeque::new(),
  37                 })
  38                 .collect(),
  39         }
  40     }
  41 
  42     /// Which worker owns a chunk.
  43     ///
  44     /// Deliberately not round-robin. Each worker keeps its own archive of
  45     /// what it has generated, and an archive only pays off if the chunk comes
  46     /// back to the worker holding it — round-robin would scatter a chunk
  47     /// across the pool and turn a 0.46 ms read into a 42 ms regeneration on
  48     /// (n-1)/n of re-requests.
  49     ///
  50     /// Hashing the coordinates rather than slicing the world into contiguous
  51     /// blocks is what keeps the pool balanced: a player standing anywhere has
  52     /// their surrounding chunks spread evenly across workers, where a
  53     /// block-per-worker split would leave one worker generating everything
  54     /// while the rest idled.
  55     pub(crate) fn preferred_worker(chunk: ChunkKey, worker_count: usize) -> usize {
  56         if worker_count <= 1 {
  57             return 0;
  58         }
  59         let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
  60         for word in [chunk.0 as u64, chunk.1 as u64] {
  61             for byte in word.to_le_bytes() {
  62                 h ^= byte as u64;
  63                 h = h.wrapping_mul(0x1000_0000_01b3);
  64             }
  65         }
  66         (h % worker_count as u64) as usize
  67     }
  68 
  69     /// Finds the next healthy worker, wrapping once from `start`.
  70     pub(crate) fn next_accepting(&self, start: usize) -> Option<usize> {
  71         (0..self.workers.len())
  72             .map(|offset| (start + offset) % self.workers.len())
  73             .find(|&index| self.workers[index].accepting_work)
  74     }
  75 
  76     pub(crate) fn assign(&mut self, worker_index: usize, request: ChunkRequest) {
  77         let worker = &mut self.workers[worker_index];
  78         debug_assert!(worker.accepting_work);
  79         worker.in_flight.push_back(request);
  80     }
  81 
  82     /// Retires only the exact request echoed by a well-formed worker reply.
  83     /// Unknown and stale replies leave all current work untouched.
  84     pub(crate) fn finish_exact(&mut self, worker_index: usize, echoed: &ChunkRequest) -> bool {
  85         self.take_exact(worker_index, echoed).is_some()
  86     }
  87 
  88     /// Retires an exact request reported as failed by the worker protocol.
  89     pub(crate) fn fail_exact(
  90         &mut self,
  91         worker_index: usize,
  92         echoed: &ChunkRequest,
  93     ) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
  94         self.take_exact(worker_index, echoed)
  95     }
  96 
  97     /// A worker processes its queue serially, so a malformed response belongs
  98     /// to its oldest outstanding request even when its envelope cannot be
  99     /// decoded far enough to recover an id.
 100     pub(crate) fn fail_oldest(&mut self, worker_index: usize) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
 101         self.workers[worker_index].in_flight.pop_front()
 102     }
 103 
 104     /// Stops scheduling to a broken worker and returns all work the engine
 105     /// must retry. Calling this more than once is harmless.
 106     pub(crate) fn disable_and_drain(&mut self, worker_index: usize) -> Vec<ChunkRequest> {
 107         let worker = &mut self.workers[worker_index];
 108         worker.accepting_work = false;
 109         worker.in_flight.drain(..).collect()
 110     }
 111 
 112     fn take_exact(&mut self, worker_index: usize, echoed: &ChunkRequest) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
 113         let queue = &mut self.workers[worker_index].in_flight;
 114         let position = queue
 115             .iter()
 116             .position(|request| request.is_same_request(echoed))?;
 117         queue.remove(position)
 118     }
 119 }

 127     #[test]
 128     fn a_chunk_always_goes_to_the_same_worker() {
 129         // The property the per-worker archive depends on: an evicted chunk
 130         // coming back into range must be routed to the worker that already
 131         // has it, or the archive never hits.
 132         for count in [1usize, 2, 3, 4, 8, 32] {
 133             for chunk in [(0i64, 0i64), (10, -40), (-1234, 5678), (i64::MIN, i64::MAX)] {
 134                 let first = GenerationWorkerRequests::preferred_worker(chunk, count);
 135                 assert_eq!(
 136                     first,
 137                     GenerationWorkerRequests::preferred_worker(chunk, count),
 138                     "routing for {chunk:?} across {count} workers was not stable"
 139                 );
 140                 assert!(first < count, "worker {first} is outside a pool of {count}");
 141             }
 142         }
 143     }

 145     #[test]

 147         // Affinity must not become a contiguous split: one worker owning the
 148         // area around the player would generate everything while the rest
 149         // idled, which is worse than round-robin.
 150         let count = 4;
 151         let mut used = [0usize; 4];
 152         for z in -6..6i64 {
 153             for x in -6..6i64 {
 154                 used[GenerationWorkerRequests::preferred_worker((x, z), count)] += 1;
 155             }
 156         }
 157         let total: usize = used.iter().sum();

 166         }

   1 //! Web Worker chunk source — the multithreaded [`ChunkSourcePort`].
   2 //!
   3 //! Each worker (`static/worker.js`) is a second instance of this same wasm
   4 //! module running on its own OS thread. The main thread posts small
   5 //! `{gen, requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality}` messages
   6 //! round-robin. Workers always generate, bake, build the collision SVO, and
   7 //! extract collision; the artifact bitfield requests only the active
   8 //! renderer's mesh, face, or serialized-node products. One encoded byte
   9 //! buffer returns through `adapters::chunk_codec`; GPU resources remain owned
  10 //! by the main-thread render driver. Healthy pools keep generation off the
  11 //! frame loop. If every worker fatally fails, the driver uses its same-thread
  12 //! source as a correctness fallback instead of leaving the world pending.
  13 //!
  14 //! Stale-result rejection lives in the engine (`install_completed`), keyed
  15 //! by the echoed request. This driver owns transport failure detection and
  16 //! reports exact failed requests through the same application port.
  17 
  18 use std::cell::RefCell;
  19 use std::rc::Rc;
  20 
  21 use js_sys::{ArrayBuffer, Reflect, Uint8Array};
  22 use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
  23 use web_sys::{MessageEvent, Worker, WorkerOptions, WorkerType};
  24 
  25 use crate::adapters::chunk_codec::decode_chunk_payload;
  26 use crate::adapters::local_chunk_source::LocalChunkSource;
  27 use crate::application::generation_worker_policy::MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS;
  28 use crate::application::ports::{
  29     ChunkPayload, ChunkRequest, ChunkSourcePort, CompletedChunk, RenderArtifactNeeds,
  30 };
  31 use crate::application::streaming::chunk_key;
  32 use crate::drivers::generation_worker_requests::GenerationWorkerRequests;
  33 use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
  34 use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
  35 
  36 pub struct WorkerChunkSource {
  37     workers: Vec<Worker>,
  38     completed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<CompletedChunk>>>,
  39     failed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<ChunkRequest>>>,
  40     requests: Rc<RefCell<GenerationWorkerRequests>>,
  41     /// Keeps browser callbacks alive for the workers' lifetime.
  42     _message_handlers: Vec<Closure<dyn FnMut(MessageEvent)>>,
  43     _error_handlers: Vec<Closure<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Event)>>,
  44     /// Same-thread source for the synchronous [`ChunkSourcePort::load`]
  45     /// contract and as a last-resort recovery if every worker has failed.
  46     fallback: LocalChunkSource<SimpleNoiseProvider>,
  47     reported_emergency_fallback: bool,
  48 }
  49 
  50 impl WorkerChunkSource {
  51     /// Spawns the pool and hands every worker the URL query, so main thread
  52     /// and workers derive the identical generator configuration.
  53     pub fn new(query: &str, default_seed: u32, pool_size: usize) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
  54         if !(1..=usize::from(MAX_GENERATION_WORKERS)).contains(&pool_size) {
  55             return Err(JsValue::from_str(
  56                 "generation worker pool size must be 1..=32",
  57             ));
  58         }
  59 
  60         let completed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<CompletedChunk>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
  61         let failed: Rc<RefCell<Vec<ChunkRequest>>> = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));
  62         let requests = Rc::new(RefCell::new(GenerationWorkerRequests::new(pool_size)));
  63         // The single-file bundle (scripts/build-single-file.mjs) has no
  64         // sibling worker.js on disk; it publishes a blob: URL for the inlined
  65         // worker script on the global scope instead.
  66         let script_url = Reflect::get(&js_sys::global(), &"__VACKROOMS_WORKER_URL__".into())
  67             .ok()
  68             .and_then(|value| value.as_string())
  69             .unwrap_or_else(|| "worker.js".to_string());
  70         let mut workers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
  71         let mut message_handlers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
  72         let mut error_handlers = Vec::with_capacity(pool_size);
  73         for worker_index in 0..pool_size {
  74             let options = WorkerOptions::new();
  75             options.set_type(WorkerType::Module);
  76             // Relative (not `/worker.js`): resolved against the document's
  77             // URL, so this still finds the sibling file when the site is
  78             // served from a subpath (e.g. a GitHub Pages project page at
  79             // `<user>.github.io/<repo>/`) instead of the domain root.
  80             let worker = Worker::new_with_options(&script_url, &options)?;
  81 
  82             let completed_sink = completed.clone();
  83             let failed_sink = failed.clone();
  84             let message_requests = requests.clone();
  85             let worker_for_fatal_reply = worker.clone();
  86             let handler = Closure::<dyn FnMut(MessageEvent)>::new(move |event: MessageEvent| {
  87                 match parse_worker_reply(&event) {
  88                     WorkerReply::Completed(done) => {
  89                         if message_requests
  90                             .borrow_mut()
  91                             .finish_exact(worker_index, &done.request)
  92                         {
  93                             completed_sink.borrow_mut().push(done);
  94                         }
  95                     }
  96                     WorkerReply::Failed(echoed) => {
  97                         if let Some(failed_request) = message_requests
  98                             .borrow_mut()
  99                             .fail_exact(worker_index, &echoed)
 100                         {
 101                             failed_sink.borrow_mut().push(failed_request);
 102                         }
 103                     }
 104                     WorkerReply::Fatal => {
 105                         let abandoned = message_requests
 106                             .borrow_mut()
 107                             .disable_and_drain(worker_index);
 108                         failed_sink.borrow_mut().extend(abandoned);
 109                         worker_for_fatal_reply.terminate();
 110                     }
 111                     WorkerReply::Malformed => {
 112                         if let Some(failed_request) =
 113                             message_requests.borrow_mut().fail_oldest(worker_index)
 114                         {
 115                             failed_sink.borrow_mut().push(failed_request);
 116                         }
 117                     }
 118                 }
 119             });
 120             worker.set_onmessage(Some(handler.as_ref().unchecked_ref()));
 121 
 122             let failed_sink = failed.clone();
 123             let error_requests = requests.clone();
 124             let worker_for_error = worker.clone();
 125             let error_handler = Closure::<dyn FnMut(web_sys::Event)>::new(move |_event| {
 126                 let abandoned = error_requests.borrow_mut().disable_and_drain(worker_index);
 127                 failed_sink.borrow_mut().extend(abandoned);
 128                 worker_for_error.terminate();
 129             });
 130             worker.set_onerror(Some(error_handler.as_ref().unchecked_ref()));
 131 
 132             let init = js_sys::Object::new();
 133             Reflect::set(&init, &"type".into(), &"init".into())?;
 134             Reflect::set(&init, &"query".into(), &query.into())?;
 135             Reflect::set(&init, &"seed".into(), &(default_seed as f64).into())?;
 136             worker.post_message(&init)?;
 137 
 138             workers.push(worker);
 139             message_handlers.push(handler);
 140             error_handlers.push(error_handler);
 141         }
 142 
 143         let (seed, config) =
 144             crate::adapters::query_config::generator_setup_from_query(query, default_seed);
 145         Ok(Self {
 146             workers,
 147             completed,
 148             failed,
 149             requests,
 150             _message_handlers: message_handlers,
 151             _error_handlers: error_handlers,
 152             fallback: LocalChunkSource::new(SimpleNoiseProvider::new(), seed, config),
 153             reported_emergency_fallback: false,
 154         })
 155     }
 156 
 157     pub fn pool_size(&self) -> usize {
 158         self.workers.len()
 159     }
 160 }
 161

 179     fn load_with_artifacts(
 180         &self,
 181         origin_x: f32,
 182         origin_z: f32,
 183         level: u32,
 184         lod: u8,
 185         reality: &RealitySnapshot,
 186         artifacts: RenderArtifactNeeds,

 188         self.fallback
 189             .load_with_artifacts(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, reality, artifacts)
 190     }
 191 
 192     fn is_async(&self) -> bool {
 193         true
 194     }
 195 
 196     fn max_concurrent_requests(&self) -> usize {
 197         self.pool_size()
 198     }
 199 
 200     fn request(&mut self, request: ChunkRequest) {
 201         // Route by chunk, not round-robin: each worker archives what it
 202         // generates, so a chunk evicted from the rolling window and later
 203         // wanted again must come back to the worker already holding it.
 204         // `next_accepting` still falls through to any healthy worker, so
 205         // affinity is a preference and never a way to strand a request on a
 206         // dead worker.
 207         let preferred = GenerationWorkerRequests::preferred_worker(
 208             chunk_key(request.origin_x, request.origin_z),
 209             self.workers.len(),
 210         );
 211         let worker_index = self.requests.borrow().next_accepting(preferred);
 212         let Some(worker_index) = worker_index else {
 213             // Fatal worker startup/runtime failures must not strand streaming.
 214             // This path is deliberately exceptional: the healthy path always
 215             // generates off-thread, while an exhausted pool favors a complete
 216             // world over a permanently pending chunk.
 217             if !self.reported_emergency_fallback {
 218                 web_sys::console::warn_1(
 219                     &"generation worker pool failed; using same-thread recovery".into(),
 220                 );
 221                 self.reported_emergency_fallback = true;
 222             }
 223             let payload = self.fallback.load_with_artifacts(
 224                 request.origin_x,
 225                 request.origin_z,
 226                 request.level,
 227                 request.lod,
 228                 &request.reality,
 229                 request.artifacts,
 230             );
 231             self.completed
 232                 .borrow_mut()
 233                 .push(CompletedChunk { request, payload });
 234             return;
 235         };
 236 
 237         let message = js_sys::Object::new();
 238         let set = |k: &str, v: JsValue| {
 239             let _ = Reflect::set(&message, &k.into(), &v);
 240         };
 241         set("type", "gen".into());
 242         set("requestId", (request.request_id as f64).into());
 243         set("ox", (request.origin_x as f64).into());
 244         set("oz", (request.origin_z as f64).into());
 245         set("level", (request.level as f64).into());
 246         set("lod", (request.lod as f64).into());
 247         set("artifacts", (request.artifacts.bits() as f64).into());
 248         let reality_words = request.reality.to_words();
 249         let reality = js_sys::Uint32Array::from(reality_words.as_slice());
 250         set("reality", reality.into());
 251         let worker = &self.workers[worker_index];
 252         self.requests
 253             .borrow_mut()
 254             .assign(worker_index, request.clone());
 255         if let Err(error) = worker.post_message(&message) {
 256             // A synchronous send failure means this worker can no longer be
 257             // trusted with its already queued requests. Retire all of them;
 258             // the engine will validate their ids and retry on healthy slots.
 259             let abandoned = self.requests.borrow_mut().disable_and_drain(worker_index);
 260             self.failed.borrow_mut().extend(abandoned);
 261             worker.terminate();
 262             web_sys::console::warn_2(
 263                 &"generation worker postMessage failed; disabling worker:".into(),
 264                 &error,
 265             );
 266         }
 267     }
 268 
 269     fn poll_completed(&mut self) -> Vec<CompletedChunk> {
 270         std::mem::take(&mut *self.completed.borrow_mut())
 271     }
 272 
 273     fn poll_failed_requests(&mut self) -> Vec<ChunkRequest> {
 274         std::mem::take(&mut *self.failed.borrow_mut())
 275     }
 276 }
 277 
 278 enum WorkerReply {
 279     Completed(CompletedChunk),
 280     Failed(ChunkRequest),
 281     Fatal,
 282     Malformed,
 283 }
 284 
 285 /// Decodes the deliberately small worker protocol. Malformed replies are a
 286 /// first-class outcome: the worker queue is serial, so the caller can fail its
 287 /// oldest assigned request instead of leaving that chunk pending forever.
 288 fn parse_worker_reply(event: &MessageEvent) -> WorkerReply {
 289     let data = event.data();
 290     let message_type = Reflect::get(&data, &"type".into())
 291         .ok()
 292         .and_then(|value| value.as_string());
 293     match message_type.as_deref() {
 294         Some("done") => parse_request(&data)
 295             .and_then(|request| {
 296                 parse_payload(&data).map(|payload| CompletedChunk { request, payload })
 297             })
 298             .map(WorkerReply::Completed)
 299             .unwrap_or(WorkerReply::Malformed),
 300         Some("failed") => parse_request(&data)
 301             .map(WorkerReply::Failed)
 302             .unwrap_or(WorkerReply::Malformed),
 303         Some("fatal") => WorkerReply::Fatal,
 304         _ => WorkerReply::Malformed,
 305     }
 306 }
 307 
 308 fn parse_request(data: &JsValue) -> Option<ChunkRequest> {
 309     let field = |name: &str| Reflect::get(data, &name.into()).ok();
 310     Some(ChunkRequest {
 311         request_id: exact_u32(field("requestId")?)?,
 312         origin_x: finite_f32(field("ox")?)?,
 313         origin_z: finite_f32(field("oz")?)?,
 314         level: exact_u32(field("level")?)?,
 315         lod: u8::try_from(exact_u32(field("lod")?)?).ok()?,
 316         artifacts: RenderArtifactNeeds::from_bits(
 317             u8::try_from(exact_u32(field("artifacts")?)?).ok()?,
 318         )?,
 319         reality: {
 320             let encoded = field("reality")?;
 321             let words = encoded.dyn_into::<js_sys::Uint32Array>().ok()?.to_vec();
 322             RealitySnapshot::from_words(&words).ok()?
 323         },
 324     })
 325 }
 326 
 327 fn parse_payload(data: &JsValue) -> Option<ChunkPayload> {
 328     let buffer: ArrayBuffer = Reflect::get(data, &"buf".into()).ok()?.dyn_into().ok()?;
 329     let bytes = Uint8Array::new(&buffer).to_vec();
 330     decode_chunk_payload(&bytes)
 331 }
 332 
 333 fn exact_u32(value: JsValue) -> Option<u32> {
 334     let number = value.as_f64()?;
 335     (number.is_finite() && number.fract() == 0.0 && (0.0..=f64::from(u32::MAX)).contains(&number))
 336         .then_some(number as u32)
 337 }
 338 
 339 fn finite_f32(value: JsValue) -> Option<f32> {
 340     let number = value.as_f64()?;
 341     let narrowed = number as f32;
 342     (number.is_finite() && narrowed.is_finite()).then_some(narrowed)
 343 }

worker_source.rs confirmed. Key observations:

1. **Re-entrancy hazard (line 200-267)**: `request()` is called from engine tick, message handlers from JS event loop. Both `borrow_mut()` the same `RefCell<GenerationWorkerRequests>`. On a single-threaded JS event loop these never interleave — but the engine tick itself is invoked from within a rAF callback; could a worker message event fire *during* the engine tick? No — JS is single-threaded; events only dispatch between call stack completions. So no re-entrancy within a tick. Safe.

2. **Engine-side pending dropped but worker ledger keeps in-flight (issue_requests retain at engine.rs:916-917)**: when pending entries are dropped because chunk left footprint, the worker ledger still holds in-flight requests. When the reply arrives, `finish_exact` matches and pushes to completed; engine discards via keep check at install_completed:866. OK. But if the engine re-requests the same chunk while the old request is still in-flight at the worker (pending dropped by the retain at 916), a NEW request is posted with a different request_id; the worker has two entries in its queue for the same chunk; both get processed; the old reply is dropped by is_same_request check. Correct but wasted work. Minor.

3. **`WorkerReply::Fatal` (line 104-110)**: `disable_and_drain` + terminate. But: if the worker had *queued* (in-flight ledger) requests that were processed before the fatal... The drain returns everything in the ledger, including ones that may complete later — they're retried by the engine, fine.

4. **Worker-side archive cross-level bug** is the big one.

Now let me check the worker.js file and lib.rs (atomics + worker_entry). Then ports.rs, body.rs, navigation.rs, player.rs, survival_inventory.rs, peripheral_shift.rs, noclip.rs, route.rs, rendering/mod.rs, camera.rs, mod.rs.
   1 // Generation worker: a second instance of the same wasm module, producing
   2 // renderer-selected chunk artifacts off the main thread. The handler is
   3 // registered synchronously at module scope so no message can be lost while
   4 // the wasm module is still instantiating; work is serialized through a
   5 // promise chain.
   6 //
   7 // Protocol (main -> worker):
   8 //   { type: "init", query, seed }        one-time generator setup
   9 //   { type: "gen", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality }
  10 //                   one chunk order; artifacts is a u8 bitfield and reality
  11 //                   is Uint32Array
  12 // (worker -> main):
  13 //   { type: "done", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality, ms, buf }
  14 //                                   buf transferred, encoded by chunk_codec
  15 //   { type: "failed", requestId, ox, oz, level, lod, artifacts, reality, message }
  16 //                                   one request failed and may be retried
  17 //   { type: "fatal", message }      worker initialization failed
  18 import init, { worker_init, worker_generate } from "./pkg/wasm_frontend.js";
  19 
  20 let wasmReady = null;
  21 function ensureWasm() {
  22   if (!wasmReady) wasmReady = init();
  23   return wasmReady;
  24 }
  25 
  26 let queue = Promise.resolve();
  27 
  28 function errorMessage(error) {
  29   if (error instanceof Error) return error.message;
  30   return String(error);
  31 }
  32 
  33 function reportFailure(message, error) {
  34   const description = errorMessage(error);
  35   console.error("[WORKER] generation failure:", description);
  36   try {
  37     if (message?.type === "gen") {
  38       postMessage({
  39         type: "failed",
  40         requestId: message.requestId,
  41         ox: message.ox,
  42         oz: message.oz,
  43         level: message.level,
  44         lod: message.lod,
  45         artifacts: message.artifacts,
  46         reality: new Uint32Array(message.reality),
  47         message: description,
  48       });
  49     } else {
  50       postMessage({ type: "fatal", message: description });
  51     }
  52   } catch (reportError) {
  53     // The browser's Worker error event is the final recovery path when even
  54     // the structured failure message cannot be cloned or delivered.
  55     console.error("[WORKER] could not report generation failure:", reportError);
  56   }
  57 }
  58 
  59 async function processMessage(message) {
  60   await ensureWasm();
  61   if (message.type === "init") {
  62     worker_init(message.query, message.seed >>> 0);
  63     return;
  64   }
  65   if (message.type !== "gen") return;
  66 
  67   const t0 = performance.now();
  68   const reality = new Uint32Array(message.reality);
  69   const bytes = worker_generate(
  70     message.requestId >>> 0,
  71     message.ox,
  72     message.oz,
  73     message.level,
  74     message.lod,
  75     message.artifacts >>> 0,
  76     reality
  77   );
  78   const ms = performance.now() - t0;
  79   console.debug(
  80     `[WORKER] chunk (${message.ox}, ${message.oz}) lod ${message.lod} generated in ${ms.toFixed(1)} ms`
  81   );
  82   postMessage(
  83     {
  84       type: "done",
  85       requestId: message.requestId,
  86       ox: message.ox,
  87       oz: message.oz,
  88       level: message.level,
  89       lod: message.lod,
  90       artifacts: message.artifacts,
  91       reality,
  92       ms,
  93       buf: bytes.buffer,
  94     },
  95     [bytes.buffer]
  96   );
  97 }
  98 
  99 onmessage = (event) => {
 100   const message = event.data;
 101   // Catch each queue item independently. A failed request must not leave the
 102   // promise chain rejected, which would silently skip every later request.
 103   queue = queue
 104     .then(() => processMessage(message))
 105     .catch((error) => reportFailure(message, error));
 106 };

worker.js confirmed. Note: the init message arrives BEFORE any gen messages (posted at WorkerChunkSource::new, lines 132-136 of worker_source.rs), so worker_init runs first. But actually — the promise chain: init message is posted right after worker creation; the worker's onmessage handler is registered at module scope. `ensureWasm()` in each processMessage — for init, it awaits wasm init, then worker_init. gen messages queue behind. Good ordering.

One subtle thing: `worker_generate` is called without checking worker_init completed — but since the promise chain is serialized and init is posted before gen messages... but wait: what if a gen message arrives at the worker *before* init (e.g., worker.post_message init at line 136, then the engine immediately requests)? Message ordering to the same worker is guaranteed (FIFO per port). So init is always first. Good.

Now, a REAL subtle race: the init message is posted in `WorkerChunkSource::new` BEFORE the worker has loaded its script and registered onmessage. Messages posted to a worker before the script is evaluated are queued by the browser and delivered after. So no loss. Good.

 275 #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
 276 #[wasm_bindgen::prelude::wasm_bindgen]
 277 pub fn get_blueprint_svg(seed: u32, rx: i32, rz: i32, voxel_scale: f32, size_world: f32) -> String {
 278     let noise = vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 279     let plan = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::generate_region_plan(
 280         seed,
 281         vackrooms::domain::entities::position::Position::new(
 282             rx as f32 * size_world,
 283             rz as f32 * size_world,
 284         ),
 285         size_world,
 286         &vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec(),
 287         &noise,
 288     );
 289     let chunk_size = if voxel_scale <= 0.1 { 20.0 } else { 10.0 };
 290     let mut chunk_bounds = Vec::new();
 291     let steps = (size_world / chunk_size).round() as i32;
 292     for i in 0..steps {
 293         for j in 0..steps {
 294             let min_x = rx as f32 * size_world + i as f32 * chunk_size;
 295             let min_z = rz as f32 * size_world + j as f32 * chunk_size;
 296             let chunk_coord_x = (min_x / chunk_size).round() as i64;
 297             let chunk_coord_z = (min_z / chunk_size).round() as i64;
 298             chunk_bounds.push(vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::ChunkBounds {
 299                 min_x,
 300                 min_z,
 301                 max_x: min_x + chunk_size,
 302                 max_z: min_z + chunk_size,
 303                 label: format!("[{}, {}]", chunk_coord_x, chunk_coord_z),
 304             });
 305         }
 306     }
 307 
 308     let options = vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::BlueprintOptions {
 309         pixels_per_unit: 10.0,
 310         show_chunk_grid: true,
 311         show_fixtures: true,
 312         show_structure: true,
 313         seed,
 314         level: 0,
 315         voxel_scale,
 316     };
 317     vackrooms::adapters::blueprint_renderer::render_region_blueprint_svg(
 318         &plan,
 319         &chunk_bounds,
 320         options,
 321     )
 322 }

 329 pub fn get_debug_region_json(seed: u32, region_x: i32, region_z: i32) -> String {

 331     use vackrooms::domain::entities::architecture::SpaceProgram;

 333     let noise = vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
 334     let size = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::REGION_SIZE;
 335     let origin = vackrooms::domain::entities::position::Position::new(
 336         region_x as f32 * size,
 337         region_z as f32 * size,
 338     );
 339     let config = vackrooms::use_cases::generate_chunk::GeneratorConfig::low_spec();
 340     let plan = vackrooms::use_cases::region_plan::generate_region_plan(
 341         seed, origin, size, &config, &noise,
 342     );
 343     let mut out = String::with_capacity(8192);
 344     write!(
 345         out,
 346         "{{\"origin\":[{:.1},{:.1}],\"size\":{:.1},\"walls\":[",
 347         origin.x, origin.z, size
 348     )
 349     .unwrap();
 350     let mut first = true;
 351     for assembly in &plan.assemblies {
 352         let vertices = &assembly.footprint.vertices;
 353         for pair in vertices
 354             .iter()
 355             .zip(vertices.iter().cycle().skip(1))
 356             .take(vertices.len())
 357         {
 358             if !first {
 359                 out.push(',');
 360             }
 361             first = false;
 362             write!(
 363                 out,
 364                 "[{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1}]",
 365                 pair.0.0, pair.0.1, pair.1.0, pair.1.1
 366             )
 367             .unwrap();
 368         }
 369     }
 370     out.push_str("],\"corridors\":[");
 371     first = true;
 372     for corridor in &plan.corridors {
 373         for pair in corridor.path.windows(2) {
 374             if !first {
 375                 out.push(',');
 376             }
 377             first = false;
 378             write!(
 379                 out,
 380                 "[{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1}]",
 381                 pair[0].x, pair[0].z, pair[1].x, pair[1].z, corridor.width
 382             )
 383             .unwrap();
 384         }
 385     }
 386     out.push_str("],\"lights\":[");
 387     first = true;
 388     for assembly in &plan.assemblies {
 389         for fixture in &assembly.fixtures {
 390             if !first {
 391                 out.push(',');
 392             }
 393             first = false;
 394             write!(
 395                 out,
 396                 "[{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{}]",
 397                 fixture.at.x, fixture.at.z, fixture.half_x, fixture.half_z, fixture.lit
 398             )
 399             .unwrap();
 400         }
 401     }
 402     out.push_str("],\"rooms\":[");
 403     first = true;
 404     for assembly in &plan.assemblies {
 405         let b = assembly.footprint.bounds();
 406         if !first {
 407             out.push(',');
 408         }
 409         first = false;
 410         let kind = match assembly.program {
 411             SpaceProgram::MainCorridor => "corridor",
 412             SpaceProgram::AbandonedExpansion => "abandoned",
 413             _ => "room",
 414         };
 415         write!(
 416             out,
 417             "[{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},\"{}\"]",
 418             b.0, b.1, b.2, b.3, kind
 419         )
 420         .unwrap();
 421     }
 422     out.push_str("],\"anomalies\":[");
 423     first = true;
 424     for anomaly in &plan.anomalies {
 425         if !first {
 426             out.push(',');
 427         }
 428         first = false;
 429         let b = anomaly.footprint.bounds();
 430         write!(
 431             out,
 432             "[\"{:?}\",\"{:016x}\",{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{:.1},{}]",
 433             anomaly.kind,
 434             anomaly.id,
 435             b.min_x,
 436             b.min_z,
 437             b.max_x,
 438             b.max_z,
 439             anomaly.gates.len(),
 440         )
 441         .unwrap();
 442     }
 443     out.push_str("]}");
 444     out
 445 }

 451 pub fn get_debug_chunk_json(seed: u32, chunk_x: f32, chunk_z: f32, voxel_scale: f32) -> String {
 452     use std::fmt::Write;
 453     use vackrooms::domain::entities::architecture::SpaceProgram;
 454     use vackrooms::domain::entities::voxel_grid::{
 455         VOXEL_CEILING, VOXEL_DAMAGED_WALL, VOXEL_DEEP_CARPET, VOXEL_DRY_CARPET, VOXEL_FLOOR,
 456         VOXEL_FLUID, VOXEL_GLIMMER, VOXEL_GRASS, VOXEL_LIGHT, VOXEL_PALE_WALL, VOXEL_RED_LIGHT,
 457         VOXEL_RED_WALL, VOXEL_STICKY_CARPET, VOXEL_TREE, VOXEL_WALL, VOXEL_WATER,
 458     };
 459 
 460     let noise = vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider::new();
1000 
1001     /// Composition root. Runs automatically when the wasm module is
1002     /// instantiated by `static/index.html`.
1003     ///
1004     /// `static/worker.js` instantiates this same module inside a Web Worker
1005     /// with `#[wasm_bindgen(start)]` skipped (`init` is passed
1006     /// `{ skip_start: true }` is not available for start fns, so instead the
1007     /// worker checks for a missing DOM and bails out here).
1008     #[wasm_bindgen(start)]
1009     pub fn start() -> Result<(), JsValue> {
1010         console_error_panic_hook::set_once();
1011         // Inside a Web Worker there is no `window`/DOM: this module was
1012         // loaded as the generation worker, which drives itself through
1013         // `worker_init`/`worker_generate` instead of `boot`.
1014         if web_sys::window().is_none() {
1015             return Ok(());
1016         }
1017         // A page that wants to choose its world before one is built sets
1018         // `__VACKROOMS_DEFER_BOOT__` before importing this module, then calls
1019         // `boot_world()` once the player has picked a seed. Booting here
1020         // regardless would generate one world and immediately throw it away —
1021         // and, worse, would read a `location.search` the setup screen has not
1022         // written yet, so the main thread and its generation workers could
1023         // disagree about which world this is.
1024         //
1025         // The flag is opt-in so every other entry point (the debug map, a
1026         // shared link, the capture harness) keeps booting on load exactly as
1027         // before.
1028         if boot_deferred() {
1029             return Ok(());
1030         }
1031         spawn_boot();
1032         Ok(())
1033     }
1034 
1035     fn boot_deferred() -> bool {
1036         js_sys::Reflect::get(&js_sys::global(), &"__VACKROOMS_DEFER_BOOT__".into())
1037             .ok()
1038             .and_then(|value| value.as_bool())
1039             .unwrap_or(false)
1040     }
1041 
1042     /// Starts the engine against whatever world the URL now describes.
1043     ///
1044     /// The setup screen writes its seed and sliders into `location.search`
1045     /// and then calls this. Everything downstream — the composition root and
1046     /// every generation worker — reads that same query string, so choosing a
1047     /// world costs no new configuration plumbing and the resulting URL is a
1048     /// shareable reproduction for free.
1049     ///
1050     /// Safe to call more than once only in the sense that it will not panic;
1051     /// the caller is expected to invoke it once, when the player commits.
1052     #[wasm_bindgen]
1053     pub fn boot_world() {
1054         spawn_boot();
1055     }
1056 
1057     /// Adapter/device acquisition is asynchronous in WebGPU. Keep the callers
1058     /// synchronous and let the composition root own the future; failures are
1059     /// surfaced both in the console and the loading HUD.
1060     fn spawn_boot() {
1061         wasm_bindgen_futures::spawn_local(async {
1062             if let Err(error) = crate::drivers::browser::boot().await {
1063                 web_sys::console::error_2(&"Failed to start WebGPU engine:".into(), &error);
1064                 if let Some(document) = web_sys::window().and_then(|window| window.document()) {
1065                     if let Some(status) = document.get_element_by_id("status-msg") {
1066                         let detail = error.as_string().unwrap_or_else(|| format!("{error:?}"));
1067                         status.set_text_content(Some(&format!(
1068                             "Failed to start WebGPU engine: {detail}"
1069                         )));
1070                     }
1071                 }
1072             }
1073         });
1074     }
1075 }
1076 
1077 /// Generation-worker entry points. A worker is a second instance of this
1078 /// same wasm module: `worker_init` builds a chunk source from the *same*
1079 /// URL query the main thread used (identical world by construction), and
1080 /// `worker_generate` runs architectural generation, lighting, the
1081 /// collision-authority SVO, and only the renderer artifacts named by the
1082 /// request bitfield. It returns one transferable byte buffer (see
1083 /// `adapters::chunk_codec`).
1084 #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]
1085 mod worker_entry {
1086     use std::cell::RefCell;
1087 
1088     use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
1089 
1090     use crate::adapters::archived_chunk_source::ArchivedChunkSource;
1091     use crate::adapters::chunk_codec::encode_chunk_payload;
1092     use crate::adapters::query_config::{generator_setup_from_query, surfel_density_from_query};
1093     use crate::application::chunk_archive::MemoryStorage;
1094     use crate::application::ports::{ChunkSourcePort, RenderArtifactNeeds};
1095     use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::RealitySnapshot;
1096     use vackrooms::frameworks_drivers::simple_noise::SimpleNoiseProvider;
1097 
1098     thread_local! {
1099         static SOURCE: RefCell<Option<ArchivedChunkSource<SimpleNoiseProvider>>> =
1100             const { RefCell::new(None) };
1101     }
1102 
1103     /// Per-worker archive ceiling, bytes.
1104     ///
1105     /// The pool shards the world by chunk affinity, so each worker archives
1106     /// roughly `1/n` of what the player visits and the pool's total stays near
1107     /// this figure however many workers there are. 32 MB is a few thousand
1108     /// coarse chunks — comfortably more than a rolling window holds, so
1109     /// pacing an area never empties it.
1110     const WORKER_ARCHIVE_BYTES: u64 = 32 * 1024 * 1024;
1111 
1112     /// `default_seed` must match the main thread's `WORLD_SEED`.
1113     #[wasm_bindgen]
1114     pub fn worker_init(query: &str, default_seed: u32) {
1115         let (seed, config) = generator_setup_from_query(query, default_seed);
1116         // In-memory for now: OPFS would make this outlive the tab, but even
1117         // held in the worker's own heap the archive is what makes the rolling
1118         // window cheap. A chunk evicted when the player turned away and
1119         // wanted again a moment later is a 0.46 ms decode instead of a 42 ms
1120         // regeneration, and the worker it comes back to is the one holding it
1121         // because the pool routes by chunk affinity.
1122         //
1123         // `generator_id` is the query string's own hash: it changes whenever
1124         // any world parameter does, which is exactly when archived geometry
1125         // stops being valid. It does *not* change when the generator's code
1126         // changes — a worker is rebuilt with the wasm module, so a code change
1127         // replaces the archive along with everything else. A persistent
1128         // archive would have to fold in a build hash.
1129         let generator_id = fnv64(query.as_bytes());
1130         SOURCE.with(|s| {
1131             *s.borrow_mut() = Some(ArchivedChunkSource::with_budget(
1132                 SimpleNoiseProvider::new(),
1133                 seed,
1134                 config,
1135                 Box::new(MemoryStorage::new()),
1136                 generator_id,
1137                 WORKER_ARCHIVE_BYTES,
1138             )
1139             // Extraction happens here, not on the main thread, so the surfel
1140             // density has to be read from the query on this side of the
1141             // worker boundary too.
1142             .with_surfel_density(surfel_density_from_query(query)));
1143         });
1144     }
1145 
1146     fn fnv64(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64 {
1147         let mut h: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
1148         for &byte in bytes {
1149             h ^= byte as u64;
1150             h = h.wrapping_mul(0x1000_0000_01b3);
1151         }
1152         h
1153     }
1154 
1155     #[wasm_bindgen]
1156     pub fn worker_generate(
1157         _request_id: u32,
1158         origin_x: f32,
1159         origin_z: f32,
1160         level: u32,
1161         lod: u8,
1162         artifact_bits: u8,
1163         reality_words: Vec<u32>,
1164     ) -> Vec<u8> {
1165         let artifacts = RenderArtifactNeeds::from_bits(artifact_bits)
1166             .expect("worker_generate received invalid artifact bits");
1167         let reality = RealitySnapshot::from_words(&reality_words)
1168             .expect("worker_generate received an invalid reality snapshot");
1169         SOURCE.with(|s| {
1170             let source = s.borrow();
1171             let source = source
1172                 .as_ref()
1173                 .expect("worker_generate called before worker_init");
1174             encode_chunk_payload(
1175                 &source.load_with_artifacts(origin_x, origin_z, level, lod, &reality, artifacts),
1176             )
1177         })
1178     }
1179 }

lib.rs worker_entry confirmed:
- `worker_init` (1113-1144): builds `ArchivedChunkSource` with `config` from the URL query — `config.level` is the query's level (boot level). The `ArchiveIdentity` includes `config.level`.
- `worker_generate` (1155-1178): passes `level` from the message into `load_with_artifacts` → `fetch` → `RecordKey::new(chunk, lod, artifacts, reality)` — NO level → cross-level cache collision confirmed.

This is Critical: when the engine switches level at runtime (door from level 0 to level 1, or noclip to level 34 and back), chunks at the same world coordinates + same LOD + same reality hash hit the wrong level's archived record in the worker. In the typical door case: player spawns at (5,5) → chunk (0,0) level 0 generated and archived in worker. Crosses door → switch_level(1) → arrival (3,3) → chunk (0,0) level 1 requested → worker archive serves level-0 record → Level-1 world never loads (until the archive is cleared by budget or reality changes — reality does change with gate crossings which change the hash).

Wait — one caveat: `reality` for the level-1 request — RealitySnapshot is not reset on switch_level (confirmed in engine.rs switch_level: no reality reset). But the delirium/strain may differ. The initial request after door transit will have the SAME reality as the level-0 generation (assuming no gate crossings in between) → direct hit. Actually the level-0 chunk (0,0) was generated at spawn with default reality. The player walks through a door — crossing the door doesn't advance reality (gates advance reality; doors don't). So yes, same reality hash → hit → wrong level payload. CONFIRMED CRITICAL.

Also note the second-order effect: even without a level switch, any `level` variation would break; but engine always requests with self.level, so only level switches matter.

Another subtlety in worker_init: the query-level archive identity is level N; if the engine later requests level M chunks, the fetch key doesn't include level so records mix. Confirmed.

 604 pub struct ChunkRequest {
 605     /// Monotonic identity assigned by the engine. A completion may only
 606     /// clear the pending entry carrying this exact id; this prevents a late
 607     /// result from an evicted/re-requested chunk from cancelling newer work.

 623     /// compare by bits so this remains an identity operation rather than an
 624     /// approximate spatial comparison.

 626         self.request_id == other.request_id
 627             && self.origin_x.to_bits() == other.origin_x.to_bits()
 628             && self.origin_z.to_bits() == other.origin_z.to_bits()
 629             && self.level == other.level
 630             && self.lod == other.lod
 631             && self.artifacts == other.artifacts
 632             && self.reality == other.reality
 633     }
