   1 //! The navigation-objective mechanic: which resident level exit the HUD's
   2 //! route needle points at, reselected on a bounded cadence and invalidated
   3 //! on level/reality transitions. Thin — `navigation.rs` owns the actual
   4 //! selection/bearing math; this module is only the engine-state glue around
   5 //! it. A child module of `engine`; see `presenter.rs` for why that gives it
   6 //! access to `Engine`'s private fields.
   7 
   8 use crate::application::navigation::{range_m, relative_bearing_deg, select_route_target};
   9 
  10 use super::{Engine, ROUTE_RECOMPUTE_PERIOD_S, RouteAnchor};
  11 
  12 impl Engine {
  13     /// Drops the cached navigation objective; the next tick reselects from
  14     /// whatever the *current* level/reality has resident. Called on level
  15     /// switches, reality transitions, and death so telemetry never crosses
  16     /// a reality address.
  17     pub(super) fn invalidate_route(&mut self) {
  18         self.route_target = None;
  19         self.route_cooldown = 0.0;
  20     }
  21 
  22     /// Reselects the route objective on a bounded cadence from the resident
  23     /// level exits — authoritative generator output, never invented. No
  24     /// resident door means no route, truthfully.
  25     pub(super) fn update_route(&mut self, dt: f32) {
  26         self.route_cooldown -= dt;
  27         if self.route_cooldown > 0.0 {
  28             return;
  29         }
  30         self.route_cooldown = ROUTE_RECOMPUTE_PERIOD_S;
  31         let player = [self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]];
  32         let selected = select_route_target(self.store.all_level_exits(), player);
  33         self.route_target = selected;
  34     }
  35 
  36     /// The presenter-facing route anchor: bearing/range are derived fresh
  37     /// from the cached target and the live player pose (cheap trig), so the
  38     /// needle tracks head movement between reselections.
  39     pub(super) fn route_anchor(&self) -> Option<RouteAnchor> {
  40         let target = self.route_target?;
  41         let player = [self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]];
  42         Some(RouteAnchor {
  43             target_level: target.target_level,
  44             bearing_deg: relative_bearing_deg(self.player.yaw, player, target.position),
  45             range_m: range_m(player, target.position),
  46         })
  47     }
  48 }
=== noclip.rs ===
   1 //! Backrooms lore made mechanical: holding a walk into solid wall long
   2 //! enough occasionally phases the player through reality. A child module of
   3 //! `engine`; see `presenter.rs` for why that gives it access to `Engine`'s
   4 //! private fields.
   5 
   6 use super::{
   7     Engine, InputFrame, LEVEL_BACKROOMS, LEVEL_GRASSLAND, NOCLIP_CHANCE, NOCLIP_PUSH_SECONDS,
   8 };
   9 
  10 impl Engine {
  11     pub(super) fn rng_next01(&mut self) -> f32 {
  12         self.rng ^= self.rng << 13;
  13         self.rng ^= self.rng >> 7;
  14         self.rng ^= self.rng << 17;
  15         (self.rng >> 40) as f32 / (1u64 << 24) as f32
  16     }
  17 
  18     /// Backrooms lore made mechanical: holding a walk into solid wall long
  19     /// enough occasionally phases the player through reality.
  20     pub(super) fn update_noclip(&mut self, dt: f32, input: &InputFrame, old_pos: [f32; 3]) {
  21         self.noclip_cooldown = (self.noclip_cooldown - dt).max(0.0);
  22 
  23         let i = input.intent;
  24         let pushing = input.locked && (i.forward || i.backward || i.left || i.right);
  25         let dx = self.player.position[0] - old_pos[0];
  26         let dz = self.player.position[2] - old_pos[2];
  27         let pinned = pushing && (dx * dx + dz * dz) < 0.002 * 0.002;
  28 
  29         if !pinned {
  30             self.push_seconds = 0.0;
  31             return;
  32         }
  33         self.push_seconds += dt;
  34         if self.push_seconds < NOCLIP_PUSH_SECONDS || self.noclip_cooldown > 0.0 {
  35             return;
  36         }
  37         self.noclip_cooldown = 1.0;
  38         if self.rng_next01() < NOCLIP_CHANCE {
  39             self.noclip();
  40         }
  41     }
  42 
  43     /// Phase through reality by pushing into walls. From Level 0 the fall is
  44     /// into the grassland; from anywhere else — including Level 1, exactly
  45     /// as the wiki warns — a noclip drops the wanderer back into Level 0.
  46     fn noclip(&mut self) {
  47         let (target, arrival) = if self.level == LEVEL_BACKROOMS {
  48             // Into the grassland you phase in place.
  49             (LEVEL_GRASSLAND, None)
  50         } else {
  51             // The way back drops you at the spawn clearing so you can't
  52             // rematerialize inside a wall.
  53             (LEVEL_BACKROOMS, Some(self.config.spawn))
  54         };
  55         self.switch_level(target, arrival);
  56     }
  57 }

   1 //! Peripheral Shift: "whenever not directly observed, the layout can warp,
   2 //! stretch, or rearrange itself" — the one non-Euclidean mechanic the game
   3 //! has today, and the template for any future level's own version of "the
   4 //! space doesn't stay put." A child module of `engine`; see `presenter.rs`
   5 //! for why that gives it access to `Engine`'s private fields.
   6 //!
   7 //! Structured as a small [`LevelShiftPolicy`] trait with exactly one
   8 //! concrete implementation ([`FabricDriftShift`], level 0's fabric drift).
   9 //! Deliberately not generalized further than that: `RealitySnapshot`'s
  10 //! epoch storage and the fixed 40u `FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL` lattice are still
  11 //! level-0-specific, and there is no second consumer yet to prove a more
  12 //! generic shape against. What this buys today is real: the level-0
  13 //! hardcoding becomes a registration instead of an inline guard, so
  14 //! `Engine::tick` no longer needs to know which levels reshape themselves.
  15 
  16 use vackrooms::domain::entities::anomaly::{
  17     AnomalyKind, FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL, WorldBounds, fabric_drift_cell_of,
  18 };
  19 
  20 use super::{
  21     BLACKOUT_HIDE_DISTANCE, BLACKOUT_SHIFT_PERIOD_S, ChunkKey, Engine, LEVEL_BACKROOMS, chunk_key,
  22 };
  23 
  24 /// A level's "the space doesn't stay put when unobserved" mechanic. A level
  25 /// with no registered policy simply has none — the space stays put, which
  26 /// is the correct default for every level but 0 today.
  27 pub(super) trait LevelShiftPolicy {
  28     /// Which level this policy governs.
  29     fn level(&self) -> u32;
  30     /// Advance the mechanic by one tick. Has full access to `Engine`
  31     /// because every existing implementation (and every plausible future
  32     /// one — a level's own chunk store, player pose, and reality state)
  33     /// needs it; the pluggability this buys is *which* mechanic runs per
  34     /// level, not isolation from engine state.
  35     fn update(&self, engine: &mut Engine, dt: f32);
  36 }
  37 
  38 /// Level 0's fabric drift: the sole concrete `LevelShiftPolicy` today.
  39 pub(super) struct FabricDriftShift;
  40 
  41 impl LevelShiftPolicy for FabricDriftShift {
  42     fn level(&self) -> u32 {
  43         LEVEL_BACKROOMS
  44     }
  45 
  46     fn update(&self, engine: &mut Engine, dt: f32) {
  47         engine.run_fabric_drift_shift(dt);
  48     }
  49 }
  50 
  51 impl Engine {
  52     /// The registered policy for `level`, if any. The only place level ids
  53     /// map to shift mechanics — adding a second level's policy later means
  54     /// adding one arm here, not touching `tick`.
  55     fn shift_policy_for(level: u32) -> Option<&'static dyn LevelShiftPolicy> {
  56         const FABRIC_DRIFT: FabricDriftShift = FabricDriftShift;
  57         if level == FABRIC_DRIFT.level() {
  58             Some(&FABRIC_DRIFT)
  59         } else {
  60             None
  61         }
  62     }
  63 
  64     /// Runs the current level's shift mechanic, if it has one. Replaces
  65     /// what used to be a hardcoded `if self.level != LEVEL_BACKROOMS` guard
  66     /// at the call site — `tick` no longer needs to know which levels
  67     /// reshape themselves, only that some might.
  68     pub(super) fn update_peripheral_shift(&mut self, dt: f32) {
  69         if let Some(policy) = Self::shift_policy_for(self.level) {
  70             policy.update(self, dt);
  71         }
  72     }
  73 
  74     /// Squared distance from a point to a drift cell's world rectangle
  75     /// (0 inside the cell).
  76     fn drift_cell_dist2(cell: (i64, i64), px: f32, pz: f32) -> f32 {
  77         let x0 = cell.0 as f32 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL;
  78         let z0 = cell.1 as f32 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL;
  79         let dx = (x0 - px).max(px - (x0 + FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL)).max(0.0);
  80         let dz = (z0 - pz).max(pz - (z0 + FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL)).max(0.0);
  81         dx * dx + dz * dz
  82     }
  83 
  84     /// A drift cell is hidden from the player once it's farther than any
  85     /// light source could plausibly reveal detail at. Named and pulled out
  86     /// on its own (rather than left as an inline expression) because it's
  87     /// the one piece of tier 2 that's a genuine "can the player perceive
  88     /// this" predicate, not blackout-specific geometry — the natural first
  89     /// thing a second shift mechanic would want to reuse.
  90     fn is_hidden_from_player(cell: (i64, i64), px: f32, pz: f32) -> bool {
  91         Self::drift_cell_dist2(cell, px, pz) > BLACKOUT_HIDE_DISTANCE.powi(2)
  92     }
  93 
  94     /// Every drift cell any resident chunk could touch counts as observed.
  95     /// The far radius adds hysteresis of a couple of cells, so a cell only
  96     /// drifts once the player has genuinely abandoned it.
  97     fn drift_near_radius(&self) -> f32 {
  98         (self.visual_policy.radius as f32 + 1.0) * self.config.chunk_size
  99     }
 100 
 101     fn drift_far_radius(&self) -> f32 {
 102         // A mismanaging wanderer loses the hysteresis: the fabric rearranges
 103         // almost the moment it leaves the streaming footprint.
 104         self.drift_near_radius()
 105             + 2.0 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL * (1.0 - 0.85 * self.survival.mismanagement())
 106     }
 107 
 108     /// Advances one drift cell's reality epoch and stops watching it. The
 109     /// single-cell primitive both tier 1 (a filtered subset of watched
 110     /// cells) and `abandon_all_watched_drift_cells` (every watched cell,
 111     /// unconditionally) are built from.
 112     fn abandon_drift_cell(&mut self, cell: (i64, i64)) {
 113         self.drift_near.remove(&cell);
 114         self.reality = self.reality.with_fabric_drift_advanced(cell.0, cell.1);
 115     }
 116 
 117     /// Leaving the level unobserves everything at once: every tracked drift
 118     /// cell rearranges, so phasing out and back never returns the wanderer
 119     /// to the hallways they left. Called from `switch_level` — previously
 120     /// that reimplemented this drain-and-advance loop inline instead of
 121     /// sharing it with tier 1's version below.
 122     pub(super) fn abandon_all_watched_drift_cells(&mut self) {
 123         let watched: Vec<(i64, i64)> = self.drift_near.drain().collect();
 124         for cell in watched {
 125             self.reality = self.reality.with_fabric_drift_advanced(cell.0, cell.1);
 126         }
 127     }
 128 
 129     /// Tier 1 — abandoned territory. Cells the player walks near are marked;
 130     /// when one falls beyond the far radius every chunk of it has long been
 131     /// evicted, its drift epoch advances, and whatever streams back in later
 132     /// is a lawfully different warren (corridors, assemblies, and anomalies
 133     /// never move — navigation survives; hallway memory does not).
 134     ///
 135     /// Tier 2 — inside a blackout the shift stalks the player in real time:
 136     /// on a slow cadence, cells that lie entirely behind the player's facing,
 137     /// beyond what any light could reveal, and fully inside the blackout's
 138     /// bounds advance immediately and their resident chunks rebuild. The
 139     /// darkness hides the swap; turning around is never a way back.
 140     fn run_fabric_drift_shift(&mut self, dt: f32) {
 141         let (px, pz) = (self.player.position[0], self.player.position[2]);
 142 
 143         // -- tier 1: mark near cells, drift abandoned ones -------------------
 144         let near = self.drift_near_radius();
 145         let min_cx = fabric_drift_cell_of(px - near);
 146         let max_cx = fabric_drift_cell_of(px + near);
 147         let min_cz = fabric_drift_cell_of(pz - near);
 148         let max_cz = fabric_drift_cell_of(pz + near);
 149         for cz in min_cz..=max_cz {
 150             for cx in min_cx..=max_cx {
 151                 if Self::drift_cell_dist2((cx, cz), px, pz) <= near * near {
 152                     self.drift_near.insert((cx, cz));
 153                 }
 154             }
 155         }
 156         let far2 = self.drift_far_radius() * self.drift_far_radius();
 157         let abandoned: Vec<(i64, i64)> = self
 158             .drift_near
 159             .iter()
 160             .copied()
 161             .filter(|&cell| Self::drift_cell_dist2(cell, px, pz) > far2)
 162             .collect();
 163         for cell in abandoned {
 164             self.abandon_drift_cell(cell);
 165         }
 166 
 167         // -- tier 2: the blackout rearranges behind the player ---------------
 168         self.blackout_shift_cooldown = (self.blackout_shift_cooldown - dt).max(0.0);
 169         let blackout_bounds = self
 170             .store
 171             .all_traversal_gates()
 172             .find(|gate| {
 173                 gate.anomaly_kind == AnomalyKind::BlackoutExpanse
 174                     && gate.affected_bounds.contains(px, pz)
 175             })
 176             .map(|gate| gate.affected_bounds);
 177         let Some(bounds) = blackout_bounds else {
 178             self.blackout_shift_debug.0 = false;
 179             return;
 180         };
 181         self.blackout_shift_debug.0 = true;
 182         if self.blackout_shift_cooldown > 0.0 {
 183             return;
 184         }
 185         let forward = self.player.forward();
 186         // The rear shift reaches past the streaming footprint on purpose:
 187         // cells it advances beyond residency simply rebuild on approach,
 188         // exactly like tier-1 drift.
 189         let reach = self.drift_near_radius().max(3.0 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL);
 190         let mut shifted = Vec::new();
 191         for cz in fabric_drift_cell_of(pz - reach)..=fabric_drift_cell_of(pz + reach) {
 192             for cx in fabric_drift_cell_of(px - reach)..=fabric_drift_cell_of(px + reach) {
 193                 let cx_w = (cx as f32 + 0.5) * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL;
 194                 let cz_w = (cz as f32 + 0.5) * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL;
 195                 // Center-based checks on purpose: a 40 u cell near the
 196                 // blackout's edge or the player's flank still shifts. The
 197                 // sliver a check this loose can expose sits in blackout
 198                 // darkness — and a half-glimpsed wall that wasn't there is
 199                 // the intended experience, not a bug.
 200                 let inside = bounds.contains(cx_w, cz_w);
 201                 let behind = (cx_w - px) * forward[0] + (cz_w - pz) * forward[2] < -4.0;
 202                 let hidden = Self::is_hidden_from_player((cx, cz), px, pz);
 203                 if inside && behind && hidden {
 204                     shifted.push((cx, cz));
 205                 }
 206             }
 207         }
 208         self.blackout_shift_debug = (true, shifted.len(), self.blackout_shift_debug.2);
 209         if shifted.is_empty() {
 210             return;
 211         }
 212         self.blackout_shift_debug.2 += shifted.len();
 213         // Mismanagement accelerates the stalking dark: at full strain the
 214         // rear shift fires three times as often.
 215         self.blackout_shift_cooldown =
 216             BLACKOUT_SHIFT_PERIOD_S / (1.0 + 2.0 * self.survival.mismanagement());
 217         for &(cx, cz) in &shifted {
 218             self.reality = self.reality.with_fabric_drift_advanced(cx, cz);
 219         }
 220         // Rebuild the resident chunks of the shifted cells in place. The
 221         // install path's player-overlap check keeps the swap safe, and the
 222         // request carries the advanced reality by construction.
 223         let cell_bounds: Vec<WorldBounds> = shifted
 224             .iter()
 225             .map(|&(cx, cz)| {
 226                 WorldBounds::new(
 227                     cx as f32 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL,
 228                     cz as f32 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL,
 229                     (cx + 1) as f32 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL,
 230                     (cz + 1) as f32 * FABRIC_DRIFT_CELL,
 231                 )
 232             })
 233             .collect();
 234         let cs = self.config.chunk_size;
 235         let targets: Vec<ChunkKey> = self
 236             .store
 237             .iter_ordered()
 238             .filter(|chunk| {
 239                 let rect = WorldBounds::new(
 240                     chunk.origin.0,
 241                     chunk.origin.1,
 242                     chunk.origin.0 + cs,
 243                     chunk.origin.1 + cs,
 244                 );
 245                 cell_bounds.iter().any(|cell| cell.intersects(rect))
 246             })
 247             .map(|chunk| chunk_key(chunk.origin.0, chunk.origin.1))
 248             .collect();
 249         for key in targets {
 250             self.force_rebuild(key);
 251         }
 252     }
 253 }

 287     /// A fake policy for a level that doesn't really have one, proving

peripheral_shift.rs:
- Tier 1: per-frame nested loops over drift cells in radius: (2*near/40)^2 ≈ (2*170/40)^2 ≈ 72 cells — O(C) per frame, small.
- Tier 2 blackout shift (every 0.75s): nested loops over cells within reach: (2*max(170,120)/40)^2 ≈ 72 cells. Then `targets` filter over ALL resident chunks (up to 1089) with `cell_bounds.iter().any(...)` — O(R × S) where R=resident, S=shifted cells — small S. Only on cooldown expiry. Fine.

Now body.rs, navigation.rs, player.rs, survival_inventory.rs — skim for hot paths. Then rendering/camera.rs + rendering/mod.rs. Then lib.rs atomics 1-150 and 460-1000 (browser boot + statics list). Also main.rs thread::spawn (for the concurrency inventory). And check atomics list complete — lines 258-420ish (need to see lines 1-150 and 460-1000 of lib.rs).
   1 //! # wasm_frontend — browser client for the vackrooms voxel engine
   2 //!
   3 //! This crate is the *outer rings* of the engine's Clean Architecture when it
   4 //! runs in a browser. The dependency rule points strictly inward:
   5 //!
   6 //! ```text
   7 //! drivers (portable WebGPU + wasm DOM)  <- outer layer
   8 //!    |
   9 //! adapters (input mapping, SVO atlas, local chunk source)
  10 //!    |
  11 //! application (player physics, streaming policy, frame orchestration, ports)
  12 //!    |
  13 //! vackrooms core (entities + use cases: VoxelGrid, SVO, generation, lighting)
  14 //! ```
  15 //!
  16 //! * `application` and `adapters` are platform-agnostic and unit-tested with
  17 //!   plain `cargo test` on the host.
  18 //! * Portable WebGPU pipeline/configuration modules also compile natively for
  19 //!   headless Vulkan tests; DOM, events, surfaces, and rAF remain wasm-only.
  20 //! * The `#[wasm_bindgen(start)]` entry point below is the composition root:
  21 //!   it wires concrete drivers into the application's ports.
  22 
  23 pub mod adapters;
  24 pub mod application;
  25 pub mod drivers;
  26 pub mod reference;
